title: skills: ship /github-weekly, source roster from Notion, auto-extend Week
body:
## Summary

Three closely-related drift fixes for the team skills:

1. **Add `/github-weekly` as a shared skill.** PR #5 made `/weekly-progress` call `/github-weekly`, but `/github-weekly` was never committed to this repo — it lived only as a personal command on one machine. Anyone other than the original author hits a dangling reference after `./install.sh`.

2. **Source the team roster from Notion.** Replace the hardcoded 9-row roster tables in `/weekly-progress` and `/github-weekly` with a runtime lookup against the [Accelerator Platform Software](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/Accelerator-Platform-Software-31fd132d3cfd80a1af67de154a08451a) Notion page, with GitHub handles resolved by querying the `aps` GitHub team. One source of truth — the page is what changes when the team changes.

3. **Auto-extend the Stories DB `Week` dropdown.** Adds a step to `/weekly-progress` (Step 0.5) and `/flow-create` (Step 1.5) that ensures the current week's option exists in the Stories DB `Week` select, auto-extending 8 weeks ahead via `notion-update-data-source` if not. Fixes the "Week dropdown only goes to W18" symptom Jesse flagged today; the dropdown self-maintains from now on.

## Why

The check-in flow had three accumulating sources of drift:
- A skill referenced from another skill but not shipped (#1)
- Two hand-maintained rosters that diverged any time the team changed (#2)
- A Notion select that needed manual extension every quarter and silently broke things when forgotten (#3)

This PR collapses each into a single canonical source.

## Changes

- `skills/github-weekly/SKILL.md` (new) — frontmatter follows team-skill convention; roster reads from Notion at run time; output is inline by default with optional file save.
- `skills/weekly-progress/SKILL.md` — Step 0.5 ensures current Week exists; Team Roster section replaced with Notion-page reference.
- `skills/flow-create/SKILL.md` — Step 1.5 ensures current Week exists when the user is setting Week.
- `install.sh` — install the new skill.
- `README.md` — document the new skill.
- (Out of band, not in this diff) the Stories DB `Week` select was extended to W26 (Jun 23) to unblock today's W19 work.

## Test plan

- [ ] `./install.sh` reports four skills installed
- [ ] `/github-weekly` standalone produces an inline 7-day report; team roster reflects the Notion page
- [ ] `/weekly-progress` Step 0.5 is a no-op now that W19 exists; deleting and re-running auto-recreates if removed
- [ ] `/weekly-progress --all` runs end-to-end with the new GitHub Activity section
- [ ] `/flow-create` setting Week on a story works without manual dropdown maintenance

title: Add native numerical validation for Qwen3.5 MoE inference
body:
Add independent numerical checks for standalone Qwen3.5 MoE text inference.

## Problem

Running the full model exposed GDN buffers being overwritten before their final use, incorrect shared-gate tensor layout, and SAL scalar precision mismatches. Generated tokens alone did not establish numerical correctness.

## Solution

Preserve live GDN buffers, correct tensor loading and scalar precision, and add an independent reference with strict checkpoint comparisons for each generation step. Add a 256-expert/top-8 tiny case covering prefill and two decode steps, supported by synthetic GDN regressions and reusable validation artifacts. Mark only the three native-oracle tests whose provenance checks require the RTL checkout. The frozen tiny checkpoint digest is registered in `docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md` with its provenance in `docs/QWEN35_MOE_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md`. A review pass then consolidated the tolerance rule, margin constants, row-position derivation and comparison-JSON writes into single owners, gated capture-mode recording consistently, restored the conservative scratch reservation for undeclared GDN geometry, and made the reference refuse an undeclared head layout for grouped heads; frozen reference arithmetic and the suite's embedded checkpoint names were left unchanged.

## Testing

- On this head (rebased onto current main, RTL present): nearest and merged test files 753 passed, 0 failed; contract lane 111 passed; light gate all six lanes green (src 801 passed / 7 skipped, 12321 tests collected); tiny canonical passed (prefill plus two decode steps, tokens and all checkpoint gates); `tools.prime_radiant check` and `asim validation hf-survey reports --check` pass; the tiny fixture regenerated before and after the review fixes is byte-identical except the oracle's provenance hashes of the edited reference sources.
- The first full validation of the review pass caught a regression the light gate cannot see: a leftover function-local import in the MoE expert path raised `UnboundLocalError` whenever checkpoint capture was on (tiny canonical and four MoE external-oracle cases failed). Fixed in this head; those five cases pass again. No arithmetic changed.
- Same runtime arithmetic on the pre-rebase head 3e71b6c4: full gate red only on lanes this branch does not own (Gemma strict logits, a C2C ledger check needing Python 3.12.3, Prime Radiant witnesses needing Verilator); tiny canonical passed; two fresh real 35B runs produced ` Paris.\n` through all 40 layers with 0 mismatches against the frozen 3,574-gate suite, and their exact repeat comparison found 0 differences across 4,174 checkpoints.
- A static guard (`tests/test_import_shadowing_guard.py`) now pins that mechanism: a function-scope use of a module-level imported name must not precede a local import of it. Zero hits across `src/asim`, `tests`, `tools`, `scripts`; against the regressed file it reports both crash sites.
- The full validation restarted on the rebased head got through contract, Prime Radiant check, src and the bulk lane (bulk: only the two known non-owned failures, Gemma and the C2C Python-version check) before it was stopped to fold the guard and merge; the 35B acceptance and repeat therefore stand on the earlier head with identical runtime arithmetic (see above), not on this exact head.

title: Add ACP metadata delivery and separate command submission from simulation stepping
body:
## What / Why

Adds reusable ASIM building blocks for native controllers to submit work and consume completed results:

- Preserve complete routing metadata through CMN/SPM ingress and encode/decode ACP byte records.
- Deliver committed ACP bytes and completion pointers using per-core address mappings, with recoverable bounded fixture queues.
- Separate command submission from simulation stepping; retain SAL/SVL packet ownership until physical output visibility.
- Verify SAL arithmetic, routing, ordering, and overflow/retry behavior.

These interfaces support native MoE simulation. Guest execution and cache coherence remain future integration work.

**Compatibility:** ACP destinations use `acp_rd_addr` and per-core OCM/DRAM bases, independently of `spm_addr`. The legacy common-base constructor and default synchronous submission remain supported.

## Gate evidence (AGENTS.md section 2)

Rebased onto `main` at `b2ab30272`; review-fix verification uses tree `34c3e7b4c784f42430147d8b8def502ff3bf35e0`.
All five connector findings are addressed with 30 new regression cases.

| Verification | Result |
|---|---|
| ASIM milestone, compatibility, and affected runtime tests | 655 passed; zero failures/errors/skips |
| Fresh native build / CTest | 11/11 passed |
| M1 handoff | Passed, including all three negative cases |
| M2 live router | 4/4 cases passed |
| M3 local layer | 10/10 cases passed; all eight positive outputs match all 128 BF16 lanes |
| Affected tests without RTL | 39 passed; zero skips |
| Exact CI lane-topology check without RTL | Passed; 13,582 collected; zero violations |
| Prime Radiant generated fixtures / coverage consistency | 69/69 current; consistency check passed |

**CI fixture follow-up (`b337a69e9`, 2026-09-18):** The admission-only fixture now
explicitly specifies no weight dependency, matching the new validation on `main`.
All assertions remain intact. Affected branch tests: **39/39 passed**; the same
surface plus upstream dependency tests on the PR merged with current `main`
(`9cb597f18`): **58/58 passed**, without RTL and with zero skips.

M1–M3 results above are from the review-fix checkpoint; they were not rerun for
this test-only correction. Broad `--pre-push` / `--fast` gates remain waived by
user instruction; canonical and structural-audit execution were not run.
No anchored artifacts require refresh for this fixture change.

New held-write regressions verify that dependent loads/EXEC are rejected before admission and succeed with the correct values after commit.

Fixed in `085ef4ccc`: the sink now preflights capacity and aperture bounds for the entire CMN step before any DSU state or credits change. Overflow/retry regressions verify stable AWIDs, preserved payloads, exactly-once writes/completions, and credit conservation across DSUs.

Fixed in `085ef4ccc`: CMN ingress copies all declared routing fields and serializes that same record, preserving the ACP target and granule while retaining the existing SPM address/source overrides. Six new regressions check the actual packed fields, physical ACP destinations, completion pointers, and defaults.

Fixed in `085ef4ccc`: whole-step capacity preflight preserves queued B matches and pending state when the sink is full. New regressions verify that draining and retrying publishes each completion exactly once, including duplicate-response and multi-DSU cases.

Fixed in `085ef4ccc`: generic SVL passthroughs retain bridge ownership through SVL retirement, SSA drain, and physical SPM commit. Regressions verify overlap rejection, correct dependent-operation results after retry, and release for K passes that produce no SPM writes.

title: feat(bridge): Add guest ACP delivery and raw execution controls
body:
## What / Why Enable raw bridge clients to receive accelerator metadata and completion pointers, and make configuration/progress reflect actual execution: - Add opt-in v2 ACP write/completion events with aperture, ordering and batch-capacity checks; bind fresh or adopted engines before accepting v2 and preserve default v1 framing. - Apply guest SVL Top-K and supported SAL configuration SRAM writes using the generated register map and a cited scalar circuit encoding. - Report SAL progress on physical SPM commits; drain runnable synchronous work and acknowledge standalone loads waiting for metadata or a READY-sector consumer so the client can submit the releasing work. - Reject incompatible transport/setup and cover adoption, metadata ordering, configuration boundaries, delayed visibility and queue retries; document the functional simulation boundary. **NOTE: Bridge v2 is the updated socket protocol connecting Terminus and ASIM.** The existing bridge forwarded CPU register accesses and accelerator progress signals. This extension adds the missing accelerator-to-CPU metadata path so guest C++ can consume the Top-K scores and expert IDs produced by ASIM. - **Version negotiation:** both endpoints (Terminus and ASIM) explicitly agree to enable ACP delivery. The existing v1 formats and regression vectors remain unchanged. - **Metadata writes (ACP_WRITE):** New message ID 0x22.. ASIM sends a 32-byte metadata write, its destination address and DSU ID. Terminus writes those bytes into guest memory through its modeled memory bus. - **Completion notifications (ACP_COMPLETE):** New message ID 0x23.. ASIM sends the completed metadata pointer and destination DSU/core. Terminus publishes the pointer in the guest-visible FSR completion FIFO only after the data is written. - **Guest consumption:** C++ can inspect and pop completion pointers, then read the corresponding RD/GD metadata from guest memory. - **Ordering and tracking:** completions must match prior writes, and pending state cannot carry across simulation sessions. - **Metadata drain:** ASIM finishes pending metadata processing, writes and memory responses before returning the synchronous activation reply, ensuring the guest can receive the results. - **Protocol validation:** the bridge supports the larger frames and checks versions, lengths, addresses, destinations and event ordering. The version bump applies to the simulator socket protocol; the existing hardware ABI stays unchanged. > [!IMPORTANT] > **The initial PR commit (`754a8c1f0`) completed `--pre-push` and `--fast` with baseline failures that were not introduced by this PR.** > Clean-`main` comparisons at `6b79e8ce3` show an existing stale CPS fixture, a C2C Python-version mismatch, and an existing Gemma numerical mismatch. wade.body: Fixed in [beab0dc4a](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/beab0dc4acb1d97f1e5af1ce5a27906290b6b4bd): fresh and adopted hemispheres now share ACP setup without replacing the existing CMN, memory, or callbacks. Passing regressions cover strict/non-strict v2 handshakes, reset/re-adoption, physical bytes and completion pointers, and refusal of incompatible receivers before acknowledgment.

Fixed in [beab0dc4a](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/beab0dc4acb1d97f1e5af1ce5a27906290b6b4bd): ACP configuration runs on the common engine path, and v2 is acknowledged only after the adopted receiver is configured successfully. Fresh/adopted delivery and mutation-free refusal cases passed, including correct guest addresses and write-before-completion ordering.

Fixed in [beab0dc4a](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/beab0dc4acb1d97f1e5af1ce5a27906290b6b4bd): ACP with the default or explicit legacy transport now fails before socket creation or readiness publication, and the CLI help/documentation explicitly require `ASIM_BRIDGE_PROTOCOL=v1`. Tests passed for unset, empty, and explicit legacy settings, plus ACP argument forwarding.

Fixed in [beab0dc4a](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/beab0dc4acb1d97f1e5af1ce5a27906290b6b4bd): a load waiting for unavailable matching-source metadata stays queued and receives admission success, while ordinary and metadata-ready loads still drain synchronously. Passing regressions cover later metadata, wrong-source metadata, matching metadata already queued, and unchanged submit-only behavior.

Addressed in [beab0dc4a](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/beab0dc4acb1d97f1e5af1ce5a27906290b6b4bd): the accepted word is now a named constant with exact citations to the pinned `external/asimov/design/sls/sal/sw/sal_cmd.c` defaults, scalar configuration, and packing functions. Its value is unchanged and matches that reference; scalar selection and unsupported-word/opmode rejection tests passed.

Fixed in [beab0dc4a](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/beab0dc4acb1d97f1e5af1ce5a27906290b6b4bd): the configuration base, extent, and word stride now come from the generated `SAL_CSR_MEMS` entry named `sal_cfg`. Passing wire-level tests derive addresses from that map and cover first/last words, adjacent invalid addresses, write-only reads, and partial-write rejection.

This limitation already exists on main, and M5’s combined packets do not request metadata waits. We’re deferring support for that combined-packet ordering from this PR; the newly supported standalone metadata-waiting loads remain covered.

Fixed in [543d71901](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/543d7190164467aac057fba141cd7f82c27d6b84): standalone and combined DATA_LOAD+EXEC loads share a no-progress watchdog instead of a total-cycle cap, with terminal state checked at the deadline. Passing regressions cover full-sector metadata-gated loads, committed combined output, and genuine stalls; combined requests needing metadata from a later client request remain explicitly deferred.

Fixed in [543d71901](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/543d7190164467aac057fba141cd7f82c27d6b84): the shared ACP configuration validator runs before socket/readiness side effects and remains enforced for direct BridgeState construction. Boundary and rejection tests verify invalid configurations neither create artifacts nor remove existing paths.

Fixed in [543d71901](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/543d7190164467aac057fba141cd7f82c27d6b84): fresh raw engines use the generated architectural Top-K reset while explicit guest writes and adopted/native settings are preserved. Reset/adoption tests and the M5 guest smoke pass.
we will address this robustness gap in the next iteration

An ACK here means admission, not completion: RTL holds later command sets behind pending loads (`sal_fsm_spm_read.sv:785–790,860`), so draining this request would block the client from sending the releasing EXEC. I reproduced the DATA fill → DATA reload → LATENT/LP first-fill → EXEC sequence with physical SPM reads and exact outputs; both pending loads complete after release, and we’re tracking clarification plus a regression test as nonblocking follow-up.

Addressed [Jesse’s review](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/pull/262#pullrequestreview-5284811505) in [543d71901](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/543d7190164467aac057fba141cd7f82c27d6b84): ACP with legacy strict-v1 readiness files is rejected before socket/readiness creation, preserving the publisher and Terminus consumer contract. Startup refusal tests and real-publisher lifecycle checks pass; normal M5 v2 sessions remain supported.

@positron-jessezhang Fixed in [71133075c](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/commit/71133075c1c3904e7e09c8b00b36c2fba45965f9): standalone raw DATA/LATENT/LP reloads now acknowledge pending admission on a READY sector, preserving its operands until a later EXEC releases it. Added physical LOAD/LOAD/EXEC regressions and arbitration/backpressure/combined-packet checks; 207 focused tests and 188 tests without RTL passed, and the three-token/two-slot C1 demo matched 384/384 BF16 lanes.

title: feat(bridge): Execute programmed SAL circuit words on the guest bridge path
body:
## Summary

Guest MoE runtimes on Terminus C1 program SAL configuration SRAM words (the RTL RMSNorm and sigmoid helper words, plus authored Shift/Exp/Add/raw-mean NORMALIZE words for SAL routing weights). This change lets the raw SPA bridge execute those words on the modeled device path, not only the scalar-multiply word and fixed slots.

- `asim.sal.programmed_circuit`: decode (`SALCircuitConfig.from_bits`), coverage walk over the shared `sal_col.sv` leg tables, element-wise evaluation through `evaluate_column`.
- `evaluate_column`: shared leg tables (RTL default arms), mult_2 offramp, array evaluation, per-config leg resolution; PE detour and LPA offramp raise.
- `cw_dispatch`: programmed `SAL_OP_GEN` (one page) and `SAL_OP_NORM` (sum-tree DATA load in the same bundle, literal epsilon); refusals name the EXEC field.
- `spa_consumer`: EXEC lowered before its DATA load is admitted.
- `cw_fp_sqrt` (Python + `asim_rust`): wrapper NaN semantics, subnormal flush.

### Pre-existing ASIM bugs fixed
- Fixed `SAL_OP_NORM` / `SAL_OP_PE` read DATA sector 0 for sector-1 commands (`sal_fsm.sv:1979`).
- A refused EXEC left its companion DATA sector READY/owned, stalling the next valid EXEC.
- `evaluate_column` default-arm mis-selections / IndexError (list in commit).
- `cw_fp_sqrt` clamped negative/NaN input to 0 instead of the canonical NaN (`chipware_fp_sqrt_wrapper.sv:80-83,108`).
- Fixed NORM/PE silently ignored cmd_dep clamp enables (now refused).
- Stale leg table in `asim sal mux`.

## Anchored artifacts (AGENTS.md section 4)
- `tests/data/sal_known_config_golden.json`: sqrt/rsqrt rows regenerated with
  `./.venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; sys.path[:0]=['tests','.','src']; from tests.test_sal_evaluate_column_encoding import _run_all_pin_configs,_GOLDEN_PATH; _GOLDEN_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(_run_all_pin_configs(), indent=2, sort_keys=True)+'\n')"` (format unchanged; other rows byte-identical).
- `docs/rust_hot_path_inventory.json` (on-touch, hand-maintained): open_debt `sal_programmed_circuit_eval`.
- `src/asim/sim/compute/sal_ops.py` is a pinned source of the release-cadence `tp2-short-parity-probes` publication: regenerate in the release-preparation PR.

## Performance
Scalar `evaluate_column` is 9-12% faster than the parent across `KNOWN_CONFIGS`, because each configuration's legs are now resolved once from the shared leg tables instead of per element. Programmed words are evaluated element-wise over the whole column (numpy) rather than in a Python per-element loop.

## Validation
Tested on the PR head (rebased on `7f42502dc`, no conflicts).
- Nearest tests incl. #181's bridge/Gold modules: 2523 passed, 246 skipped (environment). MoE native integration: 29/29.
- `scripts/pre_merge_gate.sh --pre-push`: all lanes pass. tests-bulk lane: 13300 passed; 2 pre-existing failures (`test_c2c_h2h_timing` ledger, Gemma tanh-gelu audit; fail identically on the parent).
- `--fast` and canonical ran on the same patch before the #181 rebase: remaining failures pre-existing (Gemma tiny-stress oracle) or environment (101 prime-radiant witnesses: Verilator not installed). Canonical (`scripts/run_canonical_rtlsim.py --jobs 4`): 8/8 cases pass with unchanged token IDs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: AGENTS.md: choose the gate by what a change can alter, not by its breadth
body:
## Summary

AGENTS.md section 2 chose between `--fast` and the full gate by the breadth of a change ("large in behavior ... across subsystems"). A change touching the bridge, the attention runtime and V-offset layout read as cross-subsystem and required the full gate, whose wall time is the canonical lane's longest case (the lane already runs its cases concurrently; `--jobs` beyond the case count does not shorten it). A change inside one subsystem that could move a token needed only `--fast`, whose lanes run synthetic weights and never execute the canonical default suite.

This PR makes the gate choice follow what a change can alter:

- **Step 3** — `--fast` is the whole requirement only for a change that cannot alter a produced token or the structural audit's record and does not trigger the full gate; a timing or scheduling change that moves when a value is produced, consumed or retired can alter either; uncertainty means the canonical tier.
- **Step 4, canonical tier** — any change that can alter a token or the audit's record: `--fast` plus the canonical default suite, run to completion on the exact tree pushed; `--case` and `--smoke` are prechecks. One exception to the pre-push rule: a canonical run started on the pushed tree before push may still be running at push, recorded as pending (section 8) and completed, passing, before merge; a failure after push is a section 3 report.
- **Step 4, full gate** — a rebaseline or any change to the executable canonical verification contract. Cross-subsystem breadth alone no longer requires full. "Apply the strongest match" keeps full precedence.

Owner decisions (2026-10-02): adopt the breadth relaxation; adopt the pending-at-push exception for the canonical tier only; do not move any canonical case to nightly.

## Same-PR synchronisation

- `scripts/pre_merge_gate.sh` header: full-mode note rewritten; it now also lists the files that make up the executable canonical verification contract and what full adds over `--fast` + the canonical suite (slow serial, slow Prime Radiant, mandatory llama.cpp crosscheck).
- `scripts/hooks/pre-push` comment: no longer says "before merging a rebaseline/large change"; points at section 2 step 4 and the gate header.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: items 3 and 4 follow the new steps; the Canonical status section carries the per-tier completion rules and the "unmergeable until a rerun passes" consequence.
- `docs/QUICKSTART.md`: the canonical table row and the two paragraphs that described the old "large change" rule now defer to section 2 step 4; the smoke paragraph adds the named-case precheck and says why the suite's elapsed time is roughly its slowest case; the `--jobs 8` literal is removed from the edited example (the runner's default runs every selected case concurrently).

## Intentional decisions

- The sentence "Run independent long canonical jobs in parallel, not serially" is dropped: the runner's default (`--jobs 0`) runs all selected cases concurrently, so for the default suite the instruction is redundant; it was efficiency guidance, not a gate requirement.
- "canonical change" (previously undefined) is written as "any change to the executable canonical verification contract" with the file list in the gate header; a change that alters canonical *results* is the canonical tier, not full. If the old wording was meant to cover result-changing code, this is a third relaxation; recorded here rather than left implicit.
- Measured per-case durations are not recorded in docs (they move with host and pin); the docs say only that elapsed time is bounded by the slowest case.
- AGENTS.md stays under the contract test's 24,576-byte cap (24,545 after this change); the cap is not raised.

## Validation

Tree: this branch at its head. `tests/test_agent_contract.py` + `tools/doc_checks/` + `tests/test_lane_topology.py` + `tests/test_hf_report_artifacts.py` (it pins QUICKSTART/README phrases; the first CI run caught the one this PR had reworded, now restored) + `tests/test_driver_facade_surface.py` + `tests/test_bf19_pai_reference.py`: 328 passed, 55 skipped, 3 deselected — the three `test_rust_gate_selects_reviewed_benchmark_and_propagates_failures` cases fail identically on an unmodified origin/main checkout when run from a worktree without its own `.venv` (the rust lane returns before the stubbed cargo is reached), so they are environmental; they pass on a checkout with a venv. `bash -n` on the two edited shell files. No lane command, selector or pyproject text changes, so the lane-topology contract is unaffected (its tests pass above).

Reviews: the rule text went through four rounds with gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max and three zero-context Claude reviews (plan side); the diff went through three blind rounds with gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max (last round A0 B0 C0) and two blind zero-context Claude reviews (last round A0; its B/C items — hook text, the `--jobs 8` literal, intro wording, the post-push failure consequence — are applied in the final commit).

## Review follow-ups (after the first ready)

- Codex P1 ×3: the gate header's contract list is marked non-exhaustive and gains the `.tron` artifact modules; the canonical tier requires the opt-in cases or suite for each model, execution mode or feature path the change reaches that the default suite does not exercise (if none exists, the PR says so and gets the user's go-ahead); step 4 no longer says full contains the canonical tier — full replaces `--fast` and the default-suite run, supplemental runs still apply. The executable contract is defined by responsibility (case selection, artifact construction, orchestration, acceptance checks) with the file list in the gate header; the pending-at-push exception is scoped to canonical runs and written per required run in the PR template.
- Blind reviews of the follow-up diff: gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max (two rounds, last A0 B0 after one wording fix) and zero-context Claude (A0; its remaining B/C: the dropped "run canonical jobs in parallel" sentence is recorded above as intentional; dependency/toolchain pin bumps are covered by "can alter a produced token" but not named in the examples — follow-up; `README.md:373` and `docs/QUICKSTART.md:806` keep a `--jobs 8` literal — pre-existing, follow-up).

## Owner decision after the first ready (2026-10-05)

title: Add Terminus C1 guest execution for MoE layers
body:
## Summary
This is **Milestone 5** of my MoE simulation plan. It is self-contained, and the responsibilities on the C1 are too large still... need to move the Softmax of Experts into SAL instruction set, etc. But it's a good check-in point.

Run MoE control and GOLD plan construction/execution on the simulated C1, with ASIM performing the accelerator work. Native and guest execution share one controller for routing, selected-expert FFNs, weighted combine, and bounded token scheduling; Python prepares inputs and independently verifies outputs.

- Add guest services for read-only ACP metadata, FSR completion FIFO access, progress checks, deadlines, and safe slot retirement/reuse.
- Add guest/HAL builds and isolated Terminus launching, including environment isolation, session-owned UART capture, and stale-result cleanup.
- Consolidate native/guest tests and document shared entry points, routing policies, and execution contracts.
- Align guest ACP pointers and weight preloads with SAMv2; validate the OS memory profile before launch and disable unrelated model transport.

## Integration scope

Interpreter builds and unit tests can land independently; the GOLD ABI is unchanged. Running the guest demo **requires the companion [OS/HAL #179](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-os/pull/179) and [Terminus #290](https://github.com/positron-ai/terminus/pull/290) changes** plus [ASIM bridge support in positron-ai/asim#262](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/pull/262). This PR does not advance downstream repository pins.

Current execution is functional Terminus/ASIM simulation: one local layer per token, synthetic weights, E=128/256 and K<=8. It does not qualify silicon timing or Phoenix/Palladium execution.

## Validation

- SAMv2 update: 23 focused launcher/qualification checks, 11 MoE CTests, and guest/HAL/mapping-probe builds passed.
- All nine real C1 guest cases passed against the coordinated SAMv2 stack, including partial/duplicate metadata after slot reuse; all 1,152 positive-case BF16 lanes matched exactly.
- Prior qualification also covered 24 CTests and 16 native ASIM cases. Broader ASIM gate results and reproduced baseline failures remain documented in the linked ASIM PR.

title: feat(moe_M7): Run a full OLMoE-1B-7B decoder layer on Terminus C1
body:
## Summary
One full OLMoE-1B-7B decoder layer, an attention prefill followed by the MoE block, with real BF16 weights, executed on the simulated Terminus C1 guest (FVP + ASIM). This builds on M6 (#9), which ran only the MoE block with HF-captured h.

- **Attention prefill in GOLD** (`layer_attention.py`):
  - q/k/v/o projections, RMSNorm and QK-norm;
  - RoPE via SAL_OP_PE, with a one-time theta-LUT load;
  - K/V copied into a KV window;
  - one SUBMIT_ATTN over 5 causal contexts;
  - o_proj and the residual, with h written straight into the MoE input.
- **V WMem offset** placed after the whole hopper-padded K region. ASIM's `attention_v_wmem_offset_chunks()` overlaps V onto K beyond 4 OLMoE tokens; that's recorded as an ASIM-side finding.
- **Builder/executor split** (`gold_builder`, `gold_executor`): templates plus binding slots, with no backend access in the builder. The M6 plan traces are pinned byte-identical.
- **1 GiB weight window** (SMS+0x10000000..+0x50000000), with ACP metadata at +0x50000000. All 64 experts are resident, so the M6 residency limit is gone.
- **TerminusSession**: PIO KV copy with readback, PE-LUT load, SVL reset. `validate_attention` requires every K/V copy to finish before attention and to land in disjoint places inside the window.
- **Host checks**:
  - HF eager capture and an attention oracle, with gates of 2^-6 on K/V and 2^-5 on the attention and layer output.
  - The HF output gate is keyed to the BF16-run selection (@tzhou-positron's #9 comment).
  - Staged weight images must match their plan spans and must not overlap.
- **C1 console**: progress lines and a model config header.

## Validation
- **C1 ("The capital of France is", 5 tokens):** layers 0, 1, 7, 12 and 15 pass; the final tree was re-run at layers 0 and 15.
  - K ≤ 3.4e-3, V ≤ 3.4e-3, h ≤ 4.4e-3, layer output vs HF ≤ 7.1e-3 (gate 2^-5).
  - Routing matches HF on every token.
  - With `--dump-rows`, 480 attention SAL rows are bit-exact.
- **Native:** all 16 layers pass; integration 32/32. A 12-token prompt (the `MAX_TOKENS` cap) passes at layer 0 with every attention stage checked.
- **CTest:** 42/42 (two tests timed out under a load average of about 110 and passed when rerun serially).

## Notes
- The paired positron-ai/asimov-os#196 moves the `moe-v1` profile and HAL to the 1 GiB window and adds `/dev/asimov-kv`. Its MoE pin bump follows this merge.
- Open for M8:
  - The 8-bit V offset limits one attention call to 12 OLMoE tokens.
  - KV rewrites after a read need an ASIM bridge payload-cache invalidation.
  - The SVL reset needs `ASIM_AP_DRIVEN_INFERENCE`.

title: busybox: enable taskset for core pinning
body:
Enables the busybox `taskset` applet in the Asimov rootfs.

**Problem:** The rootfs shipped without `taskset`, so there was no way to pin a process to a specific CPU core.

**Solution:** Turn on `CONFIG_TASKSET` in the board busybox config, plus `FEATURE_TASKSET_FANCY` + `FEATURE_TASKSET_CPULIST` so the `-c` cpu-list form works (`taskset -c 3 ./app`). `-c` depends on FANCY in busybox kconfig, so all three are needed; this matches busybox upstream defaults.

**Testing:** Built busybox from this config and ran it natively — applet present in `--list`, `--help` shows the `-c LIST` form, `/usr/bin/taskset` lands in busybox.links, and `taskset -c 0 … -c -p` pins to core 0 and reads the affinity list back.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Config-only change that adds a standard BusyBox utility; no auth, data, or runtime logic is modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> The Asimov rootfs **busybox** build config now ships the **`taskset`** applet so processes can be pinned to specific CPU cores on the device.
> 
> **`CONFIG_TASKSET`**, **`CONFIG_FEATURE_TASKSET_FANCY`**, and **`CONFIG_FEATURE_TASKSET_CPULIST`** are turned on in `br2-external/board/asimov/busybox.config`, enabling the **`-c` cpu-list** form (e.g. `taskset -c 3 ./app`). FANCY is required for `-c` in BusyBox kconfig; this matches typical upstream defaults.
> 
> No other files change—**`asimov_defconfig`** already points at this busybox config, so the next image build picks up **`/usr/bin/taskset`** via the usual busybox symlinks.

title: boot-fvp: never pre-arm telnet in headless runs; tell the truth about the console
body:
An armed TelnetTerminal with no reading client back-pressures its UART after 16 KiB and the guest busy-spins on `UARTFR.TXFF` — a boot that "hangs" with the UART log frozen at exactly 16383 bytes, last line truncated mid-word. Headless runs with `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1` (the combo DEVELOPMENT.md itself recommended for a live AP console) hit this a few seconds after the script exits at the boot marker; in bridge mode (userspace marker, past 16 KiB) such runs always timed out at 124 with the FVP left wedged. This is the "headless boot hang" from the Terminus+Asim thread.

The fix rides on a component fact: the telnet listener is bound regardless of `start_telnet`, so pre-arming a terminal in a headless run buys nothing — the console stays attachable either way — while costing the wedge.

## Changes

- **headless launches always pass `start_telnet=0` to the model** (`MODEL_TELNET`); `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1 --headless` can no longer wedge a boot
- **`bp.terminal_0` is never pre-armed** (interactive included): the script only ever attaches a client to `ap_terminal`, and the BP UART carries no console output — an armed, undrained terminal there was the same trap waiting
- interactive mode unchanged in behavior: `ap_terminal` keeps `=1` and the script attaches its own client immediately
- the headless success message replaces the misleading "Telnet disabled. Re-run with ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1" (the port is open regardless) with the real contract: console log path, attach-anytime `telnet localhost <port>`, and the keep-reading caveat
- the timeout path hints at the one remaining stall cause — a client that attached earlier and disconnected/stopped draining — with the resolved port to reattach
- headless startup banner lists AP/BP/SCP UART logs explicitly (AP is the boot-marker + console log; it used to print only the output-less BP log). In passing, same class: the timeout `Check: tail -f` now points at the AP UART log, and the usage comment names `fvp-ap-uart-5.log`
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` knob row rewritten to match

## Verification (farm, this branch)

- trigger scenario A/B: `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1 --headless` wedged at exactly 16383 bytes on the old script every time; with this fix it boots through to userspace (43K+ uart log)
- success path: boot to marker in 10.2s, new banner + Console/Attach messages print with the resolved port
- recovery claim: a deliberately wedged run was drained by attaching a reading client — log resumed 16383 → 43312 bytes, boot completed (what the hints promise)
- baseline: 45/45 headless boots (plain / BridgeFwd / BridgeFwd+asim) on the telnet-off path

## Remaining / out of scope

The attach-then-abandon stall is a one-way flow-control latch inside the ARM-binary component — nothing disables it in FM 11.30; the only safe states are "no client ever" or "a client that keeps reading". Mechanism write-up: terminus `model/DESIGN_LOG.md` § "TelnetTerminal: undrained console back-pressure"; launch-path hardening in the other repos: terminus#170, asimov-scp-firmware#95, asimov-tfa#39.

> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes headless FVP boots that could **hang after ~16 KiB of console output** when `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1` pre-armed a telnet terminal with no draining client (TelnetTerminal UART back-pressure).

## Summary

Add OS support for executing a local MoE layer on simulated C1 through Terminus and ASIM. The guest runs the shared interpreter engine: SAL computes input RMSNorm and routing weights, C1 selects experts and orchestrates GOLD work.

- Add opt-in `asimov-moe-local` packaging, pinning interpreter main `f8fd5a2` (merged [interpreter #7](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-interpreter/pull/7)); ordinary images retain their existing interpreter pin.

This is the OS half of positron-ai/terminus#285. Builds on the released `fvp-v0.34.0`, `scp-v0.33.0` and `tfa-v0.23.0` pins already on main (Terminus MoE support from [Terminus #290](https://github.com/positron-ai/terminus/pull/290)). wade.body:
Thanks for the review. Responses by item:

1. The fixed size is intentional: `moe-v1` is a static simulation profile, and synthetic runs sharing the reservation is fine. Your advisory is right, and the next milestone (M7, one full decoder layer) makes exactly that map change: weights become 1 GiB at SMS+0x10000000..+0x50000000, ACP metadata moves to +0x50000000, and all 64 experts are resident.
2. Agreed. A truncated image would currently be caught only indirectly, by the output gates. The M7 PR adds a host-side check of each matrix's staged length against the plan before the session opens.
3. This is intended: `--dump-rows` controls UART output only. The interpreter always fills `TokenResult.normalized`/`moe_out`, which is 32 small SPM reads per token against roughly 20 s of MoE work.
4. Confirmed. In a `MOE_LOCAL=y` image the whole interpreter package, including what the normal runtime links, moves to the MoE pin, and the Buildroot build of that image passes. That image is simulation-only, and the README requires the derived image to disable `S60asimov-runtime`, so the normal runtime is built but not exercised there.
5. The consumers of the Terminus MoE mirrors are:
   - `firmware/include/terminus_address_map.h` `TERMINUS_FVP_MOE_*`, which no code reads;
   - `host-driver/src/memory_map.py` `MOE_*`, read only by `host-driver/tests/test_memory_map_profiles.py`, a constant-consistency test;
   - the `Terminus_AsimBridge.lisa` default `acp_base`, which `boot-fvp.sh` always overrides.

   None of them bounds an allocation, mapping or preload. The LISA default and both mirrors will be updated in a separate Terminus change, which is tracked.
6. Agreed. The M7 PR adds a README note that the guest runner and the host fixture generator/checker upgrade together, and that existing synthetic manifests must be regenerated.

CI: the compiled-DTB test does run in CI. `validate` installs `device-tree-compiler` (which provides `fdtget`) and runs `test_moe_fvp_memory_profile.py`, and it passes here. You're right that CI never compiles the MoE adapter against the MoE pin; the M7 PR adds a host-compile step for `asimov-moe-local`.

Pin: #9 was merge-committed, so `58a7ab70faa33d8a87adf812fb6684133a6b884a` is on interpreter `main` and its tree is identical to the merge commit. The pin stays as it is.

title: model: one C1-SME2 (CME) per cluster (NUM_CMES=1), matching the RTL pin
body:
Story: [STORY-364 — Add SME2/VPU power domain support (C1-DSU)](https://www.notion.so/342d132d3cfd812bb78edd98d15249c7)

## What

The pinned RTL (`941a309cb`) builds one C1-SME2 unit (CME, Arm codename griffin) into every C1-DSU cluster — `C1_DSU_DynamIQ_Cluster_1.yaml` `NUM_CME: 1`, `griffin0_core u_cme_0` instantiated in the cluster wrapper, and the Nevis ID registers advertise SME2 unconditionally (`ID_AA64PFR1_EL1.SME=0b0010`, `ID_AA64SMFR0_EL1.SMEver=SME2`). The FVP's `NUM_CMES=0` default was therefore a silicon divergence: no SME on the model where silicon has it.

- Set `NUM_CMES=1` and the RTL-matched `DSU.cme.CMECFR` (ECC=1 from `CORE_CACHE_PROTECTION: TRUE`, CHI=0 from `NUM_COMPLEX_CHI: 1`) via `".default"` assignments on all five cluster instantiations. The per-cluster parameters stay live and init-time overridable (`-C cluster0.NUM_CMES=0` gives a CME-less A/B run).
- Keep `DSU.cme.power_on_by_default=true`: the Fast Models CME PPU registers are accepted but inert, so auto power-on stands in for the SCP's real CME-PPU dynamic-mode programming.
- Document the model limitations as **DD-12** (inert CME PPU at utility-bus `+0x280000`, unmodeled CME PPU IRQ/RAS/arbitration, partial CMECFR fidelity) and the decision as design-log **D-30**.

## FM 11.30 pitfall (why `".default"` and not the `NUM_CORES` binding pattern)

Delivering `NUM_CMES` through a top-level `PARAMETER` value binding kills every simulation at elaboration with `FATAL ERROR: An SMCU is implemented but FEAT_SME is not configured` — the binding fixes the sub-parameter out of the CADI store and the core model's internal FEAT_SME configuration never sees it. The same value applied as `-C cluster0.NUM_CMES=1`, or via `".default"` assignments (the semihosting-parameter idiom), works. Bisected against pristine main and the pinned fvp-v0.18.0; CMECFR content/escaping was ruled out. Recorded in D-30.

## Verified

- `make build` clean; `tests/run-all` **6/6** on the CME-enabled model; `cluster0..4.NUM_CMES=1` + CMECFR live in `--list-params`.
- Full asimov-os Linux boot on this model (with an SME-enabled BL31, asimov-tfa#33): userspace reached; SVE VL 128-bit, SME streaming VL 512-bit; no `sveaes/svepmull` (crypto ext fused off in RTL). `/proc/cpuinfo` from the booted system (both cores identical):

  ```
  processor       : 0
  BogoMIPS        : 2000.00
  Features        : fp asimd evtstrm crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop asimddp sve asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb dcpodp sve2 svebitperm flagm2 frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh bti ecv afp sme smei8i32 smef16f32 smeb16f32 smef32f32 wfxt rprfm sme2 smei16i32 smebi32i32 mops hbc lrcpc3
  CPU implementer : 0x41
  CPU architecture: 8
  CPU variant     : 0x0
  CPU part        : 0xd8a
  CPU revision    : 0
  ```
- SCP firmware pytest suite: 42 passed / 16 skipped against this model.

## Consumer ordering

An SME-advertising model is only bootable behind a BL31 built with `ENABLE_SME_FOR_NS=2` (positron-ai/asimov-tfa#33): Linux writes `SMCR_EL2` at EL2 init whenever `ID_AA64PFR1_EL1.SME != 0`, and the current tfa-v0.6.0 BL31 dies silently right after its banner on this model (verified). Downstream pin bumps should take the SME-enabled asimov-tfa release before or together with the terminus release carrying this change.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01UqQuy9BCy8ER19zmCu87JP

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Advertises SME2 on all AP cores and tightens boot ordering with TF-A; CME power sequencing still cannot be validated on the FVP (DD-13), so silicon-only regressions remain possible.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns the FVP with pinned RTL by giving all five `ARMC1NanoCT` clusters **one C1-SME2 (CME)** each: `NUM_CMES=1` and RTL-matched `DSU.cme.CMECFR` (ECC=1, CHI=0), applied via `".default"` so Fast Models still configures FEAT_SME and `-C clusterN.NUM_CMES=0` remains possible.
> 
> **DD-13** and design-log **D-30** document the decision, the FM 11.30 pitfall (top-level `PARAMETER` binding breaks SME elaboration), and remaining model gaps (inert CME PPU, unwired RAS IRQs, no core arbitration).
> 
> Downstream stacks need an SME-enabled BL31 (`ENABLE_SME_FOR_NS`) before or with this model release; otherwise Linux’s `SMCR_EL2` init traps at EL3.

title: feat(bridge): Add ACP metadata delivery and FSR completion FIFOs
body:
## Summary

Enable C1 guest software to consume accelerator metadata from ASIM. Negotiated bridge v2 writes ACP metadata into guest memory before publishing completion pointers through the modeled FSR FIFOs.

- Add per-core COUNT, STATUS, HEAD, and POP registers using pinned RTL definitions; preserve existing v1 sessions.
- Forward the full SAL aperture for configuration SRAM and theta-LUT writes.
- Define exclusive legacy/MoE memory profiles and reject incompatible legacy preloads.
- Report ACP delivery failures through both receive paths; provide a separate qualification model for missing/duplicate completions.

## SAMv2 integration

Rebased onto main `d51fef0`. Generated SAM placement remains authoritative; ACP writes use the firmware-armed SMS bridge and share C1 backing memory. The bounded MoE profile derives weights and metadata addresses from SAM exports.

The coordinated SAMv2 OS/interpreter migration is verified in [OS #179](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-os/pull/179) and [interpreter #6](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-interpreter/pull/6). This PR does not change those repositories or the upstream ASIM/RTL pins.

## Validation

- 134 focused SAM, routing, profile and preload checks passed.
- ACP transport/FIFO and fault checks, 60 receive-path scenarios, 189 v1 codec checks, and pinned FSR/C2C regeneration passed.
- Normal and qualification model builds passed; all 11 live v1 sessions passed with Terminus's declared ASIM pin.
- Real C1 SAMv2 smoke: 38 assertions passed, covering high-address RD/GD visibility, FSR pointers and slot reuse with a synthetic v2 peer. Coordinated Linux/M5 validation now passes all nine guest cases, including slot-reuse faults; all 1,152 positive-case BF16 lanes match exactly.

The initial v1 run used the separate ASIM feature checkout and failed two SAL/SVL `build_version` reset expectations; those pass with Terminus's declared ASIM pin. This was dependency-version skew, not a Terminus forwarding failure.

### Mutation review

The scoped instrument completed: 168 mutations, 148 caught and 20 survivors matching the existing diagnostic-wording/equivalent-output registry; no timeouts or untested mutants. The nightly baseline predates SAMv2 main, so the dashboard may label these survivors unclassified; every survivor was manually checked against its registered disposition.

Related: [ASIM #262](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/pull/262) and [interpreter #6](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-interpreter/pull/6).

Just for my own clarity: the way I understood our conversation on this, the goal is to (e.g.) be able to DMA-xfer a large block of data which may span _many_ descriptors, but only rely on completion/notification of the _last_ descriptor in the list.

If we look at how `xfer_k_entry_blocking()` and `xfer_v_entry_blocking()` work today, that's exactly the model they're following. They only wait on the last descriptor to complete.

I think the main difference is today, `xfer_k_entry_blocking()` and `xfer_v_entry_blocking()` assume at most **one wrap** between enqueue and completion time. But when we start sending much larger transfers, we may wrap **multiple** times. So the focus here is really about the _accuracy_ of 'done', not so much about _performance_ of that decision, right?

author: mcherba

title: Add observer hooks for save_k/save_v in model::state
body:
In preparation for hw-kv-token-tree changes, which will intercept the calls to `save_v` and `save_k` independently, I'm introducing two Observer-pattern hook points: `on_save_k` and `on_save_v`. The parameters being used for calling this hook point will be unchanged, and will be identical to those currently taken by `save_k_to_hardware` and `save_v_to_hardware`.

Registering callbacks must be done before any prompting or generation with a model, to avoid concurrency issues. Here, the registration happens in the model::state constructor, which is guaranteed to be completed before a scheduler can use the model. 

There is one behavioral change. Page write is reordered before observer notification. With this change, the planned GOF readiness observer can find page data already written when it fires. This will not cause any additional latency for the code on the hwattention_sync branch, because both the DMA block and page write calls are blocking. Reversing the order won't affect the total per-token timing.

Implementing these hook points in this way will avoid (as much as possible) merge conflicts between `hamon-hktt-dma` (where hw-kv-token-tree DMA changes are being developed) and `hwattention_sync`. 

Additionally, `make format` identified a number of minor formatting fixes in device.hpp and t_hwattention.cpp 


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the KV-save call path and ordering around page writes vs DMA notification, which can affect correctness/timing for hardware attention and any future observers; concurrency expectations depend on observers being registered before inference starts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **observer-style hook points** in `model::state` (`on_save_k` and `on_save_v`) to allow multiple callbacks to be invoked when KV data is saved, while registering the existing `tron::hardware::save_k_to_hardware` / `save_v_to_hardware` as the default observers.
> 
> Updates `save_k`/`save_v` to **write KV data into the page first**, then collect per-head pointers and notify all registered observers instead of calling the hardware save functions directly. Also includes minor `self_attention.hpp` formatting/comment tweaks (debug macro comment style and line wrapping) with no functional change.

author: mcherba

title: fix wqentry->result_size calculation
body:
`fill_attn_job_template()` was treating `wqentry->result_size` as a count of bytes rather than count of scalars. Based on use in the code, it seems clear that field is intended to be a count of bf16 **elements**, not bytes:

1. `launch_work_req` does a memset using `work_req->result_size * sizeof(bf16)` as the size if PREFILL_WITH_NANS is enabled
2. in `prepare_cmd_words' pad_bytes is multiplying by POS_DATA_SIZE to get bytes: `pad_bytes = res_bytes_per_act - (workreq->result_size * POS_DATA_SIZE);`
3. it seems wqentry->result_size is intended to match 'hw_results_size', which is a scalar and is calculated in self_attention.hpp as `static constexpr size_t hw_result_size = n_heads * (head_size + 32);` (no multiply by sizeof(bf16)
4. `hardware_job::stream_results()` treats that 'result_size' as an element count when calculating blocks
5. inside of `fill_hardware_matmul_job_template()` for matmul operations, that field is assigned directly from the 'result_size' passed in: `work_req->result_size = result_size;` (no sizeof(bf16) multiplcation)... and that 'result_size' comes from the models which always calculate as "n_heads * head_size"
6. the documentation for this field in device.hpp is pretty clear that it intends a scalar count ('fpga columns')

The main challenge I had was trying to validate this change in a definitive way... runtron runs didn't seem to produce any differing behavior before/after the change. I did run t_hwdriver, t_hwattention, t_attention, t_compute_attention_unit and t_matmul after the change and they all pass.

title: GOF/shard DMA implementation with TRON_SHARD_TEST=1
body:
Introduces a new path for writing K/V data into FPGA HBM using group-of-four (GOF) blocks. Tokens are accumulated into 4-token `gof_buffers`, promoted to immutable `completed_gofs` on completion (zero-copy swap), then DMA'd to HBM. The new path is gated by `TRON_SHARD_TEST` env var — when unset, the existing `save_k/v_to_hardware` path is used.



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> High risk because it adds a new hardware KV DMA write path (including completion polling and blocking gates) and extends token-tree edge split/coalesce logic to preserve new GOF/shard state, which could impact correctness and concurrency in scheduling and HW attention dispatch.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new *experimental* GOF/shard-based KV-to-HBM transfer pipeline gated by `TRON_SHARD_TEST`, accumulating K/V into 4-token `gof_buffer`s, promoting them to immutable `completed_gof`s (zero-copy swap), and DMAing them to device HBM with optional partial-token flushes before GOF completion.
> 
> Introduces `device_dma_tracker` to track per-device in-flight DMA and expose `poll_completions()` plus `await_layer()`; wires this into the scheduler/model loop via new observer hooks (`on_forward_poll`, `on_await_dma`, `on_flush_partial`) and extends `save_k`/`save_v` observers to receive a `node_base*` hint.
> 
> Extends the token-tree (`node_base` + `parent_edge`) to store shards, completed GOFs, embryonic GOFs, and per-session `handle_id`, and updates edge split/coalesce paths to correctly move/merge this new state; adds an FPGA test (`t_gof_dma`) and build plumbing for the new sources.
>

author: Wado-posi

title: Enable pos_shutdown in test listener with DMA cleanup
body:
## Why this change exists

`pos_shutdown()` was commented out in test listeners across the codebase with the note: *"Crashes and burns due to unfreed allocations."* This caused:

1. **Every test binary leaked hugepages and DMA allocations** (tracked in #1733)
2. **Intermittent segfaults in `t_dma`** during process exit (#1535, #2400) — all 3 test cases pass, then the process segfaults during teardown because the kernel tears down VFIO BAR mappings while static destructors still reference them

The root cause: `PosDevice::init()` allocates DMA buffers and queues, but nothing freed them. `pos_shutdown()` was disabled because calling it triggered heap asserts on the outstanding allocations.

## What changed

### DMA cleanup infrastructure
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `PosDevice::destroy()` | Matching free for `init()`. Without it, heap assert fires on shutdown. |
| `hwkv_rings` destructor | Frees 128 cache block DMA allocations. |
| `delete device` + `devices.clear()` in `pos_shutdown` | Without this, device objects leak and restart appends duplicates. |
| Zero-init pointer members in `PosDevice` | `destroy()` null-checks before freeing; uninitialized pointers cause garbage `dma_deallocate`. |
| `pos_heap_active_allocations()` | DMA allocation counter (real heap + fake-mode). Enables leak detection in test listeners. |

### t_dma segfault fix (#1535, #2400)
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| Enable `pos_shutdown()` in `TestDmaListener` | Without it, process exit races VFIO BAR teardown against static destructors → segfault. |
| Release DmaQueues in transfer test | Test acquired TX/RX queues per device but never called `release()`. |
| Baseline allocation tracking | Record `pos_heap_active_allocations()` after `pos_startup()`, warn only if tests leak above that baseline. The 288 device-init allocations (64 device.cpp + 64 consumed_head + 32 ring buffers + 128 hwkv_rings) are expected. |

### Restart lifecycle hardening
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `pos_startup()` idempotency guard | Prevents duplicate device scan if called twice without shutdown. |
| `vfio_groups = nullptr` after delete | Prevents double-free on second shutdown. |
| `get_group_fd` EBUSY retry | IOMMU teardown is async; rapid restart cycles hit EBUSY on group reopen. |

### Test + review feedback
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `t_pos_restart` (3 FPGA cases) | Restart produces same device count, idempotency, double-shutdown. |
| `t_pos_lifecycle_fake` (6 cases) | Shutdown with outstanding allocs, allocation tracking, reinit. |
| `INFO()` diagnostic in lifecycle test | Per mcherba review — surfaces allocation count on failure. |

## What this does NOT change

Production behavior is unaffected. `pos_shutdown()` was already called at process exit in Rinzler. The only behavioral change is in test infrastructure — listeners now clean up instead of leaking.

### Superseded by main (resolved during merge)
- Inline group init in `vfio_device_init` → main serialized into `vfio_init_groups()` (better race fix)
- `host_initialized` double-call guard → landed independently on main

## Test results

- `make test-host`: 53/53 passed (cloud-atlas-873f)
- `t_dma`: 5/5 clean runs on 8 FPGAs, zero segfaults, zero leak warnings, clean `pos_shutdown()`
- `make format && make lint`: clean

## Test plan

- [x] `make build-test && make test-host` — 53/53 pass
- [x] `t_dma` — 5 consecutive runs, clean shutdown, no segfault
- [ ] `t_pos_restart` (FPGA CI) — restart lifecycle regression tests
- [ ] `t_pos_lifecycle` (FPGA CI) — existing lifecycle tests
- [ ] Full CI matrix (AMD + Intel runners)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches shutdown paths for FPGA/VFIO + DMA heap lifecycles; bugs here can cause use-after-free, leaks, or restart flakiness, but changes are narrowly scoped to cleanup and tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Ensures `pos_shutdown()` actually frees **DMA-backed** resources instead of leaking hugepages/VFIO state, enabling safe teardown in tests and repeated `pos_startup()` cycles.
> 
> Adds `PosDevice::destroy()` and defensive member initialization to release DMA queues/buffers and disable mailbox/tracer write targets before BAR/IOMMU teardown; also gives `hwkv_rings` a destructor to free its ring allocations. Introduces `pos_heap_available()`/`pos_heap_active_allocations()` (real + fake) and improves heap shutdown diagnostics.
> 
> Hardens restart behavior by making `pos_startup()` idempotent, fully deleting/clearing device/global state in `pos_shutdown()`, nulling `vfio_groups` after free, and retrying VFIO group open on `EBUSY`. Updates test listeners to warn on DMA leaks, re-enables shutdown in `t_dma` (and releases per-test queues), and adds new lifecycle/restart regression tests (`t_pos_restart`, expanded `t_pos_lifecycle_fake`).
>

<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: TSX-based mwait
body:
Implement mwaitx using TSX/RTM with tpause.

mwaitx is triggered by touches to the trigger's cache line.

RTM transactions cause the transaction to abort when the trigger's cache line is touched.  The transaction entails a tpause in a rdtsc() loop.  The processor resumes as if the tpause didn't happen.  Meaning immediate wake up.   This is effectively just how mwaitx works. Clever!   (not my idea).

> **Updates join/plan behavior for HW-forwarding vs validation**: when `FWD_HW_RESULTS` is enabled, SW planning excludes pages handled by hardware and joins forward HW results into `vo_from_attn`; otherwise SW produces outputs and HW results are unpacked and compared post-join.   uninitialized content) into the shard list. The HW then loads garbage from that second shard.

```
  The loop condition should probably be < tok_ix rather than <= (tok_ix / shard_tokens) * shard_tokens.                                                     
  
  ---                                                                                                                                                       
```

hard to truly analyze visually... perhaps a quick diag test would be worth it to prove/disprove this?
is there ever an expected scenario where `nshards` != `shards.size()`? If not it seems like `nshards` is redundant since you can always use shards.size()

wade.body: cleaning up some of the "--max-layer 1" hack I put in place a long time ago. I'm still explicitly setting `is_eagle` to 'false' below, because Mark and Alexey owe us a 'better way' of doing this, and it will come from main branch when available. Until then, this allows us to continue using `--max-layers 1` arg in our branch if so desired.

I know this is a 'new module' just to evaluate whether we should use SW or HW attention forwarding. So I asked Claude to argue for/against this, cuz I figured it would raise question... it described it much better than I would have IMO :-):
```
  The argument for the static-local inline function approach (vs. the two alternatives your team will likely suggest):
                                                                                                                                                            
  vs. global variable (extern bool g_fwd_hw_attn + definition in a .cpp):
  - No .cpp needed, no ODR hazard across shared libraries                                                                                                   
  - No explicit init() call that could be forgotten, called twice, or called after the first use                                                            
  - Thread-safe init by C++11 spec — no std::once_flag, no std::atomic                                                                                      
  - Same observable result: read exactly once, same value everywhere                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                            
  vs. a field on model_config or self_attention::state:
  - No plumbing — stream_generate.hpp has no access to model state at all in the LOG_TOKEN_SELECTION path; a struct field would require special-casing that 
  path regardless                                                                                                                                           
  - The value is process-wide and immutable after init; embedding it in a per-model struct implies it could vary per instance, which would be misleading    
  - Every new call site that needs the flag (e.g., a future module) just calls the function — no constructor threading required                             
                                                                                                                                                            
  The "single location" criterion is strictly satisfied: getenv("DISABLE_HW_ATTN") and the interpretation logic appear in exactly one function body. Grep   
  for DISABLE_HW_ATTN → one hit.                                                                                                                            
```

of course, contrary opinions/feedback welcome
I thought capturing the 'max layers' in a member variable `num_hidden_layers` may be useful to leave, but I'll get rid of it. CB is right, it's not being used for anything anyway

author: mcherba

title: fix t_matmul divide-by-zero?
body:
See the comments in the code-delta... when I asked Claude to explain why this works fine on main branch, but breaks here... this was its explanation:
```
● On main: wqentry has no default member initializers at all — it's a plain aggregate. new wqentry does default-initialization, which
  for POD-like types leaves members indeterminate. So bytes_per_res_block is whatever junk was in the heap.                             
                                                                                                                                        
  On this branch: you added shards{} and nshards = 0 (default member initializers). In C++, once a struct has any default member        
  initializer, new wqentry triggers value-initialization of the whole object, which zero-initializes all members without explicit       
  initializers — including bytes_per_res_block = 0.                                                                                     
                                                        
  So on main, bytes_per_res_block is uninitialized heap garbage, which is almost never exactly 0, so the divide "works" (by accident).  
  On this branch, it's reliably 0, so it crashes every time. The bug has always existed — it was just latent on main.
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the call ordering for streamed matmul results so `prepare_matmul` must run before `hardware_job::stream_results()`, affecting launch/streaming sequencing. Low code churn, but touches hardware job preparation/launch flow and could impact streaming behavior if callers rely on the old (incorrect) order.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a crash in streamed matmul result handling by **making `prepare_matmul` a required prerequisite** for `hardware_job::stream_results()` (which uses `bytes_per_res_block` and could previously divide by zero).
> 
> Adds explicit documentation (`Note [Stream Results Prepare Dependency]`) and updates the emulation `device_matmul` streaming path to call `prepare_matmul` before setting up streams, then launch normally.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 0692b01719ee03c603e55246d7b5909ef421b556. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

wade.body:
> The explanation (and code comment) would be better if it mentioned where the divide by zero occurs, namely `hardware_job::stream_results`. However, it would probably be even better to fix the problem by computing `work_req->bytes_per_block` (and everything else possible) in `fill_hardware_job_matmul_template`.
> 
> The intent was that fill-template is called once per matmul _type_, and then prepare just fills in the specific weights address. Since I assume bytes_per_block doesn't depend on which specific layer's WQ matrix we have, computing it in fill-template reduces that work by a factor of O(30) (the number of layers). The only performance-related subtlety I can think of is if offloading from the main thread to the TX worker threads is worth it even with a 30x total penalty, which seems unlikely.
> 
> All that said, if changing to fill-template is infeasible in the current state of the code (e.g., because it has to be done differently on main vs hw_attention_sync), then a comment to the effect that this is the intent for the future would suffice. Assuming, of course, that you agree that this is a good intent.

@axch, I do think the intent here is good. But after digging into this a bit, moving that calculation into the fill_hardware-template isn't trivial. Below is a 'feasability' study from Claude:
```
  Feasibility

  To move the computation into fill_hardware_matmul_job_template, we'd need to thread a PosDevice* through the API. But                 
  fill_hardware_matmul_job_template is deep inside a chain that deliberately has no device:
                                                                                                                                        
  model plugin (llama/feed_forward/MoE)
    → ptensor::fill_matmul_template (static)                                                                                            
      → dtensor::fill_matmul_template (static)
        → fill_hardware_matmul_job_template (no device)                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                        
  Callers that would need updating:
  - ~20+ C++ callsites across h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp, h/tron/models/feed_forward.hpp, h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp,           
  h/tron/models/model.hpp, h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp, t/t_slamtest.cpp, t/t_hwdriver.cpp, t/t_dmaworkout.cpp,                    
  h/tron/emulation/device_matmul.hpp                                                                                
  - Haskell codegen in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:824 emits fill_matmul_template(...) calls                                                  
  - Both fill_hardware_matmul_job_template and fill_attn_job_template, and their fake-mode stubs
  - Multiple overloads of fill_matmul_template at each layer (tensor.hpp has ~6 overloads)                                              
                                                                                                                                        
  This is a substantial API change touching the public h/libpos.hpp surface (which CLAUDE.md flags as requiring explicit authorization).
   It's not strictly a stream_results-only fix — it's a restructuring of the prepare/template split.                                    
```

So, we need to decide if this is the direction we want to bite off right now? CC @mcherba as well....

title: Merge golden gof/shard implementations (Claude vs Gemini.
body:
Implements golden-gof-shard.md design by merging the best parts of two independent implementations:

- gal struct as authoritative GOF store (unique_ptr on edges)
- Query-driven gal creation with page_info on gal
- Trailing boundary shard creation logic
- Ascent-based shards_getting_gofs propagation
- Shard push filtering with hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload threshold
- DMA tracker clear() + bounds assertions
- Comprehensive phase1-5 integration tests

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches scheduler traversal, HW KV offload eligibility, and DMA/backfill paths, so mistakes could cause incorrect attention results or missed offloads. Changes are contained to the GOF/shard offload pipeline and are covered by expanded integration tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces per-edge GOF storage with an edge-owned **authoritative `gal` (GOF-for-all-layers) repository**, where each `gof_job` points at a `gal` holding the shared `page_info` and per-layer GOFs.
> 
> Updates the scheduler’s GOF/shard pipeline to be *query-driven*: `gal` objects are created only when a query token completes a GOF, shards needing the GOF are determined on ascent (`shards_getting_gofs`), and `gof_rodeo_impl` now DMAs only to shards whose token ranges cover the GOF position.
> 
> Reworks shard management by creating shards via **trailing-boundary logic**, adding shard offload eligibility filtering (including `hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload` and partial-shard handling), and making DMA tracking more robust via `device_dma_tracker::clear()`, bounds assertions, and reset/shutdown cleanup. Integration tests are extended to cover the new phases and edge cases.
>

PR summary                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                             
  Fix xfer_gof: DMAing unpopulated gof! assertion in backfill path
                                                                                                                                                             
  - **Bug**: When a new shard is created mid-descent, backfill_shard walks up ancestor edges to DMA prior GOFs into it. Some of those GOFs were never populated, because in an earlier pass their owning gof_rodeo_impl bailed on  shards_getting_gofs.empty() — no live shard covered the position at the moment KV completed, so populate() was skipped. Later shard creation hit the g.populated assert in shard::xfer_gof (src/tron/gof.cpp:95).                            
  - **Fix 1** — lazy populate in backfill_shard (src/tron/gof.cpp): Before calling xfer_gof, if the gof isn't populated, call populate() using the target shard's device and the gal's retained page_info. The gal's page lambdas remain valid (pages backing live queries can't be evicted), so the data is still reachable.
  - **Fix 2** — skip re-populate in gof_rodeo_impl (h/tron/models/model.hpp): Rodeo now guards on !g->populated before calling populate(). This lets backfill and rodeo run in either order — whichever sees the gof first populates it; the other just DMAs. author: mcherba

title: reduce compiler noise under nix
body:
## Background
The nix configuration file `flake.nix` specifies the toolchain and all dependencies for the tron repository. A key benefit of nix is the ability to encapsulate the development environment (tools, dependencies) into that configuration file, so that changes in tools/dependencies can be developed and released as regular PRs. Although the CI runners are set up to begin leveraging this capability, at present, they continue to rely on Ansible scripts to maintain consistent native configurations on those hosts.

I have begun to use the `nix develop` shell on my development host, to understand its impact to our work flow; and to identify and fix any problems that we will encounter once the CI hosts switch over.

An early finding was that the Clang v19.1.7 compiler that is available in the `nix develop` shell includes a cc-wrapper that is configured with a slightly more-hardened set of compiler options than the native Ubuntu-packaged clang v19.1.7 compiler. Due to these subtle changes, code that had previously built without warnings is now emitting warnings. This PR resolves the ones that I have been seeing on the `hwattention_sync` branch. 

## Changes
- Check function return values causing warnings in `huge.cpp`, `t_rinzler_{1,2}.cpp`
- Fix `src/pos/dma_queue.cpp`: unnamed `lock_guard` — lock was never actually held

This PR features the same single-commit patch as in PR #2357, rebased onto `hwattention_sync`. That other PR has been closed.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [x] Spot-check `t_rinzler_1` / `t_rinzler_2` run clean



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes synchronization in `DmaQueue::acquire` (potentially affecting queue allocation behavior under concurrency) and touches low-level hugepage file truncation handling, though changes are small and mainly add error checking/logging.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Reduces new clang/nix build warnings and fixes a real locking bug.** `DmaQueue::acquire` now stores the `std::lock_guard` in a named variable so the mutex is actually held while selecting/initializing a queue.
> 
> In `huge.cpp`, `ftruncate` failures are now checked and logged instead of ignored, and the Rinzler integration tests explicitly ignore the return value of `system("id > /dev/null")` to silence warnings.
