author: bham0n

title: t_clearhbm: direct-mode poison + ECC verify (STORY-385)
body:
## Summary

Reworks `t_clearhbm`'s poison mode to write through the WIM/RIM (9/8) window instead of the Bypass (8/8) window, so the source buffer bytes land in both data and ECC regions of each 576-byte `strip`. Adds a verify mode that confirms the write survived via an identity-matmul readback.

Background from STORY-397: the Bypass DMA used by the previous poison path auto-fills scale bytes to bf16(1.0), regardless of source bytes. That mechanistically explains why every previous attempt to reproduce the post-power-cycle defect through `TRON_POISON_BITS` has failed — the ECC bits the defect depends on weren't reachable through that path.

Two commits:
- **`t_clearhbm: call get_devices()`** (latent bug fix, separable): `ClearHbmListener` was calling `pos_startup()` directly, which populates the device mask but skips the per-device TX/RX worker spawn. Any matmul or `set_hardware_weights` call would then spin forever on `tx_worker_ready`. Switch to `get_devices()` which does both atomically. Prerequisite for any matmul work in this test.
- **`t_clearhbm: add direct-mode poison and ECC verify (STORY-385)`**: main change.

## Behavior

Three modes, gated by env vars (composable):
- `TRON_POISON_BITS=0` (default): zeroize mode, unchanged from before.
- `TRON_POISON_BITS=X` nonzero: direct-mode poison. Writes `uint16(X)` repeated into every byte of the full weight-region HBM (all 32 fetchers × 1.125 GiB = 36 GiB per device, parallel across 8 devices), via 9/8 DMA.
- `TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1`: after the poison pass, run identity-matmul readback and assert every output cell equals `bf16(X) × dequant[low_nibble_of_low_byte(X)]`.

## Scope note

Per project convention, `t_clearhbm` remains a unit test (`DISABLED TRUE` in `t/CMakeLists.txt`, opt-in via `./gen/t_clearhbm`). Promotion to a first-class tool is out of scope.

## Empirical results (STORY-385 FoM)

Ran `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x7fc0 ./gen/t_clearhbm` followed by runtron on andoria-06 (`llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast`, prompt-length 380, length 644):

| Condition                       | Post-power-cycle defect   | Direct-mode poison `0x7fc0`                          |
| ---                             | ---                       | ---                                                  |
| 1st runtron after setup         | Fails with attention NaN  | Fails with attention NaN (`m_star != -inf` assert)   |
| 2nd runtron (no intervening op) | Succeeds (state self-clears) | Fails again (poison persistent)                   |
| Runtron after zeroize           | Succeeds                  | Succeeds                                             |

**Capability achieved:** direct-mode poison puts a card into an attention-NaN state on demand and that state is clearable via the existing zeroize path. Zero false negatives on `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x4444 TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1` (all 32,768 output cells match expected `0x4544` bit-for-bit).

**Signature difference from real power-cycle defect:** our direct-mode poison is strictly more aggressive than the real defect. It persists across runtron invocations because it overwrites the full 9/8 window (36 GiB per device), where the real defect is almost certainly a much smaller ECC-state anomaly that any single runtron op overwrites in passing. Because zeroize clears both, the two states share a family of "ECC/scale bytes in a bad configuration."

**Value delivered by this PR:**
- Eliminates the power-cycle step from the FPGA team's debug cycle. Any candidate fix has to survive a test that triggers attention NaN via poison and clears via zeroize, without the multi-minute overhead of a physical power cycle.
- Narrows the defect's home to something the 9/8 window can address and zeroize's bypass-path bf16(1.0) auto-fill can clear.
- Provides a stronger stress test than the power-cycle defect itself (since our poison is wider).

**Finding a surgical pattern** that reproduces the power-cycle defect's exact fail-once-pass-after signature is a separate empirical search — tracked under STORY-395 (bisection modes) for systematic exploration, or via FPGA-team input on what the post-power-cycle ECC state actually is.

## Coverage caveat

The `reserved[16]` field of each `strip` (32 bytes of ECC region per strip) is not consumed by the systolic, so verify cannot observe it. If the defect pattern turns out to live specifically in `reserved`, a different observation mechanism is needed — out of scope for this PR, tracked under STORY-396.

## Test plan

- [x] `make gen/t_clearhbm` — clean build
- [x] `make format` — no changes needed
- [x] `make lint` — clean
- [x] `make build-test` — clean (verified by author)
- [x] Zeroize sanity (no env vars): all 9 Catch2 assertions pass on andoria-06
- [x] `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x4444 TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1`: all 32,768 output cells (4096 × 8) match expected `0x4544` bit-for-bit, exit 0
- [x] `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x7fc0` followed by runtron: **runtron fails with attention NaN on first invocation**, confirming direct-mode poison successfully induces a defective attention state
- [x] Zeroize + runtron: **runtron succeeds post-zeroize**, confirming recovery

## Related stories

- [STORY-385](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/344d132d3cfd8167abe6d39d5940edc3) (this PR)
- [STORY-397](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/346d132d3cfd8185af3ff95f3692454c) (done): characterization that showed bypass DMA auto-fills ECC to bf16(1.0)
- [STORY-396](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/346d132d3cfd813ebe14c5e57d6caa06) (deferred): reading un-written HBM requires FPGA-team input
- STORY-395 (blocked on 385): bisection modes for FPGA team debugging
author: bham0n

title: Perfetto enhancements and additional events
body:
I've had very limited luck leveraging the 'fill_policy' (and other related settings) in runtron.cfg for 'limiting' the perfetto captures. We actually already have/support phase(1), phase(2) and phase(3)  perfetto phases in the code. "phase 2" is 'generation only' (omits the prefill/prompt-parsing activity). So if we pass --gen as an argument in the tronperf script, that's what you get.

I'm currently using an environment-var strategy where I can set TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN to whatever (e.g. 4096), and if that var is defined, the code will delay the phase(2) invocation until we land on that token, then it will capture to the end of the run.

Caveat: To keep things simple for now, it does require the use of --gen flag when calling tronperf . So prompt tokens are skipped in the traces altogether *if* this env-var is supplied.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes when phased Perfetto tracing starts (including potentially never starting) and adjusts latch/phase synchronization to avoid deadlocks; incorrect thresholds could lead to missing or unexpected traces but shouldn’t affect model outputs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new phased-tracing control `TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN` that delays Perfetto *phase 2* (generation tracing) until the combined prompt+generated token position reaches a configurable threshold, allowing tail-only captures for long runs.
> 
> Hardens the tracing lifecycle in `runtron` by making the start latch one-shot (avoids UB from double `count_down`) and by releasing the start latch on any `phase >= 2` to prevent deadlock when phase 2 is skipped.
> 
> Improves trace usability by extending `perfetto/runtron.cfg` duration for long-context runs and adding/adjusting additional `TRACE_EVENT`s in the scheduler and GOF shard backfill path; docs and `perfetto/tronperf` help text are updated to describe the new env var.
>

```

    plugin_batch.reset_channels(n_attn_workers, n_main_workers);                                                                        
    free_scratchpads_barrier.reset(n_attn_workers);                                                                                     
    qs_for_attn_channel.reset(n_attn_workers, n_attn_workers);   // ← NEW, the bug
  }                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                        
  This runs after plugin_batch.reset_channels and clobbers the producer count.                                                          
                                                                                                                                        
  Why that breaks the ingested plugin
                                                                                                                                        
  The gen plugin (gen/src/tron/h/tron/plugins/ingested_gpt_oss_20b.hpp):                                                                
  - aliases rope_channel(outer_batch.qs_for_attn_channel) (line 11177) — same channel, different name,
  - sets it up as rope_channel.reset(n_workers, n_attn_workers) (line 11312) — n_workers = main+helpers ≈ 2,                            
  - has an empty run_pre_attn (line 8525): void run_pre_attn(...) noexcept { } — attn workers do NOT produce on this channel,
```

title: pos/driver support for head_size 64, selective layers in HW, plus UT coverage
body:
these changes pass all UTs that currently run in our branch plus the new one... they also pass the various tron permutations: TPx, x-Users, short/long context etc.

## Summary

Lays the device/driver-side groundwork for two gpt-oss-20b features on the existing head_size=128 bitfile: (a) running with model `head_size = 64` by zero-padding to the bitfile geometry, and (b) declaring per-layer HW eligibility so sliding-window layers can be skipped on the HW path. No model-side dispatch changes yet — the `head_size == 128` gate at `model.hpp:830` is still in place; this PR makes the lower stack ready for it.

## Changes

**`hw_head_size` constant + model/HW head_size split**
- New `hw_head_size = 128` in `h/pos/config.hpp` documents the bitfile-baked per-head W-MEM/HBM cell count.
- `hw_attn_params` (`h/libpos.hpp`) gains `hw_head_size` alongside the existing `kv_head_size` (model). HW-side stride/layout/DMA paths now read `hw_head_size`; model-side reads continue to use `kv_head_size`. `ah_kvh_size` is still programmed from `kv_head_size`, so the systolic working width tracks the model.
- `xfer_k_packed_entry` / `xfer_v_entry` (`h/pos/hwattention.hpp`, `src/pos/hwattention.cpp`) take both head sizes; HBM stride math switches to `hw_head_size`.
- New padded-shuffle helpers `shuffle_k_head_padded` / `shuffle_v_entry_padded` write a model-`head_size` source into a `hw_head_size` destination layout, leaving the upper cells as zero pad. K cacheblock `set_position` overloads accept both sizes.

**Per-layer HW eligibility**
- `hw_attn_params` gains `std::vector<bool> hw_layers` plus a `layer_uses_hw(layer)` accessor (empty ⇒ all layers HW-eligible, preserving legacy behavior).
- New `gof_configure(hw_attn_params const&, max_layers)` overload threads the field through; the legacy 5-arg overload is unchanged. New module-scope getter `tron::hardware::gof_layer_uses_hw(layer)`.
- Per-shard HBM allocation in `src/tron/gof.cpp` now skips SW-only layers — `kv_shard_layers[l] = {0, 0, 0}` when `!layer_uses_hw(l)`, and the dtor short-circuits on `layer_alloc_bytes == 0`.
- `model.hpp` populates `hw_layers` from `plugin.layers[l].attention.sliding_window_size != illegal_sliding_window` at gof-configure time. Still gated on `head_size == 128` for now.

**Tests (`t/t_hwattention_2.cpp`, FPGA)**
- Coverage for `hw_attn_params` / `gof_configure` / shard alloc gating / padded shuffle helpers.
- HBM round-trip test at `head_size = 64`.
- `unity_matrix_head_size_64` — full FSM flow (Q + K/V → DMA → HW attention → result readback) at `head_size = 64`, validating that result buffers stay at the bitfile-sized 160 entries with valid data in the first half and `sume`/`smax` at the bitfile offsets.
- `unity_matrix_head_size_64_multi_layer` — same flow over layers `{0, 2, 4, 7}` to exercise the per-layer HW mask at the device boundary.

```

Running t_hwattention_2... PASS
Running t_attention... PASS
Running t_compute_attention_unit... PASS
Running t_scheduler... PASS
Running t_generate... PASS
Running t_generate_2... PASS
Running t_rinzler_2... PASS
Running t_gof_dma... PASS
Running t_phase1_integration... PASS
Running t_phase2_integration... PASS
Running t_matmul... PASS
```


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HW-attention KV shuffle/DMA sizing and shard HBM allocation paths; mistakes could corrupt HBM layout or mis-handle layer skipping, though changes are guarded by asserts and extensive new FPGA tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Enables running HW attention with a **model `kv_head_size` smaller than the deployed bitfile’s per-head layout** by introducing a separate `hw_head_size` (via new `hw_baked_head_size` constant) and updating cacheblock shuffles and HBM DMA sizing/stride math to use the HW geometry while padding unwritten cells with zeros.
> 
> Adds **per-layer HW eligibility** (`hw_attn_params::hw_layers` + `layer_uses_hw`) and threads it through GOF configuration and shard KV allocation so SW-only layers allocate no HBM region and are skipped on free/dispatch; `model.hpp` now derives this mask from sliding-window attention layers when configuring GOF.
> 
> Expands FPGA test coverage with a new `t_hwattention_2` suite that validates padded shuffles, HBM round-trips, and end-to-end unity-matrix attention for `head_size=64` (including multi-layer and shard-mask scenarios), plus small updates to existing tests to populate the new params fields.

author: mcherba

title: resolve minibatch race in GOF firing
body:
When running `gen/t_generate_2` at "tp1" (all eight FPGA devices claimed), a `TRON_ASSERT` fires in fire_gof_rodeo (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1597): "GOF rodeo for job 17 but token at pos 348 not kv_complete at layer 0"

The problem is that in TP1, the minibatch size is sometimes not a multiple of 4, which produces a situation where the downstream minibatch can fire the GOF before the upstream has finished writing the mates' K/V.

The fix provided here:

Replace the firing-token-only predicate `(pos+1)%gof_tokens==0 && k_completing` with a per-GOF, per-layer atomic `save_count` on `tron::hardware::gof`. Every `save_k`/`save_v` on a GOF participant — firing token or non-firing mate — does `fetch_add(1, acq_rel)`; the increment that reaches `2*gof_tokens` (8) fires `gof_rodeo`. At gal construction, mates already kv_complete from prior forwards (or non-query mates without saves coming) are pre-loaded by 2. The scheduler also replicates the firing slot's `gof_jobs[]` entry into each non-firing query mate's job_id, so any mate's save can fire and `gof_rodeo_impl` produces identical work via shared `gal_ptr`/`tok_position`/`shards_getting_gofs`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches concurrency-critical paths (GOF dispatch and DMA descriptor submission) using atomics and new locking; correctness depends on memory ordering and avoiding deadlocks/contention under high parallelism.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents premature `gof_rodeo` dispatch when GOF mates complete across different minibatches by adding a per-(GOF, layer) atomic `gof::save_count` and firing only when all 8 K/V saves have been observed.
> 
> Updates `save_k`/`save_v` to increment the counter (with `acq_rel` ordering), and updates the scheduler to replicate `gof_jobs` entries to non-firing query mates and pre-load counts for mates already `kv_complete` from prior forwards.
> 
> Hardens DMA queue usage by adding `DmaQueue::producer_mutex` and locking the multi-descriptor `write_next_descriptor` + `update_tail` sequence in `xfer_blocks` to avoid concurrent ring corruption/crashes.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1b728fbfad0e447d9d30fadcab58f3cb3cbc56ef. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: bham0n

title: Scope GOF mate replication to this edge's flat-array range
body:
## Problem

`t_scheduler` and `t_generate_2` were tripping a kv_complete assertion in `fire_gof_rodeo`:

```
TRON_ASSERT(job.gal_ptr->pages[p].kv_complete_fn(layer)):
  GOF rodeo for job 3 but token at pos 2 not kv_complete at layer 0
```

The GOF mate replication loop in `full_scheduler` matched mates by abs position alone, picking the first `token_jobs` entry whose `token_positions` equals `mate_pos`. With branching, two edges can produce gals at the same gof position; the unfiltered match assigned the same `tok_id` to both gals' `gof_jobs` slots, and the later replication overwrote the earlier. `save_k`/`save_v` then incremented the wrong gal's `save_count`, the count hit 8, the rodeo fired, and the gal read its own pages — which the saves had never touched (`kv_saves=0`). Hence the assertion.

Concretely, in the failing run: a gal at `gof_pos=3` belonging to a branch edge (`edge_base=2`, `edge_start_idx=55`) captured `pages[2,3]` from its own `kv_book` (`0x...10b980`/0,1), but the saves for `tok_id=2,3` came from the *root* edge writing to `0x...15bb00`/2,3.

This regression is on `ff35fc684`, not `1224520e7` (mcherba's hwattention sync change).

## Solution

Restrict the replication search to tok_ids in `[edge_start_idx, edge_start_idx + edge.token_count())` so each gal accumulates `save_count` only from its own edge's saves. Mates without an in-edge save target fall through to the existing preload path.

## Test plan

- [x] `gen/t_scheduler` — 4 clean runs (was failing every run pre-fix)
- [x] `gen/t_generate_2` — 2 clean runs
- [x] `make lint`

wade.body: general pattern you'll see here: we stopped passing 'hw_head_size' from up above through all these functions, restored their original signatures, and they now internally pay attention to the global `::hw_baked_head_size` to determine whether padding is needed, etc. Comment updates reflect that as well.

@bham0n note: this is the other 'work-around' put in place to overcome the fact that we currently have a 'singleton' hw_attn_params block

this is the one 'sub-optimal' aspect of this work IMO... a 'copy buffer' for when model->head_size != hw->baked_head_size. Explanation:
```
  The FPGA image and HBM layout are baked for head_size = 128. HW reads Q with a fixed 128-element-per-
head stride, regardless of the model's actual head_size.                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                  
  For gpt-oss with head_size = 64, the model writes qs_for_attn at a 64-element-per-head stride. If you pointed
 HW at that buffer, every Q-head pointer past head 0 would be at the wrong offset — HW would read into the
 next head's data, mis-strided across all heads.                       
                                                                                                                                                  
 So we keep two parallel Q buffers:
  
  - qs_for_attn: model-native, n_heads * head_size (=n_heads * 64 for gpt-oss). Owned by SW; SW attention reads it unchanged.                     
  - hw_qs_for_attn: HW-shaped, n_heads * hw_baked_head_size (= n_heads * 128). Only allocated when need_q_padding = (head_size != hw_baked_head_size) is true (a static_option, so zero overhead for head_size==128 models).                                                      
                            
launch_hw_attention (self_attention.hpp:520-533) refreshes hw_qs_for_attn from qs_for_attn right before each
 HW dispatch: per head, copy the model's 64 elements into the 128-cell HW slot and zero-fill the upper 64. 
prepare_hw_attention (~line 478) points HW's activation pointers at hw_qs_for_attn when padding is needed, 
and the matmul template uses n_heads * hw_baked_head_size as the contraction size (self_attention.hpp:495) 
so HW's stride matches the padded buffer.

  Net effect: SW attention stays exact (reads native-stride qs_for_attn); HW attention sees a buffer shaped 
exactly the way the FPGA expects, with the unused upper half zeroed so it contributes nothing to the dot 
products.
```

title: move hw_attn_params away from singleton into model-state
body:
Addressing [Story 422](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/move-hw_attn_params-from-singleton-to-per-scheduler-353d132d3cfd81bcb162cbcc6ac3d242). Address this known band-aid from the GPT-OSS / Ingest support work:
```
### Known band-aid: module-scope `gof_params` and multi-model use

`gof_configure` writes to a single module-scope `gof_params` /
`gof_n_layers`. When two models share state space (notably the
target+draft pair in speculative decoding), back-to-back configures
clobber each other. The smaller model's `gof_configure` was
shrinking `gof_n_layers`, leaving gals created afterward sized too
small for the larger model's forward pass — `fire_gof_rodeo` then
tripped `layer < gal->gofs.size()`.

Current band-aid (`src/tron/gof.cpp::gof_configure`): track the
running max of `gof_n_layers` so subsequent shards/gals stay sized
for the largest configured model. Slight memory waste for the
smaller model, functionally correct as long as both models share
architecture (same `n_layers` template, same head counts, same
HW eligibility pattern).

The proper fix is to move `gof_params`/`gof_n_layers` out of
module scope and into per-model (or per-state) storage so each
model owns its own HW-attn config.
```

UTs pass, runtron combinations execute as expected.

## Summary

- Deleted the module-scope `gof_params` / `gof_n_layers` / `gof_is_configured` (plus `gof_configure` / `gof_configured` / `gof_max_layers` / `gof_hw_params` / `gof_layer_uses_hw` / `gof_reset`) from `gof.cpp` / `gof.hpp`. Removed the running-max band-aid along with them.
- Per-model HW-attn config now lives on `self_attn_state`: existing `hw_attn_cfg` plus new `hw_attn_configured` / `hw_attn_max_layers` flags. `model::state` ctor writes the `hw_layers` mask and validation asserts directly into `hw_attn_cfg`.
- `shard` ctor takes an `hw_attn_params const*` and stores it; `xfer_gof` and `backfill_shard` read from `sh->hw_params` instead of module-scope state.
- Scheduler (`full.hpp`) reads `state.self_attn_state.hw_attn_*` at every prior getter site and threads `&state.self_attn_state.hw_attn_cfg` into the shard ctor and `gof_job::hw_params`. Dropped the `min(n_layers_for_gof, model_t::n_layers)` clamp that only existed to compensate for the running-max band-aid.
- Tests: `gof_guard` rewritten as a local holder of `hw_attn_params` + `max_layers`; shard ctors that need HW pass `&gg.params`. Three test cases that asserted on the deleted module-scope contract were removed and the section numbering updated.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the HW-attention/GOF dispatch and shard allocation plumbing (scheduler ↔ model state ↔ DMA), so mis-threaded params or gating could break HW offload or cause invalid HBM accesses. However, changes are largely a state-ownership refactor with added invariants/asserts and updated tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves HW-attention configuration ownership from `tron::hardware` module-scope GOF globals to per-`model::state` storage, so concurrent models (e.g. target+draft speculative decoding) no longer clobber each other’s `hw_attn_params`/layer counts.
> 
> `shard` now stores a `hw_attn_params` pointer supplied by the scheduler/model state; shard allocation gating, `xfer_gof`, and `backfill_shard` read per-model params instead of singleton GOF state. The scheduler and GOF job wiring switch their enablement checks to `self_attn_state.hw_attn_eligible`/`hw_attn_max_layers`, and the model ctor sets the `hw_layers` mask plus validation asserts.
> 
> Also consolidates HW constants by moving `hw_baked_head_size`/max fetchers/max KV heads out of `pos/config.hpp` into `libpos.hpp` (`HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`, `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE`, `HW_MAX_KV_HEADS`, `HW_RMEM_WIDTH_ELEMS`) and updates driver/worker/shuffle/test sizing and loops accordingly, deleting tests that depended on the removed GOF singleton API.
>

At the end of the day, the tron/model level uses these. `libpos.hpp` is the current "public POS API" and as such is the 'contract boundary' between tron and pos/driver. So it made sense to put them here, in the same spirit that we also house `SYSTOLIC_ROWS`, `MAX_SYSTOLIC_COLUMNS` etc (also HW-centric values).

The stuff in `config.hpp` on the other hand represents a "POS driver implementation config" file. So stuff like PCI IDs, IOMMU base, queue sizes, DMA stuff etc belong there, and should _not_ be included up at the tron/model level. We were violating that before.

nvmd, I saw your other comment. Renamed as suggested.

`hw_attn_cfg` lives on the **scheduler's per-model state**. It always has, since we introduced that structure. I haven't moved that. All I've done is now push that down into the gof/shard layer, so that they are using the correct 'instance' for the model being driven, rather than the singleton that layer relied on before.

Here is the justification I asked claude to present before we did this work:
```
  hw_attn_cfg lives on the scheduler's per-model state, not on model_t itself. model_t is the long-lived, 
process-scoped thing (std::shared_ptr<model_t> llm at full.hpp:1137) that holds weights and shape 
constants. model_t::state is per-scheduler scratch — and that's the right scope for hw_attn_cfg, because:

  1. The mutable parts (hw_attn_configured, hw_attn_max_layers, the hw_layers mask) are wired during scheduler/state construction, not at model load.
  2. Speculative decoding gives target and draft each their own full_scheduler → own model::state → own self_attn_state → own hw_attn_cfg. That's exactly the isolation the refactor was after.
  3. The shard ctor's hw_attn_params const* is safe to hold for the shard's lifetime because every shard belongs to a forward pass driven by a particular scheduler, and the model::state outlives every shard the scheduler creates.

Naming caveat: despite the name self_attention<model>::state, the class self_attention<model> itself is
 not an instantiated per-layer  object — grep shows it's only used as a namespace for constants and the
 state template. The "one self_attention per layer" comment at self_attention.hpp:194 is conceptual, not
 literal. Practically, self_attn_state is just a chunk of model::state that groups attention-related per-pass 
scratch (HW results buffers, mutexes, attn mask, and now hw_attn_cfg).

Net: hw_attn_cfg is per-scheduler / per-forward-pass-driver, not per-process-model. Which is what you want.
```

title: src/tron: heap-allocate token_cache singleton
body:
## Summary

The `token_cache()` singleton is a `static token_cache_t it`, which means it gets destroyed during static destruction. Other globals reference it during their own destruction, leading to use-after-destroy races at process exit.

This PR switches the singleton to `static token_cache_t* it = new ...; return *it;` — intentional leak, defers destruction to OS exit. No behavioral change at runtime; only fixes shutdown.

## Test plan

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: change only affects process-shutdown lifetime semantics by intentionally leaking the singleton; normal runtime behavior should remain unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents exit-time use-after-destruction by changing `token_cache()` from a function-local `static token_cache_t` to a heap-allocated singleton (`static token_cache_t*`), so it is not destroyed during global/static teardown.

title: convert wcmd xfers from DMA back to MMIO like main does
body:
This restores our **performance** to parity with the `main` branch for SW-only attention.

It passes all the primary UTs... and now that we have @mcherba's quality fix, t_generate is also passing again:
```
Running t_hwattention... PASS
Running t_hwattention_2... PASS
Running t_attention... PASS
Running t_compute_attention_unit... PASS
Running t_generate... PASS
Running t_generate_2... PASS
Running t_scheduler... PASS
Running t_rinzler_2... PASS
Running t_gof_dma... PASS
Running t_phase1_integration... PASS
Running t_phase2_integration... PASS
Running t_matmul... PASS
```

I also executed multiple combinations of TP1, TP2, TP4, multi-user, long-context, various models including oss-20b and they all behave as expected.

Also, below is Claude's math on why we don't have to worry about FIFO overflow in the `prepare_` path anymore (with fifo-depth of 1024)
```
Legacy alone: mm_in_flight ≤ max_cmds_in_flight = 12, num_wcmds = 1 per matmul → up to 12 wcmds in flight.

  HW-attn alone: mm_in_flight ≤ 1, num_wcmds = 2 × nshards × B. With B=1 (asserted in prepare_hwattn_cmds) and 
nshards ≤ MAX_B = 32 (asserted in fill_attn_job_template), one HW-attn matmul can carry up to 64 wcmds in flight.

  Mixed: HW-attn requires cmds_in_flight == 0 to launch (its mcif_now = 1). But the converse isn't true — once an HW-
attn matmul is in flight, the next legacy at tx_launch sees cmds_in_flight = 1 < 12 and is allowed to queue behind it. So at 
the same moment you can have 1 HW-attn (≤64 wcmds) + 11 legacy (1 each) = up to 75 wcmds in the device FIFO.

  So the real "worst configuration we could ship today" against mm_cmd_fifo_depth = 1024 is ~75. ~13× under that 
generous limit of 1024.

   The conclusion is — overflow is structurally impossible at current caps — the headroom is more than sufficient today, 
but a guard with the proper retire counter is even more clearly worth having since the bound depends on MAX_B and 
max_cmds_in_flight, both of which could move.
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Switches weight-command submission from DMA-descriptor transfers to direct MMIO writes in the matmul TX path; this touches low-level device/ring ordering and could affect correctness under load if tail accounting is off.
> 
> **Overview**
> Restores matmul performance by switching weight command (`wcmd`) delivery from DMA descriptor writes back to **inline PCIe MMIO writes** in `hw_prepare()` for both legacy matmuls and HW-attention, removing the previous descriptor-based `wcmd` transfer path.
> 
> Updates command FIFO sizing assumptions by raising `default_mm_cmd_fifo_depth` to `1024`, and adds/asserts tighter invariants around `wcmd_tail`/`wcmd_tail_a` bookkeeping while cleaning up obsolete debug/assert code in the RX/TX worker paths.

author: BillBaumann

title: h/tron/models/kv_cache: per-token KV completion counters
body:
## Summary

Adds per-token, per-layer KV completion tracking to `tron::page`. New atomic
counter `kv_saves_[offset][layer]` (`std::atomic<uint8_t>[page_size][n_layers]`)
records how many of {K, V} have been saved for each (offset, layer); the call
that pushes the count to 2 is the completing save. Comes with the helpers
`mark_k_complete` / `mark_v_complete` (fetch_add(1, acq_rel), return true on
completion), `is_kv_complete` (acquire load >= 2), and `clear_kv_complete_at`
(relaxed reset across all layers, intended to be called when a new token is
assigned to a page offset).

Two new public accessors for direct V-buffer extraction ride along here:
`v_ptr(layer, kv_head, i_page)` on the `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16` path returns
a raw bf16 pointer into the page, and a new
`get_v(layer, kv_head, i_page, bf16*)` overload on the `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16`
path uninterleaves the striped bf16 storage into a contiguous bf16 buffer.
They have nothing to do with the completion counters; they're called later
by `gof::populate` / `backfill_shard` ([PR #2695](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2695)).
They land in this PR because removing them would make this file deviate from
hwattention_sync, and #2695 would then have to add them back.

`page`'s move constructor is replaced with an explicit one because
`std::atomic` is not movable; it copies the loaded counter values
element-by-element with relaxed ordering and is only invoked during
single-threaded vector construction. A forward declaration of
`struct node_base;` is also added ahead of the `tron` namespace contents
for use by future callers.

This feature is **inert** until callers wire it in (#2695 onward). No build
without HW attention is affected, and no existing call site changes.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run -Werror clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target tron` succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

## Notes for reviewers

The forward declaration `struct node_base;` is unused in this header today;
later code (Future AoF merge PRs) includes this header and references the type. 
Landing it now keeps the per-PR diffs minimal.

Originally authored by: Wado-posi, Brian Hamon

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces new per-token/per-layer atomic counters and a custom move constructor in `tron::page`, which affects concurrency behavior and object movement in a performance-critical KV cache path. Also extends AVX512 `V` access APIs; incorrect use could lead to subtle correctness/perf issues.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **per-token, per-layer KV completion tracking** to `tron::page` via a new `kv_saves_[offset][layer]` atomic counter and helper APIs (`mark_k_complete`, `mark_v_complete`, `is_kv_complete`, `clear_kv_complete_at`) intended to let callers trigger work once both K and V are saved.
> 
> Updates `page` move semantics to an explicit move constructor that copies atomic counter values, and extends V-buffer access by adding `v_ptr(...)` on the non-interleaved path and a new AVX512 `get_v(..., bf16*)` overload to uninterleave stored V data into a contiguous bf16 buffer.
>

body:
## Summary

Three coordinated changes to `ranged_mask`, plus two explanatory comments added in response to CQA review:

- **`h/tron/models/ranged_mask.hpp`** drops the stub `shard` struct in favour of `using shard = tron::hardware::shard;` — the real type lands via [#2676](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2676).
- **`src/tron/models/ranged_mask.cpp`** has two surgical fixes plus two explanatory comments:
  - Push-time cursor fix: the shard pop now uses `< hi` instead of `< edge_hi`, matching the loop comment.
  - Pop-time `dma_complete` gate is removed.
  - New comment above the `have_shard`/`have_query` guards explains why the shard guard uses the shrinking `hi` while the query guard keeps `edge_hi` (prior pop_backs already trim the query stack to match — both reach the same trim).
  - New comment in the SW→HW transition block notes that DMA-complete eligibility is enforced at push time by the walker (`h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp`), so the unconditional pop here relies on a caller guarantee.
- **`t/t_ranged_mask.cpp`** swaps the stub `b_shard` aggregate initializer for `shard(nullptr, 0, 0)` (the real shard has a deleted copy ctor; `max_layers=0` is the test-stub sentinel that makes `dma_complete()` true).

Why now: [#2676](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2676)'s headers provide the real shard type, so the local stub becomes redundant. The `dma_complete` eligibility filter is moving from pop-time to push-time — a follow-up walker PR will only push DMA-complete shards onto the shard stack, so the pop-time gate has no work left to do.

## Test plan

body:
# WILL BE CLOSED SOON -- superceded by PR #2796

## Summary

Long-pole implementation drop for the GoF/Shard merge. Lands
`src/tron/gof.cpp` (shard ctor/`xfer_gof`, `gof::populate`) plus the
pos-side infrastructure it depends on. 18 files, organized in two
layers:

- **Layer 1 — h/ infrastructure**: `h/libpos.hpp`, `h/pos/config.hpp`,
  `h/pos/device.hpp`, `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`, `h/pos/hwattention.hpp`,
  and new `h/pos/device_dma_tracker.hpp` — extends `hw_attn_params`,
  introduces `dma_xfer_state`, virtualizes `xfer`/`xfer_blocking`/
  `isdone`/`wait` on cacheblocks, adds the `device_dma_tracker`
  singleton.
- **Layer 2 — src/ implementation**: new `src/tron/gof.cpp` and
  `src/pos/device_dma_tracker.cpp`; updates to
  `src/pos/{hwattention,driver,device,dma,dma_queue,fake}.cpp`
  matching the header changes; 1-line CMake add for `gof.cpp`.
- **Tests**: `t/t_dma.cpp`, `t/t_mwaitx.cpp` — call-site updates for
  the new `dma_xfer_state` return type from `xfer_blocks`.

## Stub note

`gof::backfill_shard` is intentionally a no-op in this PR (empty body,
parameters commented out, `TODO` comment). The full implementation
walks the scheduler tree via `node_base::tree_parent` /
`tree_height` / `tree_edge_gals` — APIs added in a separate later
patch. No caller in this PR's scope reaches `backfill_shard` (its
only invoker lives in code that depends on those node_base virtuals
that don't exist on main yet). The function declaration in the
already-merged `h/tron/gof.hpp` matches.

## Debug-flag scrub & cleanup (applied during review)

`src/pos/device.cpp` previously had `#define DEBUG_INIT 1` plus
`#ifdef DEBUG_INIT`. Because the macro is always defined, the
`#ifdef` guard was unconditionally true regardless of value — the
debug code was active in every build. Fixed two ways: value flipped
`1` to `0`, and guard changed to `#if DEBUG_INIT` so the value
actually gates compilation. The neighbouring `DEBUG_RESETS` /
`DEBUG_VFIO` macros were converted to the same `#define X 0` + `#if X`
form for consistency.

Two debug-only value bumps that landed in the source branch were
reverted here so they do not propagate to main:

- `maxpolls`: back to `1e9 / timeout_ns` (~1 second), was 100×.
- `max_xfer_time_in_ns`: back to `100000000` (100 ms), was 10 s.

Other small cleanups applied during review:
- Five commented-out `wqentry` fields removed from the public
  `h/pos/device.hpp` struct.
- Three `#if 0` / commented blocks removed from `src/pos/device.cpp`
  (pseudochannel debug print, init register dump, three
  `wcmd/acmd/mdwd` req-id allocations).
- Bounds-check assert added on
  `device_dma_tracker::await_layer`'s `layer` arg, mirroring `push()`.
- Unused `nlohmann_json` link dropped from `pos` and `pos_fake`.
- TODO comment on `fake_devices` null-deref hazard.
- Move-ctor / move-assignment comments on `DmaQueue` extended to state
  the quiescence invariant the relaxed atomic loads rely on.
- One-line comment on `t/t_dma.cpp`'s `kv_xfer = true` to record why
  the kv path is the right one to exercise post-refactor.

## File-level port decisions

Six `h/` files were ported at file level from the source branch rather
than merged surgically:

- `h/libpos.hpp` — `hw_attn_params` extension touches struct layout
  pervasively; piecemeal merge fragile
- `h/pos/device.hpp` — `wqentry` extensions + `dma_xfer_state` struct
  + several constants intertwined
- `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp` — atomic state + move semantics + mutex
  introduce coupled changes throughout the class
- `h/pos/hwattention.hpp` — virtualization of cacheblock xfer API
  cuts across many methods
- `h/pos/device_dma_tracker.hpp` — new file
- (`src/pos/hwattention.cpp` + `src/pos/driver.cpp` + `src/pos/fake.cpp`
  also ported at file level on the cpp side for symmetry — they implement
  the file-level-ported headers)

`h/pos/config.hpp` is surgical (constants only); `src/tron/CMakeLists.txt`
is a 1-line add (`gof.cpp`); the rest of the `src/pos/*.cpp` and the
two test files are surgical.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target tron` succeeds locally
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target pos` succeeds locally
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target pos_fake` succeeds locally
- [x] `cmake --build gen` (full 665-target build) succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

Originally authored by: Mike Cherba, Alexey Radul, Wado-posi, Edward Kmett, Brian Hamon, Fritz Obermeyer, Hannah Van Eenoo

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches low-level POS driver DMA submission/completion logic and hardware-attention KV memory layout/transfer paths; concurrency and correctness issues could cause hangs, data corruption, or hard-to-debug device timeouts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a first cut of the **GOF/shard hardware-attention KV offload pipeline** (`src/tron/gof.cpp`): shards allocate per-layer K/V HBM regions (with per-layer HW eligibility via `hw_attn_params::hw_layers`), GOFs populate `k_hwcacheblock`/`v_hwcacheblock`, and `shard::xfer_gof` DMAs those cacheblocks to the device.
> 
> Refactors POS DMA and HW-attention transfer plumbing around a new `dma_xfer_state` token: `xfer_blocks()` now returns structured completion state (descriptor index + wrap count + optional readback), `wait_for_xfer_blocks()` consumes it, and a new `device_dma_tracker` singleton tracks/polls per-device in-flight GOF DMAs and can await per-layer completion.
> 
> Updates HW-attention cacheblock APIs to be **polymorphic** (`hwcacheblock::xfer`/`xfer_blocking` + `isdone`/`wait`), adds padded shuffle support for model `kv_head_size` differing from the bitfile’s baked `HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`, and adjusts attention job templating to support per-batch token indices plus per-shard HBM bases.
>

title: h/tron, h/pos: corrections caught during the main-stack code review
body:
## Summary

Backports corrections from the hwattention_sync → main merge stack PRs.

### Code-correctness fixes

- **`h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp`**: removed a duplicate `// Returns true if this was the completing save (count reached 2).` comment above `mark_k_complete` (the line appeared twice).

- **`h/pos/hwattention.hpp`** (`xfer_v_entry`): passed literal `0` as the `readback_offset` argument for non-final fetcher transfers in V xfers. The "no readback" sentinel is `no_readback_sentinel = 0xffffffff`; literal `0` would install a readback at offset 0, which is a real (not dead) offset. The matching `v_hwcacheblock::xfer` in `src/pos/hwattention.cpp` already used `no_readback_sentinel`, so this aligns the inline helper with the canonical call site.

- **`h/pos/hwattention.hpp`** (`check_k_range` / `check_v_range`): silently no-op stubs now have a TODO marker so future readers can grep them up. Bodies remain no-ops pending shard-aware bounds tracking.

- **`h/pos/device.hpp`** (`wqentry::in_flight`): comment claimed `hw_prepare` asserts the field is false on entry. `hw_prepare` in `src/pos/worker.cpp` does not actually assert this. Rewrote the comment to describe what the field tracks without claiming a behavior that does not exist.

### Debug-value reverts

- **`h/pos/config.hpp`**: `maxpolls` back to `1e9 / timeout_ns` (~1 second of polling, was 100×); `max_xfer_time_in_ns` back to 100 ms (was 10 s). Both bumps were debug-only and should not have remained on this branch.

- **`src/pos/device.cpp`**: `DEBUG_INIT` flipped from 1 to 0 and the guard switched from `#ifdef DEBUG_INIT` to `#if DEBUG_INIT` so the value actually gates compilation (the macro is always defined). `DEBUG_RESETS` / `DEBUG_VFIO` converted to the same `#define X 0` + `#if X` form for consistency.

### Cleanup

- **`h/pos/device.hpp`**: removed five commented-out `wqentry` fields from the public struct surface.
- **`src/pos/device.cpp`**: removed three `#if 0` / commented blocks (pseudochannel debug print, init register dump, `wcmd/acmd/mdwd` req-id allocations).
- **`src/pos/CMakeLists.txt`**: dropped unused `nlohmann_json` link from both `pos` and `pos_fake`.
- **`src/pos/fake.cpp`**: TODO comment on `fake_devices` null-deref hazard.
- **`src/pos/device_dma_tracker.cpp`**: bounds-check assert on `await_layer`'s `layer` arg, mirroring `push()`.
- **`h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`**: extended move-ctor / move-assignment comments to state the quiescence invariant the relaxed atomic loads rely on.
- **`t/t_dma.cpp`**: one-line comment on why `kv_xfer = true` is the right path to exercise post-refactor.
- **`src/tron/models/ranged_mask.cpp`**: explanatory comments on the asymmetric loop guards and the SW→HW transition's caller-guarantee.

These were surfaced by the Code Quality Agent during reviews of [#2693](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2693), [#2694](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2694), and [#2695](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2695). Backporting them here keeps the eventual main → `hwattention_sync` sync clean.

author: BillBaumann

title: fix HW-attn quality: send prefill tokens through SW always, remove them from hw_plan
body:
**Bug.** Silent SW/HW coverage gap during prefill. The scheduler's
`build_edge_ranges` optimistically moves queries from `sw_mask` to `hw_mask`
every time a shard is popped during ascent and emits an `hw_plan_entry` for
them. The model's `construct_hw_plan`, however, refuses to dispatch HW for
any minibatch where `items.size() > 1` (prompt processing — design intent
that prefill stays on SW for now). The mask and the dispatch decision were
inconsistent: the planner gave the queries to HW, HW didn't actually run,
and SW's `apply_page_tok` gate (`sw_required(job_ix)`) then skipped those K
positions because they were no longer marked SW-required.

Result: for every prefill minibatch where the KV-cache extent crossed
`MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN` (128) — i.e., where the scheduler started moving
queries from `sw_mask` to `hw_mask` at shard boundaries — most of the
legitimate causal K positions were attended over by *neither* SW nor HW.
Layer-0 attention output diverged, cascading through the residual + MLP
into every subsequent layer's K/V writes and leaving the KV cache
materially different at decode start. End-to-end this manifested as the
HW-build model producing degraded, qualitatively wrong output (e.g.
14-token non-reasoning replies vs the SW build's 83-token chain-of-thought
on the same prompt).

**Fix.** In `scheduler::full::forward()`, after `compute_forward_args` /
`finalize_ranges` have built `query_mask` and `hw_plan`, reconcile both
with the model's HW-dispatch gate at the fwd level. When
`token_jobs.size() > 1` (prompt processing — same condition the model
uses), fold each range's `hw_mask` back into its `sw_mask` and clear
`hw_plan`. SW then owns every visible (query, K-position) pair; HW
dispatch stays disabled as designed; mask + plan match reality before
either reaches the model.

**Scope.** Single localized change in `h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp` plus
explanatory Note. No API or schema changes. No behavior change for decode
fwds (`token_jobs.size() == 1` → reconciliation skipped → HW continues to
dispatch as before). The model-side `is_prompt_processing` early-return
in `construct_hw_plan` remains as defense-in-depth.

**Verification.** With the fix applied, the HW-build run produces the
same output as the SW-only run on the test prompt. KV-cache snapshot diff
between modes goes from mean-abs K = 0.12–0.59 across layers 1–31 to bit-identical.

This at least pulls our quality up to expectations while we don't support prefill in HW. That is obviously the next feature/support we should be chasing in this HW branch I guess.

author: Wado-posi

title: Implement pos_heap_v2 for DMA-able memory without fragmentation
body:
The investigation of STORY-425 led to a conclusion that the large number of 8K `hwcacheblock` objects being allocated and released was fragmenting the DMA-able, hugepage-backed memory heap.

A specification for an allocator with separate slabs for each allocation size was developed and reviewed. It is part of the changeset for this PR.

The new allocator is *disabled* by default. To enable it, set the environment variable `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`. 

The python fuzzer, `/tools/rinzler-fuzz.py` is able to reproduce the defect (when you run rinzler without `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`). Note: in order for the memory pressure to trigger cache evictions, you need more than the default 16 `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES`. (I use 32.) Evictions typically begin once the memory exceeds 50% used.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Replaces core DMA allocation plumbing behind a runtime flag and adds new concurrency/ASAN/shadow-map behavior; mistakes could cause allocator corruption, leaks, or crashes under production load. Also changes DMA-range validation and introduces new FUSE stats registration paths that run at startup.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new DMA hugepage allocator, `pos_heap_v2`, implementing per-size-class arenas backed by a hugepage pool (SMALL sub-slabs vs LARGE hugepages), ASAN poisoning/unpoisoning, optional `HEAP_V2_SHADOW` validation + `dump_profile`, and reserve-draining logic to reduce pool mutex churn.
> 
> Wires allocator selection into `pos_heap_setup()` via `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` (and build default `TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON`), updates DMA allocation wrappers (`dma_allocate*`, `pos_allocate*`, `heap_start/heap_size`, shutdown/leak checks) to route to the chosen heap, and registers a new `/rinzler/stats/dma_heap/` FUSE stats tree with per-class and pool counters plus dynamic tronstats descriptors.
> 
> Extends the HBM allocator with optional `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW`, caller-PC attribution, fragmentation-oriented stats (`free_total`, `free_blocks`), OOM profile dumping, and per-device FUSE stats under `/rinzler/stats/devices/<bdf>/allocator/`; also fixes a DMA buffer bounds check to use inclusive heap endpoints and adds new tests/make targets (notably `t_heap_v2` and a disabled contention microbenchmark).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ff19045fd05fea80d12eea14029ccad86a8793c7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->




## Performance: pos_heap_v2 vs pos_heap

A microbenchmark (`t/t_alloc_contention.cpp`, gated by `[.perf]`) compares both allocators under concurrent threads doing tight `allocate / touch / deallocate` loops. Three scenarios on andoria-06 (16 hugepages, 500 ms wall clock per scenario):

| Scenario | Threads | Legacy ops/s | v2 ops/s | v2 / legacy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single-thread baseline (class 3, 8 KiB) | 1 | 2.84 M | 49.6 M | **17.5×** |
| Same-class contention (all class 3) | 16 | 0.78 M | ~2.7 M | **~3.4×** |
| Multi-class parallelism (classes 3, 5, 8, 10) | 16 | 0.83 M | ~6.3 M | **~7.6×** |

Two structural wins:

1. **Per-op cost is lower even single-threaded.** Free-list pop/push on a per-class slab is cheaper than buddy splinter/coalesce on a global tree.
2. **Per-class mutex parallelizes as designed.** Legacy collapses to a single mutex under any concurrency; v2 scales with the number of distinct classes in flight.

### The pool.mu finding

The original v2 had a hidden bottleneck the microbench surfaced: with one slot in flight per thread, every `alloc + dealloc` cycle locked the global `pool.mu` twice (release the slab on dealloc-when-empty, acquire one on the next allocate). Per-class `arena.mu` parallelism didn't help because the work crossed the arena boundary on every cycle.

The spec anticipated this — `doc/pos_heap_v2.md` § "Open questions" Q1 RESOLVED:

> Empty-current-slab policy: eagerly return. **If churn shows up in profiling, add a global pressure-aware reserve capped to 1–2 slabs total, reclaimed before any OOM.**

This PR lights up that reserve:

- `arena_deallocate` keeps a SMALL-class slab in `partial_head` when its `nr_live` drops to 0 and no other partial slab exists in the arena. The next allocate reuses it without touching `pool.mu`.
- LARGE-class slabs (each pinning a whole 1 GiB hugepage) are not cached.
- `pos_heap_v2::drain_reserves()` walks SMALL arenas and releases cached empties; called automatically by `allocate` on first failure (implements the spec's "reclaimed before any OOM" guarantee).

A few unit tests in `t_heap_v2.cpp` had been stricter than the spec — they pinned the pre-Q1 "always release" implementation detail. They now call `drain_reserves()` before post-drain counter checks. New test `drain on pressure: cached SMALL reserve releases under acquire failure` directly exercises the spec invariant.

### Net result

- Multi-class concurrent throughput: **30× faster than baseline v2, ~120× faster than legacy.**
- Single-thread throughput: **8.4× faster than baseline v2, 17.5× faster than legacy.**
- `t_heap_v2`: 26 cases, 5570 assertions, all passing. `t_pos_lifecycle`: passes under both legacy and `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`.

author: bham0n

title: proper per-model dma_tracker design, sized by model->n_layers
body:
Removes the hard-coded `hwkv_max_layers` const used to size dma_tracker queues, and replaces the **singleton** dma_tracker with a **per-model** registry pattern, where trackers are only created/initialized inside the hw-attn-eligible code branch.

## Design Notes

### Storage in state
Use `std::optional<tron::hardware::device_dma_tracker>`, default-empty,
`emplace(cfg.max_layers)` inside the hw-attn-eligible branch. Keeps the
allocation inline on `state` (no heap), skips the cost for models that
never engage HW attention (e.g., the EAGLE draft today), and gives every
push/poll/await site a uniform `dma_tracker->method()` form.

### Lambda capture
`model<>::state` is non-movable (mutexes, latch_arena, etc.), so `this`
is a stable pointer for the state's lifetime. The lambdas at `model.hpp:885-889` become:
```cpp
on_await_dma.push_back([this](size_t l) { dma_tracker->await_layer(l); });
on_forward_poll.push_back([this]() { dma_tracker->poll_completions(); });
```

**Chosen approach: process-global tracker registry.**

Add to `pos/device_dma_tracker.hpp`/`.cpp`:
- A file-static `std::mutex registry_mu` and
  `std::vector<device_dma_tracker*> live_trackers`.
- In `device_dma_tracker::device_dma_tracker(size_t max_layers)`: take
  the lock and `live_trackers.push_back(this)`.
- In `device_dma_tracker::~device_dma_tracker()`: take the lock and
  remove `this` from the vector.
- A free function `tron::hardware::clear_all_dma_trackers()` that locks
  the registry and calls `clear()` on every entry. Idempotent.

Use raw pointers (not weak_ptr) because trackers are owned in-place
inside `std::optional<...>` on `model<>::state` — there's no
`shared_ptr` to weaken from. The lifetime guarantee is: tracker's own
ctor/dtor maintain the registry under the same mutex used by
`clear_all_dma_trackers`, so a tracker can't disappear between "we read
the pointer" and "we call clear()" — the dtor would be blocked behind
the registry lock.

`pos_shutdown` calls `clear_all_dma_trackers()` instead of the old
singleton `clear()`. This restores the singleton-era property that
shards pinned **only** by tracker queues get destroyed while devices
are alive — without it, the per-model design would silently regress,
because the tracker (now a member of `model<>::state`) outlives
`pos_shutdown` and would otherwise drop its `shared_ptr<shard>` refs
late, with `shard::~shard()` calling `free_kv_weights(dev, …)` on a
dangling device.

### Concurrency
Each tracker has its own mutex. Target and draft don't share locks.
The DmaQueue's wrap-count head is shared device state read through
`hwcacheblock::isdone(dev, xfer)`; multiple trackers can call it
concurrently — it's the same code path as today, just with different
priority queues feeding it.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HW-attention DMA completion bookkeeping and shutdown ordering; mistakes could leave in-flight DMA untracked or free shard/device resources in the wrong order. Changes are localized and include new unit tests to cover sizing, lifecycle, and concurrency.

> **Overview**
> Moves GOF/shard DMA completion tracking from a process-wide singleton (`device_dma_tracker`) to a per-model `dma_tracker` stored on `model<>::state` (via `std::optional`) and constructed only when HW attention is enabled/eligible, removing the hard-coded `hwkv_max_layers` cap.
> 
> Adds a process-global registry of live `dma_tracker` instances so `pos_shutdown` can call `clear_all_dma_trackers()` to drain queues and release shard references before devices are torn down; updates GOF rodeo/backfill paths to attribute DMA completions to the owning model’s tracker.
>

wade.body:
After further digging and attempts to verify this, it basically seems this hypothesis is theoretically correct (about the missing gate), but the conditions that would actually exercise it don't arise under the current speculation flow.

Below are the findings of investigation:

>   The shard-creation paths only fire when:
>   - Boundary path: trailing = first_trailing falls within the edge's token range. For a fresh new edge with shards.empty(), this would create a shard at the boundary
>   base.
>   - Leaf-trailing path: n->children.empty() AND trailing_tokens >= 4 (gof_tokens). Same — would create if no shard at that base exists yet.
> 
>   For the EAGLE to be the one entering this block "first" on a path that creates (rather than reuses) a shard, the EAGLE has to be the one extending a leaf edge into >=
>    4 trailing tokens past a boundary, on an edge whose shards vector doesn't already include that shard.
> 
>   With draft_tree_max_width = 1 (the default — src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:24), drafts form a chain off the accepted-path leaf. But the actual sequence of events
>   is:
> 
>   1. exact samples: extends the accepted leaf edge by 1 token. exact's compute_forward_args walks the leaf edge with edge.dirty=true. Creates any new shards (correctly
>   sized for 32 layers). Sets edge.dirty=false.
>   2. EAGLE drafts: hangs off the new tip. EAGLE's compute_forward_args walks the same leaf edge — but edge.dirty is now false (exact just cleared it), so EAGLE doesn't
>   enter the block on that edge. EAGLE then walks the draft's own edge, which is short and never triggers leaf-trailing creation.
> 
>   So in practice, the exact always touches the accepted leaf edge first (because sampling is what grows it), and the EAGLE never creates shards.
> 

I did add the extra guard for defensiveness, and did add another test that drives enough context to cross the shard-creation boundary, to ensure that logic is working as expected between draft/target models.

title: move hw_prepare to prep_worker threads per dev
body:
Add a prep_worker thread per device and make the main thread call to prepare nonblocking and queue the prepare action to the dev specific thread.

this requires some new synchronization work as prior the serialized sequence served as the synchronization baser but now we need to make that more deliberate.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core FPGA driver threading, work-queue ordering, and WQE lifetime; incorrect synchronization could cause hangs, wrong launches, or reuse of in-flight work requests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves **`hw_prepare`** off the caller/TX path onto a **per-device PREP thread** with a **`prepwork`** queue, replacing implicit ordering from synchronous prepare with explicit **`wqentry`** gates (`prep_done`, `hw_prepared`) and **mwaitx** waits.
> 
> **Prepare → launch flow:** `prepare_hardware_*` now enqueues prep work instead of calling `hw_prepare` inline; **`hardware_job::operator()`** and **`stream_results()`** wait for **`hw_prepared`** before TX launch or reading result metadata. Completion callbacks (or the direct-launch path) set **`prep_done`** so entries can be reused.
> 
> **`prepare_and_launch_direct`:** Optional **`direct_launch`** lets the PREP worker enqueue to **`inwork`** after prepare (used by MoE **`prepare_and_launch_direct`**), reducing cross-FPGA serialization on the main prepare/launch sequence.
> 
> **Ops/tuning:** Startup barrier counts PREP per device; prep threads are **joined** on shutdown. **`--prep-cores`** / **`prep_pin_thread`** (currently aliased to helper cores) and default prep core lists in **`system_optimize`**; minor **`resource-map.yaml`** comments. TX path tweaks: larger **`max_cmd_fifo_depth`**, **`short_timeout_ns`** for slot waits, more **`mwaitx`** in **`tx_wait_for_slots`**, prefetch/trace in **`hw_prepare`**, TX waits for prep before launch.

author: bgamari-positron

title: Parallelize gpt-oss expert weight loading with bounded fanout
body:
## Summary

Initial draft/RFC from an investigation into loading `gpt-oss-120b` TP4 on a vatlas4 system.

The vatlas systems are a new bring-up target for this workflow. Please read this as evidence from loading `gpt-oss-120b` onto a vatlas4 system, not as a settled runtime policy. This is not my area of expertise, and I am skeptical of the implementation until someone familiar with generated model loading, `app_pool`, tensor placement, and FPGA weight loading reviews it carefully.

This PR is a single commit against `main`. It intentionally does not include the #2614 in-process weights-cache work or the previously cherry-picked `99c6708f2db8e38fa1932c4c42d89cba72479e44` commit.

## Changes

- Generated expert safetensor loading now calls a C++ helper that visits experts in parallel.
- Per-tensor quantization/load work uses bounded fanout via `TRON_PER_TENSOR_LOAD_WORKERS`, defaulting to 16 workers.
- `set_hardware_weights` is serialized per target `PosDevice`; `alloc_hardware_weights` remains unwrapped because the allocator path already locks.
- Rotated placement shares atomic rotation state across loader threads while preserving thread-local placement contexts.
- Tag-selected model builds pass `--min-support working` so local `support_level: none` overrides cannot emit stale plugin declarations.

## Evidence

Tested candidate:

```text
base:          main
commit:        b556b5527
binary sha256: dd7cb0c14ae73fa642469a7e8e1a644c092af5d7ea3f99e668ae1580f6b7d5ae
```

Live load results on a vatlas4 system:

| Model shape | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-oss-120b` TP4 | success | 108.359s tensor allocation/load; about 149.4s from config start to ready |
| `gemma-2-9b` TP1, replication 4 | success | slowest instance loaded in 18.247s; slowest add-to-ready about 40.0s |
| `llama-3.3-70b` TP2, replication 2 | failed | both instances segfaulted at dense safetensors token-embedding load, not the expert-parallel path |

The earlier cached-weight baseline for `gpt-oss-120b` TP4 spent 497.782s in the model-load phase, so the current candidate is comfortably under the 10 minute platformd watchdog for that shape.

## Test Plan

Checks run before updating this PR branch:

```text
uv run --with pyyaml python config/test_model_definitions.py: pass, 48 tests
uvx ruff format --check config/test_model_definitions.py: pass
git diff --check: pass
fourmolu on touched Haskell files: pass
clang-format on touched C++ files: pass
targeted t_placer rotated-placement regression: pass
cmake --build gen --target rinzler -j16: pass, 6:13.15
vatlas4 live load, gpt-oss-120b TP4: pass
vatlas4 live load, gemma-2-9b TP1 replication 4: pass
vatlas4 live load, llama-3.3-70b TP2 replication 2: failed as noted above
```

An unbounded local production build saturated the guest and required a reset. The repeatable build command on this system was `cmake --build gen --target rinzler -j16`.

## Review focus

- Is generated expert-load parallelism the right boundary for this optimization?
- Is the per-device `set_hardware_weights` lock sufficient for low-level DMA queue safety?
- Should `TRON_PER_TENSOR_LOAD_WORKERS` default to 16, or should it derive from model shape or hardware metadata?
- Is shared rotated placement state the right representation under parallel expert loading?
- Does the Llama dense safetensors failure expose an existing issue that this PR should avoid touching or explicitly regression-test?

Refs #2776

wade.body:
I think `alloc_hardware_weights` should be fine... it uses `allocator::allocate()` which _is_ thread-safe (uses a mutex).

But `set_hardware_weights` is not. So concurrent accesses on the *same* PosDevice would contend on (e.g.) `load_weight_q` DmaQueue with no lock/guard protection.

I'm inclined to balk at this a bit... this sort of free-floating lock placement is detached from what it's actually protecting. IMO it would be better to add a mutex member to the PosDevice (or DmaQueue) and use it directly inside of `device::set_hardware_weights`. A few reasons:

1. it co-locates the lock with the thing it's protecting... in this case (critically) the `load_weight_q` which is mutated inside that function
2. finer-grain control over the lock period: based on my read of the code, it's really only the `xfer_blocks` we need to span with protection. The `wait_for_xfer_blocks` busy-spin is is just a read of monotonic, per-range descriptors. I _think_ it would be safe for concurrent waiters to land there, cuz they'd have their own disjoint desc values.
3. with this placement, it forces two parallel callers to fully serialize, even over that `wait_for_xfer_blocks` which as discussed, I don't think is necessary
4. any future parallel state/access to that DMA q from elsewhere will have to do this same thing (and can be missed). If we put it at-the-source, we don't have that potential drift

On the other hand, I also get nervous about introducing mutex locks in high-volume functions like that, if not absolutely necessary for a general solution. At the end of the day this is probably 'fine' just because I don't think we're actually parallelizing across the **same device**, right? Ergo, this approach may be acceptable.

I would still ultimately defer to @mcherba 's input/insight on this matter.

title: pos/alloc: instrument HBM allocator with FUSE stats and HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #2785. Instruments `tron::hardware::allocator` (the HBM allocator) with FUSE stats and opt-in caller-attribution shadow map, mirroring `pos_heap_v2`'s observability surface for the host DMA heap.

- `/rinzler/stats/devices/<bdf>/allocator/{capacity,free_max,free_total,free_blocks,allocations,deallocations}` — six gauge/counter endpoints per device. Byte stats are whole-device totals (scaled by `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE` internally).
- `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW` (compile-time CMake option on the `system` library): per-allocation caller-PC capture at the `alloc_kv_weights` / `alloc_hardware_weights` API boundary plus a `dump_profile()` diagnostic. Symbol resolution via `addr2line` against the rinzler binary.
- Write-triggered `dump_profile_trigger` FUSE control file per device — `echo 1 > .../dump_profile_trigger` fires a snapshot to `$TRON_HBM_PROFILE_PATH`. Always reads as 0.
- OOM error messages in `driver.cpp` now include caller PCs unconditionally (useful even without HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW); SHADOW build also fires `dump_profile("kv_OOM" / "weights_OOM")`.

This is the "extract to main" companion of the same work that exists on `pos_heap_v2`. Commits cherry-picked verbatim from the original development, plus one compatibility commit (`580ad39a1`) that aligns `src/pos/fake.cpp` with the structure used on hwattention_sync (drop the local minimal `struct PosDevice`, use the real one from `pos/device.hpp`, change `fake_devices` to a nullptr-initialized `PosDevice*` array, add empty `devices` global + `pos_list_devices()`) and adds explicit `#include "pos/alloc.hpp"` to `src/rinzler.cpp` / `src/runtron.cpp` so `pos_devices_register_fuse_stats()` is visible without relying on a transitive include path that doesn't exist on main.

Used in the diagnosis of MMLU heap-exhaustion crashes that motivated [STORY-425](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/356d132d3cfd81f28995f545be1bd260). Related characterization work tracked under [STORY-446](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/35ed132d3cfd81d48e1ee87bcc26c276) (HBM allocator fragmentation characterization).

## Test plan

- [x] \`make build-test\` clean
- [x] \`make test\` — same parallel-contention pattern as the base branch; all directly-relevant tests pass individually: \`t_heap_v2\`, \`t_tronstats_convention\`, \`t_pos_lifecycle\`, \`t_pos_lifecycle_fake\`, \`t_heap\`, \`t_alloc\`.
- [x] HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW build path: \`cmake --preset native -B gen-shadow -DHBM_ALLOC_SHADOW=ON\` then \`cmake --build gen-shadow --target rinzler -j\` builds clean.
- [x] Used in MMLU diagnostics on \`pos_heap_v2\` — \`dump_profile\` output is well-formed and resolves cleanly via \`addr2line -e gen-shadow/rinzler -f -p <pc>\`.
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Reviewer-approved

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes allocator layout behind a compile flag and registers live device pointers in FUSE callbacks; misconfigured `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW` across TUs would corrupt `PosDevice`, but the PR routes the macro through `system` to prevent that.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **observability** to the per-device HBM `tron::hardware::allocator`, parallel to the host `pos_heap_v2` story: fragmentation gauges (`free_total`, `free_blocks`), capacity, and cumulative alloc/dealloc counters, plus optional **caller-PC shadow** when `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW` is enabled at configure time (declared **PUBLIC on `system`** so `sizeof(allocator)` stays consistent wherever `alloc.hpp` is included).
> 
> **FUSE** exposes `/rinzler/stats/devices/<bdf>/allocator/*` (byte metrics scaled by `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE`); shadow builds add write `dump_profile_trigger` / read `dump_profile_output`. **`rinzler` / `runtron`** call `pos_devices_register_fuse_stats()` before stats start.
> 
> **Driver** paths `alloc_kv_weights` / `alloc_hardware_weights` always record return addresses for OOM logs; shadow builds also `dump_profile` on failure. A sysfs test confirms **read callbacks** can return strings larger than stored-value limits.
>

body:
## Summary

Long-pole implementation drop for the GoF/Shard merge from `hwattention_sync`, re-cut from the current source-of-truth tip so that Alexey + CursorBot review feedback already lives in-tree (via #2795, which merged into `hwattention_sync` first). **Supersedes #2695**, which was based on an older `hwattention_sync` snapshot.

Lands `src/tron/gof.cpp` (shard ctor/dtor + `xfer_gof`, `gof::populate`, `k/v_hwcacheblock::xfer`) plus the pos-side
infrastructure it depends on. 23 files, organised in three layers matched to the three commits in this branch:

- **Commit 1 — `h/` infrastructure** (7 files): `h/libpos.hpp`,  `h/pos/config.hpp`, `h/pos/device.hpp`, `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`, `h/pos/hwattention.hpp`, new `h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp`, and a small `h/tron/gof.hpp` update (`dma_tracker` fwd decl, `POS_PER_PAGE` rename, `backfill_shard` signature). Extends `hw_attn_params` (`pre_attn_scalar`, `hw_layers` as `mask_t<128>` per Alexey's feedback in #2795), introduces `dma_xfer_state`, virtualises
  `xfer`/`xfer_blocking`/`isdone`/`wait` on cacheblocks, and adds the per-model `dma_tracker` (renamed from the original
  `device_dma_tracker` on hwa).
- **Commit 2 — `src/` implementation** (11 files): new `src/tron/gof.cpp` and `src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp`; updates to
  `src/pos/{hwattention,driver,device,dma,dma_queue,fake}.cpp` matching the header changes; 1-line CMake add for `gof.cpp`; `src/pos/CMakeLists.txt` adds `dma_tracker.cpp` to both `pos` and `pos_fake`. Also folds in the DEBUG_BARS sibling fix in `src/pos/vfio.cpp` (same `#ifdef` -> `#if` pattern Bill applied to `DEBUG_INIT` in #2695).
- **Commit 3 — Tests** (5 files): new `t/t_gof_dma.cpp` (FPGA round trip) and host-runnable `t/t_dma_tracker.cpp`; `t/t_dma.cpp` and `t/t_mwaitx.cpp` get structured-binding updates for the new 5-field `dma_xfer_state` returned from `xfer_blocks`; `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers the two new tests.

## Stub note

**`gof::backfill_shard` is intentionally a no-op in this PR** (parameters commented out, `TODO` comment). The full implementation walks the scheduler tree via `node_base::tree_parent` / `tree_height` /
`tree_edge_gals` — APIs added by the separate token-tree edge-state patch (PR 9 in the merge plan). No caller in this PR's scope reaches `backfill_shard` (its only invoker lives in the scheduler reshape that depends on those `node_base` virtuals which don't exist on main yet). The 3-arg declaration in `h/tron/gof.hpp` matches.

## What changed vs #2695

This PR is functionally equivalent to #2695 plus the feedback that landed via #2795 in `hwattention_sync`:

- `find_matched_range` end-of-array `last` bug fix (CursorBot).
- `tok_ix` -> `kv_tok_pos` parameter rename + comment on `fill_attn_job_template` (axch).
- `MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN` doc comment reworded to "0-based token position in its sequence" (axch).
- `hw_attn_params::hw_layers` migrated from `std::vector<bool>` to `tron::mask_t<128>` with the empty-mask semantic corrected so a default-constructed mask means "no HW anywhere" rather than the inverted "all HW" (axch).
- `device_dma_tracker` -> `dma_tracker` (renamed on hwa during the same period; per-model instead of singleton).

## Production-path tweaks (intentional, HW-team confirmed)

This is sidecar work in the sense that no new logic activates on main (nothing here calls `gof.cpp`), with three deliberate
production-path changes carried forward from #2695:

- `default_mm_cmd_fifo_depth` 32 -> 1024 (HW-team-confirmed correct value; 32 was a conservative debug default).
- `DmaQueue` producer mutex + wrap-count tracking — closes a race that was latent on main; makes `find_matched_range` debug dumps actually correct.
- `vhbm_map` virtual HBM mapping + `hbm_north/south_offset += bar4_offset` fix in `src/pos/device.cpp`.

## Debug-flag scrub

- `src/pos/device.cpp` continues to carry the `#define X 0` + `#if X` guards for `DEBUG_INIT` / `DEBUG_RESETS` / `DEBUG_VFIO` introduced by #2695.
- `src/pos/vfio.cpp` `DEBUG_BARS` converted to the same pattern. Previously `#define DEBUG_BARS 0` followed by `#ifdef DEBUG_BARS`, i.e. always-on regardless of value.

## File-level port decisions

Eight `h/` + `src/` files were ported at file level from the source branch rather than merged surgically:

- `h/libpos.hpp` — `hw_attn_params` extension touches struct layout pervasively; piecemeal merge fragile.
- `h/pos/device.hpp` — `wqentry` extensions + `dma_xfer_state` struct + several constants intertwined.

`h/pos/config.hpp`, `h/tron/gof.hpp`, and the rest of the `src/pos/*.cpp` are surgical (constants + small interface updates).

> **Attention job and model contract** — `hw_attn_params` gains `pre_attn_scalar`, a per-layer **`hw_layers`** bitmap (`mask_t<128>`: unset = SW-only), and documented split between model `kv_head_size` and bitfile **`HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`**. `fill_attn_job_template` now takes per-batch **`kv_tok_pos`**, **`shard_layer_t`** HBM bases, and binds a device; work requests carry **`tok_ix_per_b`**, shards, and **`in_flight`**. The global **`hwkv_rings`** / `save_k_to_hardware` entry points are removed in favor of virtual **`k`/`v_hwcacheblock::xfer`** (and blocking variants) with padded K/V shuffles when head sizes differ.
> 
> **DMA completion** — Transfers return **`dma_xfer_state`** (queue, end descriptor, wrap count, optional readback) instead of descriptor pairs. **`DmaQueue`** tracks ring wraps, serializes multi-descriptor submits with **`producer_mutex`**, and completes via **`check_xfer_complete`**. **`dma_tracker`** is per-model (priority queues per device, `await_layer`, `clear_all_dma_trackers` on **`pos_shutdown`**); **`free_kv_weights`** is added. **`xfer_blocks`** / **`wait_for_xfer_blocks`** gain readback verification and richer timeout dumps.
> 
> **Device / config** — Command FIFO depth default **1024**, **`attn_supported`** from caps, **`vhbm_map`** for KV readback, and HBM BAR offset fixes. KV layout constants move to **`pos/config.hpp`**; tests add **`t_gof_dma`** (FPGA) and **`t_dma_tracker`** (fake).
> 
> **`backfill_shard`** remains an intentional no-op until token-tree **`node_base`** APIs exist; no production caller depends on it in this drop.

## Summary

Wave-2 gatekeeper slice from `hwattention_sync`: token-tree edge state for the
hardware-attention scheduler. Adds the per-edge GoF/shard ownership fields, the
`node_base` shard/gal virtuals, and supporting caches — **all inert on `main`
today** (nothing populates `gals`/`shards` until the walker lands). Also folds in
the #2820 DMA bug fixes and a small scheduler-trace enrichment.

## What's in here

**Gatekeeper (`h/tron/scheduler`)**
- `token_tree.hpp` — `parent_edge` gains `gals` / `shards` / `dirty` / `handle_ids`
  fields, a per-edge append cache, and an `edge_shard` cache. The old stub
  `shards()` becomes `edge_shards()` with a real implementation. `split_edge_at` /
  `coalesce_nodes` propagate the new fields across topology changes; `seq_tip`
  gains a `handle_id` stamp.
- `full.hpp` — surgical: `node_base` gains `tree_parent` / `tree_height` /
  `tree_is_root` helpers plus three pure virtuals (`find_shard`, `add_shard`,
  `tree_edge_gals`), with concrete overrides on `node<book>`. The one existing
  call site renames `edge.shards()` → `edge.edge_shards()` (same behavior — empty
  span until the walker populates).

**Folded in — #2820 backport** (`h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`, `src/pos/driver.cpp`,
`t/t_dma.cpp`)
- DMA wrap false-completion fix (STORY-471): `xfer_blocks` stamps
  `dma_xfer_state.end_wrap_count` with the producer wrap (`DmaQueue` gains
  `producer_wrap_count`) rather than the consumer wrap captured at enqueue.
- Weight-TX bounds split (STORY-472): KV TX checks the KV region, weight TX checks
  the weight region; each assert stamps fetcher + computed end.
- `t_dma` regression test for the wrap-count semantics.

**Other**
- `h/tron/models/model.hpp` — the `"forward"` scheduler TRACE_EVENT also carries
  `n_tokens` alongside `n_token_jobs`, matching hwa.
- `t/t_token_cache.cpp` — `<algorithm>` include hygiene.
- `doc/` — new `hw-kv-token-tree.md` design doc, `token_tree_v2.md` refresh, 11
  figure images.

## Inert-on-main notes

Two spots carry a `TODO Remove ... when the PR 10 walker (GoF/Shard lifecycle)
lands`:
- `split_edge_at` documents the invariant that the walker (not the split) owns
  saving/partitioning `gals`/`shards`; `dirty=true` forces rebuild.
- `node<book>::add_shard` adds a defensive `edge_shard` cache invalidation so the
  API is locally correct without the walker. This diverges from hwa by one line —
  drops out with PR 10 or gets mirrored to hwa.

## Dependencies

Builds on already-merged #2676 (shard headers), #2693 (KV completion counters),
#2796 (shard ctor/dtor + `dma_xfer_state`), #2694 (ranged_mask real shard type).

## Test plan

- `make build` clean (205/205 targets).
- `t_dma` (458311 assertions), `t_token_cache` (74), `t_ranged_mask` (243),
