Not a real bug. The suggested fix wouldn't even help.

  - Failure mode is a safe false-negative. As CursorBot itself states, the worst case is a transient "not done yet" when it's actually done — the caller polls again and it resolves. The dangerous direction (false-positive → premature buffer reuse) is exactly what STORY-471 / #2820 fixed, and that path is unaffected.
  - The mutex doesn't protect consumed_head anyway. consumed_head is FPGA-written mmap'd device memory; the FPGA is not a producer_mutex participant. producer_mutex guards producer-side state (qtail / producer_wrap_count). Reading consumed_head "under" the lock — CursorBot's implied fix — buys nothing, because the external writer never takes the lock. Reading lock-free device memory and tolerating a self-correcting stale observation is the intended design.
  - Verbatim from hwa, and this is precisely the STORY-471 region that got dedicated work + a regression test.

  → Recommendation: no change. Safe-by-design.

I've added a to-do to follow up on this later, but for now this is Claude's evaluation:
```
  CursorBot is technically correct: the returned span points into a thread_local buffer shared across all parent_edge instances, so two live edge_shards() results would alias. But:

  - Doubly inert in PR 9. edge_shards() has the guard if (shards.empty()) return {}; at the top, and nothing in this PR populates shards. So the thread-local path is never even reached on main — it returns {} early every time.
  - Single call site, vetted in hwa. The lone caller (compute_forward_args) iterates immediately; the in-code comment already documents the "no aliasing" contract. This is the same function flagged as Concern #2 in pr9_quality.md (CursorBot's aliasing angle, my alignment angle — same thread_local std::vector<std::byte> pattern).
  - The activation risk is PR 10's. The walker is what populates shards and could introduce additional/nested call sites. The robust fix (make edge_shard_info hold a pointer instead of a reference → use std::vector<edge_shard_info>) changes a type in ranged_mask.hpp and should land in hwa first to avoid divergence.
```

title: h/runtron, perfetto: stream_generate phased-tracing + token-timing instrumentation
body:
## Summary

Ports the accumulated `stream_generate` tracing/logging instrumentation from
`hwattention_sync`, plus the matching `tronperf` `--help` text and a
`README.perfetto.md` note. Completely orthogonal to the GoF/shard merge stack —
depends on nothing in it.

## What's in here

- **`TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN=N`** (env-gated phased tracing): with `--trace-gen`,
  defers phase 2 (start tracing) until the total token position (prompt +
  generated) reaches `N`. Default `0`/unset preserves the original behavior
  (trace from prompt-parse completion). Lets long-context captures keep the ring
  buffer on steady state instead of warm-up.
- **`LOG_TOKEN_SELECTION` / `LOG_TOKEN_TIMES`** debug macros — `#ifdef`-guarded,
  commented out by default, inert unless explicitly defined.
- **`perfetto/tronperf`** — `--help` documents `TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN`.
- **`README.perfetto.md`** — user-facing docs for the same var.

## Behavior change (benign — calling out)

Per-token timing source switches from `std::chrono::clock::now()` to
`tron::hardware::system::tsc_in_ns()`. This changes `state::token_start`
(`clock::time_point` → `uint64_t`) and the `report_token` signature; both call
sites are self-contained within this file. Affects **logged timing values only**,
not generation results. `tsc_in_ns()` already exists on `main`
(`h/system/system.hpp`).

## Test plan

- `make build` clean (363/363 targets); `runtron` links.
- `t_stream_generate_race` passes.
- New includes (`<cstdlib>`, `system/system.hpp`,
  `tron/models/hw_attn_config.hpp`) all already available on `main`.

Originally authored by: Mike Cherba, Wado-posi

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes affect tracing start timing and log timing only; generation and sampling paths are unchanged aside from observability gates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN`** so phased Perfetto runs (`--trace-gen`) can delay **phase 2** (start tracing) until **prompt + generated** token count reaches `N`, instead of always starting at parse complete. Parse-complete and per-token callbacks both gate `perfetto_phase.start_phase(2)` on that threshold; unset/`0` keeps prior behavior. **`README.perfetto.md`** and **`perfetto/tronperf`** document the env var.
> 
> In **`stream_generate.hpp`**, per-token progress timing switches from `std::chrono` to **`tron::hardware::system::tsc_in_ns()`** (`token_start` is now TSC nanoseconds)—**logged timings only**, not generation. Optional **`LOG_TOKEN_SELECTION`** / **`LOG_TOKEN_TIMES`** compile-time hooks remain off by default.

title: Serialize hugepages tests with RESOURCE_LOCK to prevent lock contention
body:
The 6 hugepages-labelled tests (t_bf16, t_permutation, t_safetensors,
t_pos_lifecycle, t_heap, t_alloc) share one exclusive flock on
/dev/hugepages/libpos but carry no RESOURCE_LOCK. The host CI job runs
`ctest -LE fpga -j`, so they execute in parallel and collide on that lock:

    INIT: Allocating 16 hugepages from /dev/hugepages/libpos* on numa ALL
    [error] Failed to acquire lock after 8 attempts

This surfaced on #2832 but is a latent race affecting any branch — purely a
function of CI scheduling, not the PR diff.

This adds `RESOURCE_LOCK hugepages_lock` to all 6 tests so ctest serializes
them, mirroring the existing `RESOURCE_LOCK fpga` pattern.

Originally authored by @jwiegley (f90c80934), where it has been stranded
inside the still-open Cachix CI-migration PR #2198; extracted here as a
standalone fix for main. Unblocks #2832.

Note: once this lands, #2198 will conflict on these 6 lines — drop its copy
of f90c80934 on rebase.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CMake-only test properties; no application code, auth, or data paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`RESOURCE_LOCK hugepages_lock`** to six tests that allocate from `/dev/hugepages/libpos` so **CTest** serializes them under parallel runs (`ctest -j`), matching the existing **`RESOURCE_LOCK fpga`** pattern.
> 
> **Catch2** tests updated via `add_catch_test`: `t_bf16`, `t_permutation`, `t_safetensors`, `t_pos_lifecycle`. **`t_heap`** and **`t_alloc`** get the same lock on their `set_tests_properties` lines. No production or runtime behavior changes—only test scheduling to avoid flock contention failures in CI.

title: Planning layer: iterative walker + HW-attention model state
body:
## Planning layer: iterative walker + HW-attention model state

Ports the GoF/shard **planning layer** from `hwattention_sync`: the recursive→iterative
scheduler rewrite (golden-gof-shard descent/ascent) together with the model-side
HW-attention state it drives.

This is a re-slice of the original plan. The walker (`full.hpp`) and the model HW-attention
state (`model.hpp`/`self_attention.hpp`/`common.hpp`) are **one inseparable feature** — the
walker reads model state and `model::forward` consumes what the walker produces (bidirectional),
so neither half compiles without the other. The boundary that *does* hold is **planning layer**
(this PR: scheduler + model headers) vs **execution layer** (next PR: `src/pos` device runtime).

### Inert on `main`
HW attention is **off by default** (`hw_attn_config.hpp`'s `USE_HW_ATTN` gate;
`fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` → false), so `hw_attn_eligible` stays false and every HW-attn block in
the walker is skipped. The only always-on change is the recursive→iterative tree-walk refactor,
which is behavior-preserving. No build-infra change; no CI label needed.

### Commits
1. **Code** — `full.hpp` (walker), `full.cpp`/`generation.cpp` (handle_id propagation),
   `model.hpp`/`self_attention.hpp`/`common.hpp`/`llama.hpp` (HW-attn state, `construct_hw_plan`,
   `prepare`/`launch_hw_attention`), `token_tree.hpp` (drop obsolete PR-9 note).
2. **Docs + tests** — 5 new HW-KV design docs (`attention-scheduling`, `hw-kv-sched`,
   `hw-kv-sched-detailed`, `hw-kv-examples`, `hw-kv-design`) + 2 relocated `golden-*` docs + the
   `doc/images/` figures they reference + `doc/tree-vis/` (Python tooling that generates the
   figures); `t_phase1_integration` and `t_phase2_integration`.

### Reviewing aid
`full.hpp` is the big bite. It interleaves two things in the same functions: (a) the
recursive→iterative conversion (a no-op refactor) and (b) the GoF/shard descent/ascent semantics.
They don't separate cleanly into commits, but reading them as two passes helps.

### Verification
`make build` + `make lint` clean; ported code byte-identical to source. `t_phase1_integration`,
`t_phase2_integration`, `t_scheduler`, `t_token_cache`, `t_generate_2/3`, `t_generate_host_2` pass;
`t_generate` 7/7 incl. FPGA determinism — confirms the layer is inert on `main`.
```
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 83

Label Time Summary:
fake            = 254.48 sec*proc (40 tests)
fpga            = 439.32 sec*proc (20 tests)
hugepages       =  12.95 sec*proc (6 tests)
main            =   0.47 sec*proc (1 test)
min_slices_2    = 140.48 sec*proc (2 tests)

Total Test time (real) = 751.65 sec

The following tests did not run:
         43 - t_alloc_contention (Disabled)
         82 - t_slamtest (Disabled)
```

Depends on PR 6c (gof.cpp / dma_tracker), PR 7, PR 8, PR 9. The device execution layer (and the
default-on gate flip) follow in the next PR.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large cross-cutting scheduler/model changes and async GOF DMA when HW is enabled; mitigated by default-off gate and behavior-preserving SW path, but the iterative walker refactor still warrants careful review.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR lands the **planning layer** for hybrid FPGA/CPU attention: extensive design docs (walker flattening, GOF/shard lifecycle, ranged SW/HW masks, join phase) plus **`doc/tree-vis/`** tooling to generate radix-tree figures for those docs.
> 
> On the code side, **`model.hpp` / `common.hpp`** wire scheduler output into the forward pass: per-batch **`hw_workload`** (`hw_pass`es over device shards and queries), **`construct_hw_plan`** built from **`hw_plan_entries`**, and SW attention planning that respects **`ranged_mask`** (`sw_required` / `visible`) instead of treating all KV pages as software work. KV **`save_k` / `save_v`** now drive **GOF completion** (`save_count` → **`gof_rodeo`**) to populate GOFs and enqueue shard DMA via an optional per-model **`dma_tracker`**. Legacy **`hw_kv_section`** / HW-validation SW sections are removed. HW attention stays **off unless `USE_HW_ATTN=1`** and eligible devices exist; the paired scheduler walker rewrite (iterative descent/ascent for GoF/shard planning) is described in the PR but is the other half of the same feature boundary.
> 
> **Risk:** Medium while gated—touches scheduling/model contracts and async GOF DMA when enabled; default path should remain SW-only behavior-preserving aside from the walker refactor noted in the PR description.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 475acd3c0d7bb64164f0b0e5e6ed3cb03e4e556c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

Real concern, but it's inert in this PR — the flagged line isn't reachable here. This is the planning layer; hardware attention is gated off on main and the HW plan is never populated:
  
  1. fwd_hw_attn_enabled() defaults to false (no USE_HW_ATTN), so full::forward() passes an empty hw_plan_entries span and construct_hw_plan returns at the hw_plan_entries.empty() check.
  2. Independently, build_edge_ranges only emits an hw_plan_entry at a shard boundary, and nothing pushes onto the shard_stack yet (see ranged_mask.hpp: "Since shards are always empty today, only query events fire"). So hw_plan is empty regardless of the gate.

  So pass.hw_tok_ix = entry.last_token_ix.i is dead code in this PR and can't affect generation.
  
  I did create a story/bug [STORY-507](https://app.notion.com/p/positron-ai/HW-attention-hw_tok_ix-uses-batch-relative-coords-but-consumer-treats-it-as-absolute-372d132d3cfd815eb881e83010bd2b47) for follow-up, incase there is a real issue here.

author: Wado-posi

title: Resolve corrupted work_req assertion in TP2
body:
In TP2 or higher, it is possible for a work_req to be reused too soon. When the issue occurs, the following log messages are logged:

```
[error] TRON_ASSERT(other_sp.m_star != -std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()): Encountered -inf m_star in a valid scratchpad. KV_head 5, to worker 0, from worker 11, batch_job_ix 6
```

Currently, this problem is quiescent with the original heap implementation, but when `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`, the defect is reproduced very quickly in soak tests.

The fix is to make sure the previous work request is finished before reusing to begin a new prepare.
- Add wait_until_work_req_idle()
- Wait for previous launch of a work_req to complete before mutating

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes synchronization on the hot path for hardware matmul/attention scheduling; incorrect ordering could stall or mis-handle in-flight work, but the fix uses an existing atomic guard already set at enqueue and cleared on completion.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **TP2+ race** where plugins reuse the same `wqentry` / `hardware_job` launcher while matmul/attention launches are still asynchronous: the main thread could **fill or prepare** the next job before TX/RX workers finished reading the prior entry, leading to corrupted `work_req` state (especially visible with `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`).
> 
> Adds **`wait_until_work_req_idle`**, which spins on `wqentry::in_flight` with **acquire** loads until the prior job’s completion callback clears it with **release** (set at enqueue, cleared after the job completes). That wait runs at the start of **matmul/attention fill**, **matmul prepare**, and **attention prepare** so fields are not mutated while a launch is still in flight. Documents the protocol in **Note [WQEntry Reuse Race]** and ties the existing enqueue `in_flight` store to that note.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ac19c45de1a1e1e19d08a9603d3debe89a0c06af. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

wade.body:
I have some reservations about this... I literally went down this road a couple weeks ago or so, and almost committed the same spin-wait you've added. But I loathe spin-waits, and we backed it out for a couple reasons (which I let Claude summarize for me below):

---
1. It turns a loud tripwire into a silent forever-hang.

"When RX is stuck (which is the symptom here), the callback that clears in_flight never fires; the next hw_prepare for that wqentry will spin forever instead of failing loudly… The original assert was a useful tripwire — restoring it would surface the real first violation faster."

The spin only "works" when the completion path is healthy — which is exactly when you don't need it. When it isn't healthy (the arena-allocator soak case), it converts a diagnosable assert into a hang.

2. The serialization it adds already exists. We worked out that main relies implicitly on the rxinfo_ring overflow backpressure at the top of hw_prepare:

"in_flight is cleared before rx_head increments, so per-slot backpressure transitively guarantees per-wqentry backpressure as well. So main never trips the same condition. The assertion exists for a case main physically can't hit: hwattn introduced multi-device matmul dispatch [the same wqentry re-targeted to a different device]."

---

I did fix some wrap-count bugs with https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/commit/9e4ebd056e080ecf464e6d4d8dfc9083f1fa732f awhile back.

I suppose we can land this if it's critical to get the test pipeline moving forward. But spin-waits just suck in general, IMO. I wonder... is "m_star == -inf" really even a "reused too soon" bug? It's on matmul_rx_q (raw desc_idx polling, no check_xfer_complete). If this is an unserialized upstream issue, or false-completion feeding a stale scratchpad, the fix should be to serialize/correct that signal... not wait indefinitely/blindly on 'in_flight' IMO. Just feel like there's more sleuthing to be done ;-p

author: bham0n

title: Make token-tree `used` pin-derived; fix used-set leak and lost-wakeup hang
body:
## Summary

An alternative fix to the token-tree lifecycle bugs Alexey's stress test exposes
(#2862 coalescence, #2863 `used`-set, #2864 hang), stacked on `axch-verify-used`
with the three invariant checks cherry-picked in so it validates against the
strongest workload (100 waves, all asserts on).

**Re-diagnosis of #2864:** it is **not** a stack overflow — reproduced and
captured all-thread backtraces showing a **lost-wakeup deadlock** (test thread on
the wave latch, scheduler worker asleep on an empty queue). It is the *same*
defect as the #2863 `used`-set undercount: a wrongly-cleared `used` ancestor of a
live request makes `compute_forward_args` prune the subtree, the listener never
fires, the pipeline drains, the worker sleeps. (Full write-up:
`for_claude/token-tree-new-approaches.md`.)

## Approach: pin-derived `used`

- `used()` is now an inline accessor derived from a per-node `pins_below` counter,
  not an incrementally-maintained flag. Pins come from (1) client `seq_tip`s and
  (2) pending listeners. This makes the used-set **exact by construction** and
  guarantees a subtree with in-flight work is never pruned — killing the hang.
- Drop `mark_used`/`mark_unused`/`check_usage` and all ad-hoc `used = true` growth
  writes (the source of the leak).
- `seq_tip::set_node` funnels pin/unpin (release on the worker); split seeds the
  intermediate's pins; coalesce transfers them; release follows tombstones.
- #2862: coalesce idle single-child intermediates on release (detected via
  `pins_below == child->pins_below`); relax the invariant for directly-pinned
  single-child nodes (which legitimately cannot coalesce until released).
- `verify_used_set` additionally asserts no pending listener survives at
  quiescence.

## Validation

- `t_token_tree_stress` (100 waves, all three invariants): 20/20 runs green,
  "All tests passed (303 assertions)". ~70x faster than baseline (the slowness was
  used-leak-driven traversal growth).
- `t_token_cache`: pass (74 assertions / 8 cases).
- `t_stream_generate_race`: 2/2 on FPGA.
- `make format`, `make lint` clean.

## Relationship to #2871

Targets the same root cause as Wade's #2871 (which is directionally right);
differs by deriving `used` from a single subtree pin counter (exact, no
boolean-closure recomputation) and pinning in-flight listeners directly.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core scheduler token-tree lifecycle, pinning, coalescing, and forward traversal invariants; bugs could strand requests or corrupt eviction/used-set behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the token tree’s incrementally maintained **`used` boolean** with **`used()` derived from `subtree_pins`**, counting client **`seq_tip` holds** and **pending listeners** (pinned on extend, unpinned when notifications fire). **`mark_used` / `mark_unused` / `check_usage`** and ad-hoc `used = true` on reuse/split/create are removed so the live set matches pins by construction and **`compute_forward_args` no longer skips subtrees that still owe in-flight work** (lost-wakeup hang).
> 
> **`seq_tip::set_node`** is the single funnel for tip repoints (pin new, worker release/unpin old); **`release_node`** follows tombstones, unpins, and may **`coalesce_if_unpinned_single_child`**. Coalesce/split transfer pin counts; **`coalesce_nodes`** refuses parents with listeners and merges **`subtree_pins`** onto the survivor. **`verify_tree` / `verify_used_set`** gain listener and deferred-coalesce checks; stress tests bump waves and assert used-set per wave. **`stream_generate`** uses **`unpin_node`** when clearing an eagle speculator without enqueueing release.
>

author: Wado-posi

title: Free and repopulate GOF staging buffers after DMA completion (Story 2814)
body:
Treat each gof's two 8 KB hwcacheblock staging buffers (k.data/v.data) as a reconstructable cache: free them once every in-flight DMA that reads them has completed, and rebuild on demand (reacquire + rebuild position tables + repopulate from the host KV pages) when a later submission needs the GOF. The durable copies remain the host books and device HBM, so the free is a cache eviction -- GOF identity (gal.gofs[layer], gof_job refs, shard state) is unchanged. See Note [GOF staging eviction].

Interface / behavior:
- gof: add dma_inflight (atomic) + staging_mutex, prepare_for_dma() (reacquire + populate + reserve a credit under the mutex before xfer_gof), free_staging_if_idle() (frees both buffers once dma_inflight hits 0), and the inflight_guard RAII credit (commit() after xfer_gof keeps it).
- hwcacheblock: alloc_buffer/release_buffer/clear/is_allocated; k/v gain non-virtual rebuild_positions()/reacquire_buffer() (no new pos virtuals).
- pending_xfer: add pinned_gof (shared_ptr<gof>) pinning staging for the life of its in-flight DMA and serving as the dma_inflight decrement target.
- dma_tracker::push() is now noexcept (a post-submit failure terminates rather than unwinding into a free-under-DMA); poll_completions decrements and frees outside dma_tracker::mu to avoid a staging_mutex<->mu lock-order inversion.
- Submission sites gof_rodeo_impl and backfill_shard route through prepare_for_dma / commit / push.

Tests:
- t_dma_tracker (pos_fake): staging lifecycle, inflight_guard, poll-frees-after- last, clear-drops-pin, prepare/free allocation-neutrality.
- t_gof_dma (FPGA): free -> reacquire -> fill -> xfer -> readback; and prepare_for_dma reacquire/populate/credit.
- t_gof_staging_leaks (FPGA, new): real DMA-heap allocation-balance leak suite across submit/track/complete/free + multi-device fanout.

Validated: make build-test clean; t_dma_tracker 33/1718; t_gof_dma and t_gof_staging_leaks pass on FPGA (slice-scoped); make format + lint clean.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes DMA staging lifetime, concurrent free vs submit paths, and lock ordering; bugs could use-after-free staging under live DMA or corrupt GOF state.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Story 2814** treats each GOF’s two 8 KB `hwcacheblock` staging buffers as a **reconstructable cache**: after HBM DMA completes, `dma_tracker::poll_completions` can evict them via `gof::free_staging_if_idle`; the next transfer uses `prepare_for_dma` to reallocate, rebuild `positions` tables, and repopulate from host KV pages.
> 
> The lifecycle is guarded by **`dma_inflight`**, **`staging_mutex`**, and **`inflight_guard`**: credit is reserved before `xfer_gof`, **`commit()`** after descriptors are live, and **`pending_xfer::pinned_gof`** keeps the GOF (and staging) alive until completion decrements the last credit. **`dma_tracker::push` is `noexcept`** so post-submit failures terminate instead of freeing staging under active DMA; staging frees run **outside** the tracker mutex to avoid lock inversion with `staging_mutex`.
> 
> **`gof_rodeo_impl`** and **`backfill_shard`** share this path. **`clear()`** remains an abandon-only shutdown hook and does not treat queue drain as completion.
> 
> Tests cover fake lifecycle (`t_dma_tracker`), FPGA round-trip/reacquire (`t_gof_dma`), and a new FPGA leak suite (`t_gof_staging_leaks`).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 576843b189e9803f0fc48fc4483ff7a62012a461. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: Move inwork queue from CKSTAILQ to new minfifo implementation
body:
Add minfifo, a minimal Vyukov style Multi Producer Single Consumer Fifo queue and move from  using the CKSTAILQ to it for enqueueiung to devices

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the hot path between app threads and TX workers; correctness depends on minfifo memory ordering and queue-full handling, though new tests cover MPSC behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the per-device **in-work** path from a **mutex-protected Concurrency Kit STAILQ** to a new **`tron::minfifo`** lock-free **multi-producer / single-consumer** ring (2048 slots via `inwork_ring_size`).
> 
> **Enqueue** (`enqueue_hardware_matmul_job_to_device`) no longer takes `inwork_mutex`; it atomically updates `enqueued_work` / `work_req_count` and pushes `wqentry*` into `inwork_queue`, **asserting** on overflow instead of an unbounded list.
> 
> The **TX worker** dequeues with `dequeue()` and blocks on **`mwaitx`** using `dequeue_wait_hint()` on the next cell’s sequence word, rather than watching the STAILQ head pointer.
> 
> Related tuning: **`max_cmd_fifo_depth`** is raised from **32 → 1024** (aligned with HW), and several device counters (`enqueued_work`, `dequeued_work`, `work_req_count`) are **`std::atomic`**. **`mwaitx`** gets a corrected minimum timeout so short waits don’t jump to multi-ms sleeps. **`t_minfifo`** adds concurrency and capacity tests; `minfifo` is linked into **`pos`** and **`pos_fake`**.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b8739108f7af86a1a2bffc1e7873e3f2eabf8006. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

```suggestion

```

don't mention 'Story' numbers in comments...
we don't really need this comment IMO... and this Perfetto trace event really isn't related to `Note [GOF staging eviction]` directly. It's a useful event no matter the context
minor nit: `public` is redundant in a struct (members are public by default)

I can't help it lol... I'm always concerned with performance. So I asked Claude to summarize my concern (cuz it often words things better than I can):

> **Eviction is unconditional on every completion** — rebuild thrashing risk. free_staging_if_idle frees whenever dma_inflight reaches 0, and populate (the swizzle) is the bulk of the rebuild cost. For the prefill→HBM offload pattern this is a clear win (staging genuinely isn't needed again). But for any pattern that re-DMAs the same GOF in quick succession (multi-shard backfill fanout, speculation), you now pay a full free + reacquire + reswizzle each time, with no hysteresis.

Maybe it won't materialize, but after this lands in `main` we might find combinations where this has a larger impact than what we speculated. So just seems worth keeping in mind in case we need to optimize it a bit later.

title: Cache cpu_frequency_hz reciprocals for cycles_to_ns / ns_to_cycles
body:
## Summary
- Replace the two 64-bit divides in `precise_scale` with a 64x64→128 multiply + shift (one `mulq` on x86_64) — `cycles_to_ns` / `ns_to_cycles` drop from ~30–50 cycles to ~5.
- The TSC calibration thread caches fixed-point reciprocals of `cpu_frequency_hz` alongside it and refreshes them on every freq update; writes are ordered reciprocal-then-frequency so a reader past the existing `!= 0` gate observes a valid pair.
- `ns_per_cycle` stored in Q.64 (all fractional — ns-per-cycle < 1 for any freq > 1 GHz). `cycles_per_ns` stored in Q.61, reserving 3 integer bits for the small cycles-per-ns rate (covers up to ~8 GHz; realistic x86_64 invariant TSC is 2–4 GHz). Round-to-nearest at both reciprocal computation and the final shift preserves the strict round-trip behavior the existing precision tests rely on.

## Test plan
- [x] `make t_system` — all 12 cases pass, including the strict round-trip at `ns = 1e10` and the precision sweep from 1 µs to `cycles_to_ns(UINT64_MAX - 1000)` (error is 0 ns for all realistic scales, 1 ns at the UINT64_MAX edge vs. the 1000 ns tolerance).
- [x] `make t_mwaitx` — passes (heavy `ns_to_cycles` user).
- [x] `make lint`.
- [ ] Confirm on a non-AMD host (Intel Xeon) that calibration converges and conversions stay accurate.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core timestamp math used widely via get_corrected_ns; ordering and rounding must stay correct, though tests and asserts mitigate regressions.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Speeds up hot-path TSC conversions** by caching `cpu_frequency_hz` reciprocals as Q3.61 fixed-point values and using `__uint128_t` multiply + round-shift in `cycles_to_ns` / `ns_to_cycles` instead of `precise_scale`’s 64-bit divides.
> 
> The TSC calibration thread recomputes those reciprocals on every frequency update via new `update_freq_reciprocals()` (with freq bounds asserts) and publishes them **before** writing `cpu_frequency_hz`, so readers past the existing `cpu_frequency_hz != 0` gate always see a consistent pair. Header documentation in **Note [Cycle Frequency Reciprocals]** explains the format and ordering; `precise_scale` is left in place for other callers (e.g. in-loop `new_freq` estimation).
>

author: mcherba

title: fix BS 'prompt_parsing' guard, allow batched-decode through HW path
body:
## Summary

Addresses Alexey's review feedback items 5 (`model.hpp`) and 10 (`full.hpp`), about the insufficient/inaccurate 'is_prompt_processing' guard.

Replaces the forward-level `is_prompt_processing` guard that disabled hardware attention for *any* multi-token batch with per-edge HW/SW routing. The old guard (`q_batch->items.size() > 1`) conflated two unrelated things: prompt
prefill (which genuinely must run in SW) and batched decode across multiple resident users (which is fine on HW). The practical consequence was that **as soon as a second user was resident, all attention fell back to SW** — batched
decode never took the HW path.

## What changed

**Per-edge HW eligibility — `model.hpp`, `construct_hw_plan`**
- Drop the `is_prompt_processing = (items.size() > 1)` early return.
- Skip HW for a plan entry only when it actually has more than one query (`queries.size() > 1`). A HW pass carries a single causal K-boundary shared by all of its queries, so it can only serve a single-query edge. See Note [HW Attention and multi-query edges].

**Scheduler mask reconciliation — `full.hpp`**
- Replace the forward-level "if `token_jobs.size() > 1`, move all HW work to SW and clear the plan" with per-edge folding: only queries on multi-query HW plan entries (`entry.query_mask.count() > 1`) are moved HW→SW, keeping `query_mask` consistent with `construct_hw_plan`, which skips exactly those entries. `hw_plan` is no longer cleared on mixed workloads.

**Effect — batched decode now runs on HW.** Independent single-query decode queries from different sequences each land in their own HW plan entry (each a single-query edge), so they stay HW-eligible. Prefill and speculative-decode
trees (multi-query edges) continue to run in SW. Previously the presence of any second token forced the entire forward to SW; this is the behavior change the title refers to.

## Testing

- runtron with 3, 4, 6 resident users runs cleanly with these changes. 



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core HW/SW attention routing and join correctness paths; behavior shifts for multi-user batched decode (intended HW enablement) while prefill/speculative multi-query edges remain SW-only.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes hardware attention being disabled whenever a forward had more than one token**, which wrongly treated batched decode from multiple resident users like prompt prefill and forced the whole pass to software attention.
> 
> **Per-edge HW eligibility** in `construct_hw_plan`: drops the `q_batch->items.size() > 1` early return and skips HW only when an `hw_plan_entry` has **more than one query** (`query_mask.count() > 1`)—prefill and speculative trees stay SW; independent single-query decode edges each get their own entry and remain HW-eligible. The same predicate is used at the **full edge** level (not just queries in the current minibatch) so scheduler folding and plan construction stay aligned when edges split across minibatches.
> 
> **Scheduler reconciliation** in `full.hpp`: instead of moving all HW work to SW and clearing `hw_plan` when `token_jobs.size() > 1`, it folds **only** queries on multi-query HW plan entries from HW→SW, with partial range updates when a range mixes prompt and decode queries. `hw_plan` is retained for mixed workloads.
> 
> **Attention join hardening** in `self_attention.hpp`: when merging HW pass results, **skip passes that do not include the current batch job** so unpack/join does not read never-DMA'd buffers; SW scratchpads are marked valid only when `m_star` has left `-inf`, reducing bad joins under multi-token batches with multiple users (symptom gate, with a TODO on root cause).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4f5c3da03f46e18d791b7f147d123e1b8f8a04d6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: mcherba

title: Weight load reuse stage 03
body:
First pass at opening up the APIs to enable Weight load reuse with HW attention.  Currently we end up with batches of 16, and the sooner we can get gof_rodeo out of the main thread and not blockign the better.  While a gof_rodeo only happens every 4 token positions in generation, during prompt parsing we see 32 of them per batch of 128 token positions at each layer, and it's taking about the same amount of time as the Actual attention work  and should be non-blocking.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Large changes to HW attention correctness, async KV DMA ordering, and multi-device synchronization; regressions could cause wrong attention results or stale HBM reads.
> 
> **Overview**
> Expands **hardware attention** toward weight-load reuse: multi-query passes are planned with **EMEM-aware** shard/query limits (`max_shards_for_emem`, `maximum_hwattn_batch_size`), per-query `last_hw_token_pos`, and multi-Q metadata via `tok_ix_per_b` instead of a single shared `tok_ix`.
> 
> **GOF KV offload** is reworked to be less blocking on the forward path. Completed GOFs are prepared with `prep_xfer` / `xfer_n_blocks`, then submitted either **locally** or through a **per-device `gof_xfer` manager queue** (`minfifo` + batch submit under `producer_mutex`). `dma_tracker` gains `push_batch`, **`await_layer` waits all devices**, and optional `await_all` for deterministic tests. Scheduler/model changes add **multi-binding `gof_jobs`** (shared-prefix sibling GOFs), prefix-based shard eligibility, async backfill task dispatch, and barriers (`wait_for_gof_xfer_submits`, cooperative drain).
> 
> **Prompt/prefill** can stay on HW for shared K/V boundaries (scheduler no longer forces multi-query edges entirely to SW); causal tails are reconciled into SW masks. HW launch ordering in ingest moves **`prepare/launch_hw_attention` before `save_k`/`save_v`** so attention overlaps persistence. **`USE_HW_ATTN` defaults on**; bitfile **WLR** capability is checked at device init.
>

author: hvaneenoo-positron

title: WLR Hw-Attention Stage 3
body:
## Summary

Stage 3 of hardware attention: extends the HW path from single-query decode to
**multi-query prompt parsing**, fenced by EMEM/metadata capacity, together with the
GOF DMA-transfer plumbing and ingest codegen that drive it. The development history
is consolidated into four reviewable blocks.

## High-level blocks

**1. GOF DMA transfer tracking & lock-contention refactor**
`shard.hpp`, `gof.*`, `dma_tracker.cpp`, `hwattention.hpp`, `driver.cpp`, `device.hpp`
Contiguous per-layer started/done DMA prefixes with out-of-order hole handling,
reservation rollback, watermark accounting, and SW-only-layer premarking so the done
prefix flows over layers that never DMA. Batches K/V block submission through a single
critical section (`xfer_n_blocks`) to cut lock contention, plus the supporting
`DmaQueue` descriptor plumbing.

**2. Multi-Q HW prompt parsing, EMEM-fenced**
`self_attention.hpp`, `model.hpp`, `worker.cpp`, `hw_attn_config.*`, `common.hpp`, scheduler
HW attention for prompt prefill with batched Qs (up to `MAX_B`) and multiple physical
subpasses when KV spans more shards than EMEM allows. `construct_hw_plan` builds
EMEM-safe passes and coalesces compatible prompt queries; the worker shares one K/V
load per batch and emits per-Q metadata per subpass; the scheduler stops blanket
HW→SW folding for multi-query edges and reconciles short queries / causal tails above
the HBM boundary. HW attention gated off for non-ingested models.

**3. Ingest codegen + C++ entry points**
`ingest/src/*.hs`, `model.hpp`
Emits `{Launch,Prepare}{Prompt,NonPrompt}HwAttention` statements from the ingest
pipeline so ingested models drive HW attention during prompt parsing, plus the C++
entry points they target (early-launch batch-size gate and prepare/launch forwarders).

**4. cursor[bot] review findings**
Hardens the metadata-ring batch budget (`MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS` + a `static_assert`
on ring capacity), gates `use_hw_attn_for_this_model` on EMEM capacity so models whose
head count exceeds EMEM fall back to SW consistently (with a correct disable-reason
log), fixes the `WARN_IF_METADATA_WRAPS` block so it compiles, removes leftover
commented-out debug scaffolding, and re-enables the golden generate tests that were

wade.body:
**Not reachable as filed — but we're hardening the fragility it points at.**

The "clash across prepares" can't actually exhaust the ring with the current
constants:

- `B` is capped at `MAX_B = 32`. `maximum_hwattn_batch_size` returns
  `min(metadata_entry_count/2 = 64, hw_max_b)`, and `hw_max_b = maximum_batch_size(...)`
  is hard-clamped to `MAX_B = 32`. So the `/2` metadata term never binds — the
  activation cap (32) is always tighter.
- `num_hw_subcmds ≤ 4` (asserted at worker.cpp:870; matched planner-side by
  `physical_subpasses ≤ max_hw_subpasses_per_pass = 4`).
- **Single pass:** `B * num_hw_subcmds ≤ 32 * 4 = 128` = `metadata_entry_count`
  exactly — the `num_metadata_wds ≤ 128` assert (worker.cpp:877) can't trip.
- **Cumulative across a layer's same-device passes:** each query lands in exactly
  one pass, and total device queries = minibatch `≤ MAX_B = 32` (TP replicates
  queries; shards split K/V, not the batch). So `Σ(Bᵢ · sᵢ) ≤ 32 * 4 = 128`. The
  prepare-all-then-launch-all `prepared_mdwd_owners` CAS can't fail either.

So `MAX_B * max_hw_subpasses_per_pass == metadata_entry_count` exactly — the ring is
correctly sized, just implicitly. The real defect is that this is an **undocumented
coincidence**: nothing enforces it, and the `/2` misrepresents the per-query cost.
Hardening (no runtime behavior change, since the returned cap is bit-identical):

- Budget `md_max_b = metadata_entry_count / MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS` (= 32) instead
  of `/2`, and hoist `MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS` to `tron::hardware` as the single
  source of truth.
- Add `static_assert(MAX_B * MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS <= metadata_entry_count)` so a
  future `MAX_B` or subpass-ceiling bump breaks the build instead of overflowing the
  ring at runtime.

**Correct that the `/2` is misleading, but it's not a live overflow — we're
hardening it into an enforced invariant.**

The `/2` term never actually binds: `maximum_hwattn_batch_size` returns
`min(metadata_entry_count/2 = 64, hw_max_b)`, and `hw_max_b = maximum_batch_size(...)`
is hard-clamped to `MAX_B = 32`. So `B ≤ 32` for every input, and the metadata cap of
64 is dead. With `num_hw_subcmds ≤ 4` (worker.cpp:870), worst-case metadata is
`B * num_hw_subcmds ≤ 32 * 4 = 128` = `metadata_entry_count` exactly — so neither the
`num_metadata_wds ≤ 128` assert (worker.cpp:877) nor the `prepared_mdwd_owners` CAS
can trip, even across a layer's same-device passes (total device queries = minibatch
`≤ MAX_B = 32`, so `Σ Bᵢ·sᵢ ≤ 128`).

The genuine problem is exactly what you flag — the budget *pretends* one word per Q
when the worker consumes up to `num_hw_subcmds`, and the ring only survives because
`MAX_B * max_hw_subpasses_per_pass` happens to equal 128. Fixing the representation
without changing behavior:

- `md_max_b = metadata_entry_count / MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS` (= 32) instead of `/2`.
  Runtime is bit-identical: `hw_max_b ≤ 32 ≤ 32`, so `min(md_max_b, hw_max_b)` is
  unchanged for every input.
- `static_assert(MAX_B * MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS <= metadata_entry_count)` so raising
  `MAX_B` (the stray `64` suggests that was once intended) or the subpass ceiling is a
  compile error rather than a silent ring overflow.

**Right that the cap doesn't model subpasses — but it can't overflow today; we're
making the invariant explicit.**

`construct_hw_plan` caps queries-per-pass at `maximum_hwattn_batch_size`, which is
`min(metadata_entry_count/2 = 64, hw_max_b)` with `hw_max_b` hard-clamped to
`MAX_B = 32`. So `B ≤ 32`. `physical_subpasses` is bounded by
`max_hw_subpasses_per_pass = 4` (asserted at self_attention.hpp:722; matched by the
worker's `num_hw_subcmds ≤ 4`). Worst case `B * physical_subpasses ≤ 32 * 4 = 128` =
`metadata_entry_count` exactly, so the ring can't overflow and the prepare-time assert
can't trip — including cumulatively, since total device queries = minibatch `≤ MAX_B`.

So the safety margin is real but *accidental*: `MAX_B * max_hw_subpasses_per_pass`
equals the ring size with nothing enforcing it, and the budget claims 1 word/query.
Hardening (provably no runtime change — the cap value is bit-identical):

- `md_max_b = metadata_entry_count / MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS` (= 32) rather than `/2`.
- `static_assert(MAX_B * MAX_HW_SUBPASSES_PER_PASS <= metadata_entry_count)` to catch
  any future bump at compile time instead of as a runtime ring overflow.

(Note: the planner's per-pass `physical_subpasses` already matches the worker's
`num_hw_subcmds` exactly — both are `ceil(covered_shards / max_shards_for_emem(...))`,
and `max_shards_for_emem` ignores head dim — so no per-pass divergence to account for.)

**Confirmed real — fixed.** Thanks, this one is a genuine silent-wrong-output bug
(just not reachable by any current model).

Root cause is an eligibility/plan inconsistency: `use_hw_attn_for_this_model()` is a
pure runtime flag, and the compile-time `model_shape_is_hwattn_eligible()` checks
`head_size ∈ {64,128}` and `n_kv_heads` but **not** `n_heads`. `max_shards_for_emem`
returns 0 exactly when `n_heads > 128`. So a head_size-128, small-`n_kv_heads`,
high-GQA model with `n_heads > 128` is eligible + flag-on → `configure_hw_attention`
sets the HW layer mask → descent marks HW ranges → `construct_hw_plan` hits
`physical_shards_per_pass == 0` and silently returns an empty plan. The SW path then
runs only `sw_required` for those HW-offloaded (non-sliding) layers, so the
HW-covered tokens are computed by neither path → wrong attention output.

Fix (h/tron/models/model.hpp):

- `use_hw_attn_for_this_model()` now returns `false` when
  `max_shards_for_emem(n_heads, head_size, shard_tokens) == 0`. That predicate is the
  single lever gating `configure_hw_attention`'s HW mask, so the whole model becomes
  SW-only consistently — the real fallback the old log line only promised.
- The now-unreachable `physical_shards_per_pass == 0` branch in `construct_hw_plan`
  becomes `TRON_ASSERT(physical_shards_per_pass > 0, …)` (always-on) instead of a
  silent `return`, so any future mask/plan inconsistency aborts loudly rather than
  zeroing output.

Provably inert for every current model (all have `n_heads ≤ 128`, so the guard is
false and the predicate is unchanged). Added a unit test locking the boundary the
gate keys on (`t/t_dma_tracker.cpp`, `[hwattn_emem]`): `max_shards_for_emem` ≥ 1 for
`n_heads ≤ 128` and == 0 for `n_heads > 128`, for both head sizes.

```
The out-of-range branch is a fallback for layers beyond the bitset's capacity (max_tracked_layers = 256). But it can't actually run:
```

False positive: the coalescing guard's subpass divisor `physical_shards_per_pass = max_shards_for_emem(n_heads, ., shard_tokens)` is the exact quantity the worker splits subcommands by (`max_shards_per_hw_cmd` = the same function, with the hdim arg ignored, and the first shard always the full 1024 tokens) -- call it `S`. Equal `query_physical_subpasses = P` therefore pins every coalesced Q to one covered-shards band `(P-1)*S < covered <= P*S`. The worker builds exactly `P` subcommands with base shards at `0, S, ..., (P-1)*S`, and every Q in that band has `covered > (P-1)*S`, so it reaches the last (and every) subcommand's base -- `tok_ix >= subcmd_base_tok` always holds and `local_tok_ix` never underflows. author: Wado-posi

title: Add host CPU temperature / frequency / power telemetry to Perfetto traces
body:
## Summary
Adds host CPU telemetry (temperature, frequency, package power) to Tron Perfetto traces,
complementing the sibling story's kernel/OS events. Closes #3198. Two independent layers
(they toggle separately):

- **App-side `hw` sampler** (`src/pos/hwperf.cpp`) — a background thread polls `/sys` and
  emits `TRACE_COUNTER`s on a new `hw` track_event category: hwmon CPU temperature,
  cpufreq avg/max, and RAPL `energy_uj` → Watts. Works in the in-process `--trace FILE`
  backend (unlike ftrace). On by default; `TRON_HW_SAMPLER=0` opts out,
  `TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS` tunes the 100 ms interval,
  `TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS=1` adds per-sensor temperature detail.
- **Hardware ftrace** — `power/cpu_idle` + `power/cpu_frequency` added to the `--os-events`
  overlay (daemon backend only).

### Tracks emitted, per socket

| Track | Source | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `socket<N> package temp (C)` | hwmon `Tdie`/`Tctl`/`Package id N` | one per socket |
| `socket<N> core temp min/avg/max (C)` | the per-die/per-core sensors | aggregated |
| `<driver> socket<N> <label> (C)` | every individual sensor | only with `TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS=1` |
| `cpu avg/max freq (MHz, N of M app cores)` | cpufreq sysfs | bounded sample, see below |
| `<domain> power (W)` | RAPL `energy_uj` | needs the grant below |

**Temperatures are aggregated by default.** The raw sensor count is large and
vendor-dependent — a dual EPYC exposes 26 (`k10temp`, 13/socket), a dual Granite Rapids
~146 (`coretemp`, one per core) — so the default is package + min/avg/max per socket (4
tracks/socket), which still surfaces a single hot die in the max. Per-sensor detail is one
env var away. Individual sensors are named `<driver> socket<N> <label>`, so a multi-socket
box never produces anonymous tracks.

**Frequency is a bounded sample, and the track name says how bounded.** A cold
`scaling_cur_freq` read blocks: reading all 384 cpus of a dual EPYC measures ~7.9 s per
pass on `acpi-cpufreq` (warm reads no cheaper), so a full scan can't run at trace cadence.
The sample is taken over the configured **app (compute) cores** — the cores tron actually
pins compute to — so a loaded run can't read as idle; it falls back to online cpus when no
app core list is configured. This needed one new accessor,
`tron::hardware::system::app_get_cpus()`, exposing the configured app cpu list (a snapshot
that `app_pin_thread()` doesn't consume).

## Why the diff touches runtron.cpp / perf.cpp (hw-sampler lifecycle)
The hw sampler's enable/disable is consolidated into the single
`start_tracing()`/`end_tracing()` pair (`src/pos/perf.cpp`) instead of being wired
separately into `runtron.cpp`'s phase callbacks + teardown and the SIGUSR1 path — so every
trace path (whole-run, phased `--trace-gen`, pass-gated `--trace-passes`, rinzler SIGUSR1)
enables the sampler at session start and disables it before the flush by construction. The
sampler thread starts once at `pos_startup()` and joins at `pos_shutdown()`; it parks on a
condition variable until a trace begins, so a process that never traces pays only a
sleeping thread (no periodic wakeups), and the first sample lands immediately on enable
rather than up to an interval later.

`disable_hw_sampling()` is a **real quiesce**, not a flag store: the sampler holds a mutex
across each tick body, so once `disable` acquires it no tick is emitting and none can
start. That is what lets `end_tracing()` flush a settled session. It costs at most one tick
body of blocking, on the trace-teardown path only.

⚠️ **One behavior change, now fixed.** An earlier revision of this PR moved
`disable_malloc_tracing()` in `runtron.cpp` such that the phased path no longer disabled it
after `join()` — so a phased run that ended before phase 3 left malloc tracing on for the
rest of the process and inflated `detected_mallocs()`. Caught in review; the post-join
disable is restored. Malloc tracing otherwise keeps its existing deliberate placement
(enabled after model load, so one-time load allocations stay out of the counter).

**Pre-existing hang, deliberately not fixed here:** on the phased path nothing counts
`tracing_end_latch` down when phase 3 never fires (`TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN` above the tokens
actually produced, or an early stop), so `tracing_manager->join()` hangs. Only the *start*
latch has that fallback. Not introduced by this PR; tracked as STORY-689, and the comment
in `runtron.cpp` now says so instead of implying the case is covered.

## ⚠️ Security tradeoff — RAPL power loosens a CVE mitigation
`energy_uj` being root-only **is** the CVE-2020-8694 (PLATYPUS) power side-channel
mitigation. tron runs non-root, so `perfetto/grant-rapl-read` (invoked by `tronperf` /
`wrapper`) runs `sudo -n chmod a+r` on `…/intel-rapl:*/energy_uj`. **`a+r` re-exposes the
side channel to all local users until reboot.**

`a+r` is a deliberate choice rather than a mirror of the tracefs `chown -R $USER` alongside
it, and the asymmetry is the point: tracefs can afford exclusivity because ftrace is
single-owner anyway, so only one capture runs at a time regardless. RAPL is a read-only
counter with unlimited concurrent readers, wanted by plain `runtron --trace FILE` runs as
much as by daemon captures, and the grant outlives the run that made it (plain `runtron`
never calls the script — it inherits whatever state is there). `chown` would leave it
mode-400 owned by one user, so the next developer's capture silently strips power tracks
from a colleague's in-flight run. `README.perfetto.md` now documents this explicitly, with
`chgrp` to a shared group as the narrowing option for a multi-tenant host, and no longer
presents `chown` as the safe default.

Two hardening fixes from review: the grant is now a **no-op under `TRON_HW_SAMPLER=0`** (a
kernel-events-only capture never touches the mitigation), and it uses **`sudo -n`** so a
headless runner (`--detach`, LSF) warns and continues instead of appearing to succeed or
hanging on a prompt. When zones are present but unreadable the sampler logs that once,
naming the grant script, rather than dropping power silently.

## Testing
`t_hwperf` (host, `pos_fake`): **22 cases / 122 assertions**, all passing.

The layouts that decide whether counter names are correct and unique are covered against
**synthetic sysfs trees** (`TRON_HW_SAMPLER_SYSFS_ROOT`, and a root parameter on the
readers), because no single host exhibits them and several appear on no CI host at all:
sparse sensor indices, missing labels, non-sensor filenames, multi-socket ordinals, two
CPU-temp drivers loaded at once, package-label priority, RAPL name collisions, RAPL zones
present-but-unreadable, cpufreq bounding, and the app-core vs online-cpu selection. Plus a
sampler **lifecycle** case (park → enable → tick → disable → re-enable → teardown,
idempotent) and a **quiesce** case that sweeps `disable()` across the tick phase.

Three fixes were **mutation-tested** — the bug reintroduced, the suite confirmed red, the
fix restored:

| Reintroduced bug | Result |
|---|---|
| temp track named by device basename instead of driver + socket | 2 cases fail |
| `disable_hw_sampling()` as a bare flag store (no quiesce barrier) | fails 3/3 runs |
| frequency sample strided over all cpus instead of app cores | 2 assertions fail |

The quiesce case needed the phase sweep to have teeth: written the obvious way — wait for a
tick, then disable — it passes even with the barrier removed, because `disable` then always
lands in the interval sleep.

### Still outstanding (needs real hardware — not run)
- **`config/test-benchmarks.json` entries recorded for 2 of the 4 platform keys**:
  `granite_rapids_6962p` (delphi-3af6, 1.76/1.65/1.65 s, 10 MB) and `genoa32`
  (andoria-11, 1.34/1.36/1.35 s, 9 MB). `genoa96` and `granite_rapids_6960p` are still
  unbenched for `t_hwperf`, because the hosts that report those keys are currently
  unusable — andoria-cf8c fails its Dice health check (EACCES on
  `/opt/positron/bin/dice`, reported separately) and delphi-17bb is `closed_Adm`.
  Partial coverage is the norm for this file: 32-49 other tests are missing per key.
- ~~Re-validate the capture rows on both vendors.~~ **Done** — see "Capture validation" below.
- **Unresolved Intel claim:** that `coretemp` caches each sensor's MSR read for ~1 s. Attempted
  from a 20 ms Intel capture: 41 samples over a 1.1 s window, 1 value change — which cannot
  separate 1 Hz caching from coretemp's 1 °C quantisation. The in-process backend can't settle
  it (see the 5 s window note below); needs a daemon capture. Impact is cosmetic — 8 tracks
  either way, and repeated counter samples render as a flat line.

## Usage
```
# whole-run, in-process file backend (hw counters, no daemon):
gen/runtron --trace out.trace -m <model> ...
# full app + kernel + hw timeline (daemon backend):
perfetto/tronperf --os-events --output-file out.trace -m <model> ...
# rinzler serving (SIGUSR1 timed capture):
perfetto/wrapper --os-events -n rinzler -c rinzler
# per-die temperature detail:
TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS=1 gen/runtron --trace out.trace -m <model> ...
```
Disable the sampler with `TRON_HW_SAMPLER=0`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Capture validation (2026-07-31, both vendors)

Three in-process captures through `bin/runtron --remote` (exclusive whole-box leases), analysed
with PerfettoSQL. Both vendors pass every structural check.

**Intel — delphi-3af6 (Xeon 6962P):** 8 aggregate temp tracks exactly (`avg` fractional over 72
cores, min/max integral at 1 °C); **146** per-sensor tracks under `TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS=1`
(73/socket, all `coretemp socket<N> <label>`), with the aggregates still present so detail is
additive; **0** per-sensor leakage in the default run; **0** PCI-named tracks;
`cpu avg/max freq (MHz, 8 of 112 app cores)` — "app cores", and 112 matches the app cpu list
counted independently from runtron's log; RAPL `package-0`, `package-1`,
`dram (intel-rapl:0:0)`, `dram (intel-rapl:1:0)` with the `dram` collision qualified, 187–297 W
per package and **0** negative samples; 14 tracks / 14 unique names; sampler cadence mean
**107.9 ms** against the 100 ms interval.

that box has 8 CCDs per socket), named `k10temp socket0 Tccd1 (C)` etc. — **this is the item-4

author: mcherba

title: Add pass-windowed generation tracing to runtron
body:
## Summary

`--trace-passes SPEC` records only the named primary forward passes — trace
size is bounded by window width, not run length. `0` also captures startup
(init + model load).

    bin/runtron -m llama-3-8b -l 32 \
      --trace-gen story662.pftrace --trace-passes 0,5-8 -- "prompt"

Result: inference unchanged; the trace shows model load, a silent gap
(passes 1–4 gated), then exactly 4 `forward` slices with full detail, all
slices paired. Sample: `/scratch/bcraig/story662-traces/`.

## What

- New runtron option `--trace-passes SPEC` guiding Perfetto instrumentation
  (requires `--trace-gen` — a file path for in-process capture, or `traced`
  to record through the external daemon): application track events are
  captured only during the selected
  primary forward passes. SPEC is 1-based ranges (`2-4`, `500-`, `-150`,
  `10,60,100-110`); `0` selects **startup** — everything before the first
  forward pass (init, device bring-up, model load). Prompt parse is pass 1,
  not startup. Takes precedence over `--trace` when both are given.
- Emission-side gate: the TrackEvent macros in `h/common/perfetto.hpp` AND in
  a process-global atomic (storage isolated in `src/pos/trace_gate.cpp`,
  coupled to allocator tracing). The scheduler opens/closes the gate at the
  `full_scheduler::forward()` boundary via a per-scheduler pass counter
  (`h/common/trace_passes.hpp`); speculators/EAGLE children are excluded and
  no-work forwards do not count.
- Windowed runs use a duration-free in-process session — legacy `--trace` /
  `--trace-gen` keep their 5 s cap — with an exception-safe start/action/stop
  lifecycle on a core-0-pinned thread (`h/runtron/trace_lifecycle.hpp`).
  `--trace-passes` overrides `TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN` (warns). Composes with
  `--trace-gen traced` daemon mode: the gate is emission-side and
  backend-agnostic.
- Response-slice pairing: the pre-forward "Generate response" BEGIN records
  iff the gate is open at that moment; the END restores the state captured at
  BEGIN, so the pair records or drops together — including repeated
  generations (`--isolated-iterations`), where the second run starts with the
  gate closed by the first run's teardown.
- Tests: `t_trace_passes` (unit — spec parser incl. the `0` grammar, pass
  counter, gate semantics, lifecycle, surrogate scheduler),
  `t_trace_passes_host` (integration on llama-3-8b-host — real forwards,
  in-process capture, pairing incl. the repeated-generation regression), CLI
  validation cases in `t_runtron_cli`; shared trace-inspection helpers in
  `t/trace_test_util.hpp`.

## Why

Legacy tracing is all-or-nothing: `--trace`/`--trace-gen` capture every pass
and stop at a hardwired 5 s, so long-run traces are either truncated or
unusably large, and there is no way to inspect a specific region deep in a
long generation. Pass windowing bounds capture by window width instead of run
length — measured on andoria-02: a 3-pass window of a 30-pass run is 927 KB
vs 9.1 MB legacy; an 11-pass window at pass ~7900 of an 8000-pass run is
6.5 MB. The `0` (startup) selector additionally captures init/model load,
which no legacy file mode records.

STORY-662 (Flow): https://www.notion.so/3a4d132d3cfd81599e7feb3fd9b98344

## Test plan

- `make test-host REMOTE=1` green via Distributed Dice (all host tests,
  including the three new binaries).
- The repeated-generation pairing fix (`eebdd5cad`) was verified red/green:
  with the fix stashed, the extended "keeps actual trace slices paired" case
  fails on the orphan response END; with the fix restored it passes. The
  regression test ships in this PR (`t/t_trace_passes_host.cpp`).
- Hardware validation on andoria-02 (llama-3-8b via Distributed Dice; all
  specs below with `--trace-gen FILE`). Analyzed with trace_processor SQL
  and a packet-level BEGIN/END walker:
  - `--trace-passes 2-4` (`-l 32`): exactly 3 `forward` slices, 0 unfinished;
    walker control: begins == ends exactly, response slice correctly absent.
  - `--trace-passes 0,5-8` (`-l 32`): 4 forwards; ~405 K loading-category
    events land before the first forward; passes 1–4 emit nothing (clean
    gated gap); response slice present and paired.
  - `--trace-passes 7900-7910` (`-l 8000 --dont-stop`): exactly 11 forwards,
    0 unfinished — the entire trace is the window, deep in an ~8000-pass run.
  - `--trace-passes 0,2-4 --isolated-iterations 2` (`-l 32`): pre-fix repro
    of the repeated-generation defect — walker measured the predicted orphan
    response END (ends = begins + 1); the `eebdd5cad` fix targets exactly
    this scenario.
  - `--trace-passes 5-` open-ended (`-l 32`): 28 complete forwards
    (passes 5 to end) plus one final forward truncated by session stop —
    the same stop-mid-slice signature the legacy baseline shows; a
    capture-boundary artifact of open-ended windows, not a pairing defect.
  - `--trace-passes 2-3` with both `--trace` and `--trace-gen` present:
    exactly 2 forwards — passes-windowed capture wins the precedence.
  - `--trace-passes 50-55` (`-l 128 --dont-stop`): exactly 6 forwards,
    0 unfinished.
  - `--trace-passes 120-` (`-l 128 --dont-stop`): 9 complete forwards
    (passes 120 to end) plus the same open-ended stop artifact.
  - `--trace-passes 10,60,100-110` (`-l 128 --dont-stop`): exactly
    13 forwards in three distinct clusters (disjoint multi-window works),
    0 unfinished.
  - Legacy `--trace-gen` baseline (`-l 32`): 30 forwards, whole run —
    9.1 MB vs 927 KB for the 3-pass window of the same workload.
- Sample capture for reviewers: `/scratch/bcraig/story662-traces/` holds the
  startup-spec trace (`0,5-8`) with a README of what to look for — drop it
  into ui.perfetto.dev or trace_processor to see the startup span, the gated
  gap, and the 4-pass window.
- `make format` and `make lint` clean at HEAD.
- Slice bench entries captured for the three new test binaries on `genoa32`
  and `granite_rapids_6962p` (one class per vendor); on the other two
  platform keys the tests use slice's unbenched fallback until someone
  backfills with a forced-class bench run.

## Risk & rollback

Tracing subsystem only; inference behavior is unchanged — the gate is
emission-side, defaults open, and legacy modes bypass windowing entirely
(pinned by a unit test; golden-logit tests untouched). Cleanly revertible: no
flags, migrations, or config to unwind.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches global Perfetto macro overrides and scheduler tracing lifecycle; inference is emission-only with gate default-open, but Perfetto SDK bumps need macro re-validation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`--trace-passes SPEC`** (with **`--trace-gen`**) so Perfetto application track events are recorded only during chosen **primary forward passes** and optional **startup** (`0` = init/model load before pass 1). Pass specs use 1-based ranges (`2-4`, `500-`, `0,5-8`, etc.); windowed in-process traces drop the legacy **5s duration cap** and run until generation ends.
> 
> **Emission gating:** `h/common/perfetto.hpp` wraps TrackEvent macros with `application_track_events_enabled()`; the scheduler toggles the gate at `select_trace_pass()` / `complete_trace_pass()` around `full_scheduler::forward()` via `trace_pass_counter`. Speculators are excluded. **`stream_generate`** preserves BEGIN/END pairing for the "Generate response" slice across repeated generations.
> 
> **runtron** takes a dedicated windowed path (`runtron_trace_lifecycle`, `start_tracing(..., legacy_local_duration=false)`). **`--trace-passes`** wins over **`--trace`** and overrides **`TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN`** (warns). Docs/`tronperf` help and tests (`t_trace_passes`, `t_trace_passes_host`, CLI cases) added; benchmark entries for new tests on two platforms.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1c41d959efe72d826818607908f0b60b21730216. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

This all looked good to me when I went through it Bret. I did ask claude to do a review as well. Below are the items it came up with. I do think there's some merit to a few of them, but could be a follow-up if you prefer. I'll approve as-is.

>   1. Perfetto internal-macro override is fragile against silent version drift (highest-value issue).
>   h/common/perfetto.hpp #undefs and re-defines PERFETTO_INTERNAL_TRACK_EVENT_WITH_METHOD and
>   PERFETTO_INTERNAL_CATEGORY_ENABLED, copying Perfetto's implementation (including the GCC 7 workaround). The >   #ifndef … #error guards only fire if the macro is renamed or removed — they will not catch a Perfetto bump that changes the macro body while keeping the name. In that case the override silently diverges from upstream (e.g., a new fast-path or arg the copy doesn't replicate) with no compile error.
>   - Suggestion: pin the reviewed Perfetto version/commit in the comment ("re-diff these overrides at vX.Y") and, if
>   feasible, add a runtime test asserting the gate actually suppresses a real emitted slice under the current Perfetto
>   (the t_trace_passes gate-filter test partially does this — good — but tie it explicitly to the override contract).
> 
>   2. The gate only covers emission sites that include common/perfetto.hpp. Any translation unit that emits track events
>   via a direct Perfetto include would bypass the gate and leak events into a windowed trace. Worth a one-line note in
>   the header (and/or a lint/grep guard) that all track-event emission must route through this header.
> 
>   3. Process-global mutable state + relaxed atomics — document the single-writer assumption.
>   detail::configured_trace_passes (inline optional in a header) and the application_track_events_gate atomic are
>   process-global and unsynchronized aside from the gate's relaxed loads/stores. This is fine for runtron's single
>   generation-pipeline model, and relaxed is acceptable for best-effort tracing — but it does mean events racing a gate
>   flip on other threads land in/out non-deterministically, and it assumes exactly one generation pipeline
>   configures/flips at a time. A short comment stating that invariant would help the next reader who tries to reuse this
>   outside runtron.
> 
>   4. UX gotcha with repeated generations. As documented, pass numbering restarts per scheduler, so --isolated-iterations
>   3 --trace-passes 5-8 produces three windows, not one, while startup (0) fires only once. It's in the README, but it's
>   an easy surprise — consider surfacing it in the --trace-passes help text too (currently the CLI help doesn't mention
>   the per-generation restart).
>

The writeup/description claims "New **Perfetto** option --trace-passes SPEC..." but it's really a new **Runtron** option to guide Perfetto instrumentation behavior right? Just a nit... looks like it works well though.

The majority of runtron developers (if not all) use the perfetto/tronperf script to launch Perfetto against runtron. So that script needs an update to take this new parameter, and forward it to runtron (like it does other options today)

author: mcherba

title: RX-stall, NaN, memory-bloat fixes
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the RX-stall/NaN and memory-bloat issues that prevented us from reaching 
long-context / multi-user runs on GPT-OSS-120b. Also fixes independent HW-attention correctness, 
The combined changes allow four concurrent 128K contexts to complete prefill and decode without 
RXSTALL, command-ring corruption, metadata assertions, or hugepage OOM.

## Key changes

- Fix GOF dispatch across ancestor and sibling tree edges. A token save now credits every matching GAL target, and positional HW residency is derived from the contiguous completed-GOF prefix rather than a non-positional count.
- Defer GOF K/V staging allocation until DMA submission, avoiding long-lived staging buffers for inactive work while preserving the existing release/reacquire lifecycle.
- Keep prepared ACMD and metadata DMA sources valid for the full 512-request  preparation window. Metadata ownership now extends through RX completion, including correct device-aperture addressing across logical rollover. Included extending the ACMD buffer to 4096 in size, and the Metadata ring buffer to 65536.
- Preserve prepare-ahead WCMD MMIO performance without overflowing the 1,024-word hardware FIFO. Requests retain stable WCMD copies in `rxinfo`; prepare posts only within a 960-word window, launch publishes deferred commands in order, and RX returns word credits. A five-second launch timeout captures diagnostics instead of waiting forever if capacity stops advancing.
- Allocate raw HW result buffers before attention workers launch, closing a container-growth race.
- Enable model-selected HW attention by default and lower early launch to four-user aggregate batches.

## Validation

- `make format`, `make lint`, and `make build-test`
- Focused worker, GOF, scheduler, DMA tracker, and launch-threshold tests
- `t_gof_dma`: 4,871 assertions passed
- `t_hwattention_batch`: 227 assertions passed, including metadata rollover
- Four-user 128K run with prompt chunk limit 128: all four requests completed at 107.142 prefill tok/s/user and 22.165 decode tok/s/user (45.115 ms/tok), peaking at 340 KV books / 37.35 GB
- No RXSTALL, OOM, ACMD theft, or metadata assertion. The run observed one recoverable late `rxinfo overflow` and completed normally.

## Known FPGA constraints

- The AMEM query-group cap is a temporary host workaround until [llm_fpga#340](https://github.com/positron-ai/llm_fpga/issues/340) is fixed in deployed bitfiles.
- Compound HW-attention passes remain disabled because the current FPGA can strand the final one or two result words for those requests.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core FPGA command lifecycle, GOF DMA residency, and HW attention scheduling on security- and correctness-critical inference paths; mistakes could corrupt rings, read uninitialized KV, or stall RX under load.
> 
> **Overview**
> Targets **long-context, multi-user GPT-OSS-style runs** that were hitting RX stalls, NaNs, ring corruption, and hugepage pressure.
> 
> **GOF / scheduler:** `gof_job` now holds **multiple targets** per query so K/V saves credit every matching GAL on ancestor/sibling edges; cooperative `gof_rodeo` carries `(job_ix, target_ix, layer)`. HW KV residency for shard push and attention planning uses **`count_complete_prefix_gofs()`** instead of a total count, so holes in out-of-order DMA cannot expose unread HBM. GOFs use **`deferred_staging`** so K/V buffers allocate at `prepare_for_dma()`; GAL creation is keyed by GOF-ending position with mates wired across split edges.
> 
> **POS worker / device:** Host **ACMD** and **metadata** shadow rings grow to cover the full 512-request prepare-ahead window; metadata ownership lasts until **RX** completion, with segmented DMA across device metadata aperture rollover. **WCMDs** are copied into `rxinfo`, published under `wcmd_post_mutex` with a **960-word** prepare window and word-level `wcmd_words_in_flight` credits returned on RX; launch posts deferred WCMDs in order. **Compound HW-attn split** is forced off; **`max_qs_for_emem`** gains a temporary **AMEM** cap (llm_fpga#340).
> 
> **Executor:** Raw HW result buffers are allocated during **plan assembly**; default **early HW launch** threshold drops to **4** users; model-selected HW attention default follows env unless `USE_HW_ATTN` overrides.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fa2798442b8cd00ea8376f2fb8b8f0e80bc93e3c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

wade.body: this is a fallback strategy only... `prepare` will still write all the commands it can, but if it bumps up against the limit, it will 'defer' those to be done in the `launch` path (here) instead

I wish ;-p. And we could revisit this for sure. I was focused on robustness with these changes above all. This is a 'non blocking' mutex (**try_lock**)... it's an opportunistic attempt to write the wcmds in the `prepare` path (which is the majority scenario), but we don't want to actually _wait_ on the tx_launch. And most importantly we don't want to _reorder_ the wcmds between the prepare and launch threads interleaving. The comments above (and surrounding) attempt to explain how it works.

One primary 'miss' (bug) we had before is that each request `prepare` generates could contain up to **8** actual commands. 512 request * 8 commands = 4096 for ACMD ring buffers now. It's definitely 'worst case' but is also safe.

author: mcherba

title: Rebuild GOF page captures when a KV book relocates
body:
### Symptom

SIGSEGV after ~210 of 1204 MMLU-Pro questions. The signal handler catches SIGSEGV, logs a
backtrace, then aborts, so the core is recorded as SIGABRT.

Reproduced three times with a byte-identical stack (same binary file offsets each time), at 212,
207, and ~210 questions. Deterministic, not a flaky race.

### Stack

Resolved from the core with `addr2line -f -C -e gen/rinzler <offset>`:

| Frame | Offset | Symbol |
|-------|--------|--------|
| #5 | `0x20036ec` | `tron::hardware::gof::populate` — `src/tron/gof.cpp:155` |
| #6 | `0x1ea8712` | `std::__atomic_base<unsigned>::fetch_add` (shared_ptr refcount, inlined) |
| #7 | `0x2003dac` | `std::__shared_ptr<tron::hardware::shard>::get()` |

The caller frames put this on the **shard eviction/reacquire path**, which is exactly what
`populate`'s own comment predicts (`src/tron/gof.cpp:132-135`): it fires on first populate and
again after each eviction/reacquire.

### Root cause — confirmed by instrumentation

Proven on 2026-08-10 at HEAD `63e203c6c1f` with temporary diagnostics (`GOF_UAF`,
`RELOC_GALS`, `GOF_STALE_OFFSET`; all marked `TODO(crash-chase)`). The causal chain, with
matching book addresses from one run:

```
17:39:57.726  RELOC_GALS: edge at abs_ht 1471 repointing book 0x7f0d86e9d600
              -> 0x7f0da5002040 (shift 14) while holding 364 gals
              whose page captures are not updated
17:39:58.671  GOF_UAF: page_info[0] (token 1468) owner book 0x7f0d86e9d600
              freed before populate, layer 0
17:39:58.671  signal handled: Segmentation fault (11)
```

1. `defrag()` merges a child book into its parent and drops the last reference to the child
   (`full.hpp:1161` — "this defrag frees my_book").
2. `_relocate()` repoints the edge to the new book and invalidates the edge's append cache,
   but leaves `parent_edge.gals` holding page pointers into the **old** book.
3. The old book is freed.
4. The next `gof::populate()` on one of those gals invokes `k_head_fn`, dereferencing freed
   memory. SIGSEGV.

A gal's page_info captures a bare page pointer plus an offset into the book that owns the page. Defragmentation can splice that book into its parent and drop the old owner, leaving the capture dangling and causing gof::populate() to dereference freed memory.\n\nRebuild affected captures through the same factory used at construction. Walk the entire anchored subtree because a gal can straddle an edge boundary and reference an ancestor book from a descendant that owns a different book. Also document shard HBM ownership and release behavior.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Fixes a use-after-free in KV-book defrag and changes when wcls weight commands are posted to the device—both are correctness-critical paths that can crash or corrupt hardware state if wrong.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes a deterministic UAF/SIGSEGV** when `defrag()` splices a child KV book into its parent: gal `page_info` captures kept bare `page*` pointers into the freed book, so later `gof::populate()` crashed.
> 
> After `_relocate`, the subtree now rebuilds affected captures via the same `make_page_info` factory used at construction. Repair walks the whole anchored subtree (not just edges still on the old book) because a gal can straddle an edge and reference an ancestor book from a descendant that owns a different book. Each `page_info` also records a weak `owner_book` so only captures for the moved book are rewritten.
> 
> **Separately**, wcls preparation now calls `defer_weight_commands_until_launch()` so its WCMD stays staged until `tx_launch` instead of posting during prepare while final-layer expert matmuls may still be active (which could corrupt the first W-Mem ping/pong block). Other matmuls keep prepare-time weight prefetch. Adds FPGA tests covering deferred staging and concurrent expert+wcls launch.
> 
> Also documents shard HBM ownership and release lifetime.

author: Wado-posi

title: Add Perfetto memory allocator tracing
body:
Add a debug-only Perfetto `memory` category for selective DMA and HBM allocator tracing without flooding steady-state allocation paths.

## Problem

Allocator pressure, HBM activity, heap expansion, reserve draining, large-slab acquisition, and OOMs were difficult to identify in existing Perfetto traces. Tracing every DMA allocation would produce excessive event volume.

## Solution

Register the debug-tagged `memory` category and add these selective allocator events:

- `hardware::allocator::allocate` — requested HBM allocation size
- `hardware::allocator::deallocate` — released HBM address
- `hardware::allocator::dump_profile` — profile tag; available with `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW`
- `pos_heap_v2::expand` — number of DMA hugepages added
- `pos_heap_v2::drain_reserves` — number of cached slabs released
- `pos_heap_v2::oom` — requested size, size class, and caller addresses
- `slab_pool_t::acquire_large` — LARGE allocation size class
- `slab_pool_t::release_small_hugepage` — complete SMALL hugepage reclamation

Routine LARGE pre-drains and steady-state DMA allocation/deallocation remain untraced to avoid event flooding. Wildcard-only trace configurations do not enable this category; it must be explicitly enabled with `memory`. Structured trace assertions cover the event payloads, and the `t_hwalloc` Slice benchmark metadata is refreshed.

## Testing

- Default `build-test`, `t_heap_v2`, `t_hwalloc`, and `[perfetto]` passed; HBM-shadow `[perfetto]` and `[shadow]` passed
- `make lint`, `git diff --check`, and touched-file `clang-format-19 --dry-run -Werror`
- Dice `bin/slice bench --remote --remote-sku sku0 --update t_hwalloc` passed and refreshed the `genoa96` metadata
- DUT captures validated the expected memory events and annotations alongside model loading and generation activity

Enabling the `memory` category had negligible performance impact. We compared three runs with the category enabled against three otherwise identical runs with it disabled. Each used llama-3.1-8b with hardware attention enabled (8K-token input, 64K-token output). Enabled traces contained 10,131 memory events; disabled traces contained none, and all traces had zero loss indicators.

| Median metric | Disabled | `memory` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Model loading | 1.465630 s | 1.467667 s | +0.14% |
| Generation time | 573.704928 s | 574.418353 s | +0.12% |
| Generation throughput | 114.228 tok/s | 114.086 tok/s | -0.12% |
| TTLT | 577.146341 s | 577.840951 s | +0.12% |

No material performance regression was measurable; all median changes were below 0.2%.
